AD.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted), as required by the EU country of arrival. Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
AD.rabies_titer: Under the EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
AD.parasite_treatment: None required under EU rules (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.
AD.quarantine: None if EU requirements are met.
AD.timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
AD.private_aviation: No airport in Andorra; private jets land in Spain (e.g. Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell, Barcelona) or France (e.g. Toulouse); EU entry rules and points of entry of that country apply for third-country arrivals.
AD.export: Leaving: the EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport or certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement).
AD.authority: Government of Andorra – Ministry of Agriculture (veterinary service); at entry, the Spanish or French authorities

AE.microchip: Mandatory permanent microchip; the chip number on the health certificate must match the implanted chip.
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination given according to the manufacturer's instructions. The first dose may not be given before 12 weeks of age. A first or lapsed vaccination needs 21 days before the titre blood draw. No 21-day wait if the booster is continuous. USDA additionally says at least 21 days before travel.
Dogs: canine distemper (CDV), canine parvovirus, infectious canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (leptospirosis may be replaced by a lab test if the exporting country does not vaccinate).
Cats: feline panleukopenia, feline rhinotracheitis, feline calicivirus.
Vaccination record or passport must show microchip number, species, colour, sex, date of birth, vaccine name, manufacturer, batch number and date.
AE.rabies_titer: High-risk origins only (any country not on MOCCAE's low-risk list): FAVN/RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/ml from a lab approved by the exporting country's authority. The sample must be at least 21 days after a first or lapsed rabies vaccination, or any time if the booster is continuous. The result is valid 365 days if the vaccination stays continuous and no booster is given; otherwise retest. Official MOCCAE low-risk list: Australia, Austria, Andorra, Bahrain, Barbados, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Fiji, Finland, French Polynesia, Falkland Islands, Hong Kong, Iceland, Ireland, Jamaica, Japan, Kuwait, Liechtenstein, Mauritius, Malta, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Portugal, Singapore, San Marino, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, Vanuatu, Netherlands, Bulgaria, Slovenia, Palau, Latvia, Albania, Croatia, Maldives, Spain (excluding Melilla and Ceuta), Cyprus, Korea, Montenegro, Seychelles, Suriname, Micronesia, Greece, Marshall Islands, Bahamas, Lithuania, Macedonia. Germany and Italy are not on MOCCAE's list; confirm with MOCCAE before travel. USDA states a titre is required for US-origin pets, with the sample no more than 12 months before travel.
AE.parasite_treatment: Preventive treatment for internal and external parasites within 14 days before shipment, recorded on the health certificate or passport. USDA suggests fipronil or permethrin for external parasites and praziquantel for internal parasites.
documents: MOCCAE import permit (valid 90 days from issue; entry with an expired permit is refused)

Official health certificate issued or endorsed by the exporting country's competent veterinary authority (USDA: valid 10 days after issuance; US certificates need original ink USDA signature and embossing)
Vaccination record or passport with microchip number
Rabies titre lab certificate (high-risk origins only; can be recorded on the health certificate)
For release at port: customs declaration or bill of lading showing delivery data
If transiting other countries: proof or attestation that the pet did not mix with other animals in transit
Bengal and Serval cats: fifth-generation pedigree certificate
Service, emotional-support or medical dogs: training certificate, owner medical report, and a non-transfer pledge (5 working days to process)
AE.import_permit: Required. Apply online through MOCCAE digital services before travel. Issued in about 1 working day (5 working days for service, emotional-support or medical dogs). Valid 90 days per MOCCAE; USDA APHIS states 30 days, so use the permit within 30 days of issue. Fees: AED 200 per head for the import permit, plus a release permit of AED 500 per dog or AED 250 per cat. Limit: maximum 2 companion animals per person per year (2 cats, 2 dogs, or 1 of each). Returning resident pets are exempt from the limit.
AE.quarantine: No routine quarantine for compliant pets. Inspection, and lab testing if required, happens on arrival at the MOCCAE port quarantine centre. Non-compliant pets are rejected (re-exported at the owner's expense) or confiscated.
AE.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or the EU: for high-risk origins (including the USA, France, Germany and Italy) a titre test on a continuously vaccinated pet has no waiting period after the blood draw, so allow for lab turnaround (2–4 weeks), then the MOCCAE import permit and an official health certificate within 10 days of travel. From MOCCAE low-risk origins (e.g. UK, Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Switzerland) no titre is needed. From scratch, plan at least 2 months (low-risk origins) or 3–4 months (high-risk origins needing a first titre): microchip → rabies and core vaccines (first rabies dose at 12 weeks or older) → titre test, if high-risk, at least 21 days after a first rabies dose → MOCCAE import permit → parasite treatment within 14 days of travel → official health certificate (USDA: within 10 days) → MOCCAE release permit and inspection on arrival.
AE.restricted_breeds: Banned (dogs, including mixes): Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Tibetan Mastiff, Neapolitan Mastiff, Dogue de Bordeaux, Boerboel, Bullmastiff, Cane Corso, Bully Kutta (Alangu or Indian Mastiff), Perro de Presa Canario, Japanese Tosa. Exception for service, emotional-support or medical dogs under specific rules. Cats: Bengal and Serval need a fifth-generation pedigree. Minimum age at import: 12 weeks (low-risk origin) or 15 weeks (high-risk origin).
AE.private_aviation: MOCCAE says pets are shipped 'according to IATA conditions' and released at a MOCCAE quarantine centre. Release documents include a customs declaration or bill of lading. USDA states pets must travel to the UAE as manifested cargo. List the pet on the aircraft's cargo manifest or air waybill and pre-arrange MOCCAE inspection through the handling agent. Relevant MOCCAE centres: Al Maktoum Airport (DWC), Dubai Airport Cargo Village, Dubai Airport Free Zone, Zayed International Airport (Abu Dhabi), and Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah airports. Confirm with MOCCAE (800 3050, info@moccae.gov.ae) and the FBO before each flight. Transit: no permit is needed for airside transit at the same airport (the pet must be isolated). A MOCCAE transit permit is needed if the pet enters UAE territory.
AE.export: Leaving the UAE requires a MOCCAE veterinary health certificate for export or re-export of live animals, issued after a physical inspection at the export point (e.g. Dubai Airport Cargo Village or Al Maktoum Airport centre). Valid 30 days. Fee AED 100 for a personal consignment of 2 or fewer pets (AED 400 standard). About 1 working day. Not required: certificate of origin or a destination import permit copy for companion animals. Bring the passport or vaccination booklet and any tests the destination requires. Returning residents: pets must have a MOCCAE health certificate on departure and a rabies vaccination valid until return to re-enter under the resident rules.
AE.authority: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)

AG.microchip: Required; proof of microchipping goes with the license application.
vaccinations: Rabies: given within 1 year of importation.
AG.rabies_titer: Rabies FAVN result within accepted levels from an OIE/WOAH-approved lab, submitted with the license application. No waiting period is stated, so confirm with VLD.
AG.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasites treated within 7 days of export with approved products, recorded on the certificate (products and dates).
documents: Import license.
Medical history including Ehrlichia and Lyme test results (dogs); FIP, FeLV and FIV testing and vaccination history (cats).
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet within 7 days before arrival, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement).
AG.import_permit: Required. Only pets with a duly issued import license are accepted. Apply to the Veterinary & Livestock Division (vld@ab.gov.ag, fax 268-460-1759).
AG.quarantine: No standard quarantine is stated. Non-compliant pets may be refused or confiscated.
AG.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN (lab turnaround), then the license, then parasite treatment and the health certificate within 7 days of arrival, then APHIS endorsement.
AG.restricted_breeds: Pit bull-type dogs and mixes may not land. Look-alike dogs need certification from a recognized kennel club stating they are not pit bulls.
AG.authority: Veterinary & Livestock Division, Ministry of Agriculture, Antigua and Barbuda

AI.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip, verified by the vet.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine at least 30 days before departure and within its 12- or 36-month validity. Boosters of unexpired vaccines may be under 30 days if the previous vaccination is listed.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis (adenovirus), parvovirus, parainfluenza and leptospirosis.
Cats: rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia, pneumonitis and FeLV.
AI.parasite_treatment: Negative fecal flotation and internal parasite treatment within 21 days before departure. External parasite treatment within 14 days before departure; free of ticks (Amblyomma, Boophilus).
documents: Pet Import Permit Application (Cat & Dog), Government of Anguilla Department of Agriculture.
US Veterinary Health Certificate for Anguilla (ISO microchip number, age 13 weeks or older), APHIS-endorsed, valid 14 days after issuance.
AI.import_permit: Required. Apply through gov.ai (Pet Import/Export requirements page); a fee form is provided, but the amount isn't published.
AI.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies at least 30 days before departure, permit application, fecal test and deworming within 21 days, health certificate and tick treatment within 14 days, APHIS endorsement.
AI.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier type or other 'ferocious' dogs are prohibited and will be seized, unless the Chief Veterinary Officer is satisfied otherwise.
AI.export: Leaving Anguilla: a licensed local vet issues the health certificate, endorsed by the Government Veterinarian if the destination requires it.
AI.authority: Government of Anguilla – Department of Agriculture (Chief Veterinary Officer)

AL.microchip: Required: ISO microchip, or a legible tattoo applied before 3 July 2011, per the EU-model certificate used by Albania
vaccinations: Rabies: required. Must be current; per the EU model, given at ≥12 weeks of age, with ≥21 days after the primary vaccination before entry
Young unvaccinated pets: an owner declaration form exists (APHIS 'Pet Not Vaccinated Against Rabies'). Acceptance is not guaranteed; confirm in advance
AL.rabies_titer: Not required if the pet travels directly from, or transits only, Annex II-listed or EU countries (the US is covered). Otherwise required per the model certificate: ≥0.5 IU/ml, sample taken ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before travel. An owner declaration covers transit through unlisted countries
documents: Albania health certificate for dogs, cats and ferrets (non-commercial). For US origin: issued by a USDA-accredited vet and APHIS-endorsed within 10 days of travel
Owner declaration (non-commercial movement / transit through unlisted country, where applicable)
Rabies vaccination record
AL.timeline: Plan at least 1 month if coming from a listed country (4+ months if a titer is needed): microchip → rabies vaccine (wait 21 days) → [titer + 3 months if unlisted origin] → health certificate within 10 days of travel
AL.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of Albania / National Food Authority (AKU)

AM.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules; recommended
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within last 12 months (multi-year vaccine OK while valid)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
documents: International pet passport with clinical exam mark ≤14 days (≤2 pets), or EAEU Form 15 certificate (APHIS: issued and endorsed within 5 days of travel)
AM.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal pets (EAEU); APHIS states up to 5 without special permission
AM.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → exam/certificate within 5 days
AM.authority: Food Safety Inspection Body of Armenia (EAEU common veterinary requirements)

documents: ISV zoosanitary import licence (original), valid 60 days from issue per the USDA FAS report (general rule for animal import permits)
Veterinary health certificate from the country of origin. ISV accepts APHIS-issued health certificates (USDA FAS AO2023-0004). Exact pet certificate content is not published.
Proof of current rabies vaccination (APHIS general guidance for countries with unknown requirements)
AO.import_permit: Required. Per the USDA FAS FAIRS export-certificate report AO2023-0004 (29 Nov 2023), ISV (Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry) issues zoosanitary licences for importing pets under Animal Health Law 04/04 and Decree 70/08. For animals and animal products in general, the report says only ISV can issue the import permit, the original must accompany the shipment, it is valid 60 days from issue and covers a single shipment. ISV contact listed in the report: isvetangola@gmail.com.
AO.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: request the ISV zoosanitary licence and its written conditions (processing time unknown) → vet health certificate and government endorsement as ISV instructs → travel within the licence's 60-day validity.
AO.authority: Instituto dos Serviços de Veterinária (ISV), Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Angola

AR.microchip: Not required by SENASA for entry (no microchip requirement on SENASA entry page). If present, record on CVI.
vaccinations: Rabies: required, with a vaccine authorized in the origin country and still valid on the day of entry; a first (primary) vaccination must be given at least 21 days before entry.

Puppies/kittens under 3 months: may enter unvaccinated if the origin authority certifies age and no exposure to urban rabies in the prior 90 days. Animals from WOAH rabies-free countries/zones are exempt if stated on the CVI.
AR.parasite_treatment: Internal and external broad-spectrum antiparasitic treatment within 15 days before CVI issue (or passport endorsement), with products approved in the origin country; record product, active ingredient, date.
documents: Original CVI from the origin country's official veterinary authority (Spanish must be one of the languages), valid 60 calendar days from issue provided rabies vaccination remains valid
Clinical exam by a registered vet within 10 days before CVI issue (stated on the CVI)
Alternatively: a valid official pet passport endorsed by the origin's veterinary authority before shipment, containing the same health data (Spanish or English accepted)
AR.import_permit: Not required for pets accompanying their owner. Pets shipped as cargo (unaccompanied) require a prior SENASA border-intervention request at least 24 business hours in advance and pay the internment fee.
AR.quarantine: None routinely. Non-compliant animals may be retained or subjected to sanitary measures at the owner's cost.
AR.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: broad-spectrum parasite treatment within 15 days of the CVI, vet exam within 10 days of the CVI, official CVI/endorsement in the origin country, then SENASA document and identity check on arrival. From scratch, plan at least 4 weeks (a first rabies dose at least 21 days before entry).
AR.restricted_breeds: SENASA states no breed restrictions for dogs or cats.
AR.private_aviation: SENASA performs documentary, physical and identity checks at the point of entry; no cost for accompanied pets. Confirm SENASA availability at the arrival airport/FBO before booking.
AR.export: Leaving Argentina: SENASA issues the CVI based on destination requirements. Book a SENASA appointment online (up to 30 days ahead), bring private-vet health certificate and vaccination records (originals + copies). For Ezeiza, documents can be emailed up to 10 days before the flight. CVI validity 5/10/up to 60 days depending on destination; returning pets may re-enter Argentina within 60 days on the SENASA-issued CVI if rabies is valid.
AR.authority: SENASA (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad y Calidad Agroalimentaria)

vaccinations: Rabies: certificate from a salaried government vet (or other competent authority) that the pet was vaccinated no later than 30 days before arrival (A.S.A.C. 24.0307(d)).
AS.rabies_titer: Not specified in the territorial code. Pets from the US mainland must meet Hawaii's requirements (FAVN-based), since they must quarantine in Hawaii.
documents: Government-vet rabies vaccination certificate (vaccinated at least 30 days before arrival)
Proof of compliance with Department of Agriculture entry conditions (permit/conditions set by the Director; get them before travel)
US mainland/Guam origin: proof of the mandatory Hawaii quarantine
AS.import_permit: Entry is only under conditions set by the Director of Agriculture; get them in writing from the American Samoa Department of Agriculture before travel.
AS.quarantine: Hawaii, NZ or Australia origin: per DOA conditions. Continental US, Guam or Trust Territories origin: mandatory quarantine in Hawaii for a period set by the Department of Agriculture (A.S.A.C. 24.0317(2)).
AS.timeline: Get DOA conditions first. US mainland pets must first complete Hawaii's import programme and the required quarantine. Length is set by DOA and Hawaii rules, so no fixed lead time.
AS.private_aviation: A direct private flight from the US mainland or Europe with a pet is not allowed. US-mainland pets must quarantine in Hawaii first, and EU-origin pets are not an allowed origin. Pets arriving without full prior compliance are returned or destroyed.
AS.export: For export to New Zealand, MPI treats American Samoa as Category 2 (rabies-free); the crate needs a vet-applied seal on departure day (USDA).
AS.authority: American Samoa Department of Agriculture (Director of Agriculture)

AT.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
AT.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
AT.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Austria does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
AT.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
AT.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
AT.restricted_breeds: Several Länder (e.g. Vienna, Lower Austria, Vorarlberg) have listed-dog rules (licence, muzzle, leash) for residents; confirm with the destination Land before travel.
AT.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Austria and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airports on Austria's point-of-entry list published by the European Commission: Vienna, Linz, Klagenfurt, Salzburg, Graz and Innsbruck. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
AT.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
AT.authority: Federal Ministry of Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection (BMSGPK)

AU.microchip: Microchip required; identity is tied to the RNAT. For Group 3, a competent-authority (official government vet) identity check before the RNAT blood draw cuts quarantine from 30 to 10 days.
vaccinations: Rabies (Group 3): vaccination valid from the RNAT blood draw through export.
Other vaccines and tests per the import permit.
AU.rabies_titer: Group 3: RNAT by FAVN or RFFIT, at least 0.5 IU/ml. Export only 180 days or more after the lab receives the sample. The RNAT is valid 12 months from sampling; a retest plus a permit variation avoids restarting the 180 days.
AU.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatments as set out in the import permit and DAFF step-by-step guide.
documents: DAFF import permit (BICON)
RNAT declaration and lab report (Group 3)
Competent-authority identity check (optional, enables 10-day quarantine)
Government-endorsed veterinary health certificate
Dogs (per USDA summary for US origin): tests for Leishmania infantum, Brucella canis (unless desexed), Leptospira Canicola (unless vaccinated)
PEQ booking confirmation
AU.import_permit: Yes for Group 2 and 3, via BICON. Apply early: Group 3 pets cannot be booked into quarantine until the permit is issued.
AU.quarantine: Group 2: at least 10 days. Group 3: at least 10 days only if the competent-authority identity check was done before the RNAT blood draw and at least 180 days before export; otherwise at least 30 days. All quarantine is at the Mickleham PEQ facility (Melbourne). Book only after the permit is issued, via the Post Entry Biosecurity System or by phone (1800 900 090). The facility accepts arrivals 05:00-14:30 Mon, Tue, Sat, Sun and 05:00-21:00 Wed-Fri.
AU.timeline: Allow at least 210 days (about 7 months) for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or most EU countries (Group 3): official identity check, RNAT blood draw, then export no earlier than 180 days after the lab receives the sample; meanwhile apply for the DAFF import permit, book Mickleham quarantine once the permit is issued, complete pre-export tests, treatments and the certificate, then fly into Melbourne. Group 2 (rabies-free) countries need less time (weeks to a few months).
AU.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terrier/American Pit Bull Terrier, Perro de Presa Canario. Some cat hybrids (e.g. Savannah) are prohibited. Confirm with DAFF before travel.
AU.private_aviation: Allowed with conditions. Pets normally arrive as manifested cargo directly into Melbourne (no domestic transfers). For a private or chartered flight, DAFF must be told before departure: the permit must be varied (fees apply), and DAFF gives written approval after a document check before the flight leaves. Group 2/3 flights must land at a first point of entry airport in Victoria. The pet must be crated before the aircraft enters Australian territory and stay crated until it reaches PEQ. On mixed flights, Group 2 pets stay sealed the whole flight; Group 3 pets may be uncrated until Australian territory.
AU.export: Export certification is through DAFF (MICoR lists destination requirements; export health certificates are government-endorsed). Group 3 pets returning to Australia can use the identity check on their Australian export certification.
AU.authority: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF)

AW.microchip: AVID or ISO-compatible. With another chip type, the pet must travel with a scanner.
vaccinations: Rabies: pets over 3 months, at least 1 month before travel; the certificate lists vaccine name, lot and expiry. Under 3 months: exempt (stated on the certificate).
documents: Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet within 14 days of arrival, USDA-endorsed (digital via VEHCS), including NWS (screwworm) certification statements.
Prior approval from the Director of the Veterinary Service of Aruba (vetservice@dvg.aw, +297 585 0400).
Residence: in the US or Aruba continuously for 6 months before export (pets under 6 months: born in and always in the US), unless exempted in writing.
AW.import_permit: No separate permit is named, but the Veterinary Service of Aruba must approve the documents before shipment.
AW.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies at least 1 month before, health certificate within 14 days, APHIS endorsement, Aruba approval before departure.
AW.export: Return to the US: Aruba is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs need a screwworm certificate from an official vet. Aruba is not on the CDC high-risk list.
AW.authority: Veterinary Service of Aruba (Departamento di Salubridad Publico)

BA.microchip: Required: transponder, or a clearly legible tattoo applied before 3 July 2011
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet at ≥12 weeks of age, not before the microchip. For EU/EFTA pets, valid from 21 days after the primary vaccination; boosters must fall within the validity period
BA.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EFTA or listed third countries (Annex IV Part B). Required from non-listed countries: ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, sample taken ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before import/transit
documents: EU pet passport (EU/EFTA origin), OR
Veterinary health certificate from the official vet of the origin country (third countries), valid 10 days from issue to the entry check
BA.import_permit: Not needed for ≤5 pets; more than 5 pets requires the full import procedure (contact info@vet.gov.ba)
BA.timeline: Plan at least 1 month from EU/listed countries; 4+ months from non-listed countries (titer + 3-month wait). Health certificate within 10 days of arrival
BA.private_aviation: Must enter through a BiH-designated traveller entry point with veterinary checks. Confirm in advance that the arrival airport performs pet checks
BA.export: To the EU: health certificate (model KZV-EU-11a) issued via an official or authorised vet registered with the Veterinary Office of BiH. New EU certificate rules apply from 22 April 2026 (Regs (EU) 2026/131, 2026/705). Echinococcus treatment is needed if going to FI/IE/MT/NO (listed under Reg 1152/2011)
BA.authority: Office for Veterinary Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Kancelarija/Ured za veterinarstvo BiH)

BB.microchip: ISO 11784 / ISO 11785 Annex A microchip, implanted before or at the time of rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine, first dose at 3 months or older. Wait 35 days after a primary vaccination, or after revaccination following a lapse (vaccination day = day 0). Boosters on or before the expiry date.
BB.rabies_titer: Required only for pets in a Category 2 country within the 3 months before travel (Category 1 = rabies-free or low risk; the US is Category 1) and for all sea arrivals. Blood drawn at an approved lab at least 30 days after vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. Pets must have spent 3 continuous months in Category 1 countries to use the Category 1 route.
BB.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: ticks plus tapeworm (praziquantel) within 7 days before leaving. Heartworm test (dogs over 6 months) within 30 days, ELISA antigen; Knott's test if positive or previously treated. Cats: none.
documents: Barbados import permit (Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture), valid 6 months.
Official export health certificate: exam within 7 days of travel, endorsed by an official government vet (APHIS digital endorsement via VEHCS). Valid 10 days from endorsement.
Customs broker (required); airline 'Pre-Alert' listing the animals.
BB.import_permit: Required, obtained FIRST from Veterinary Services, Barbados. Valid 6 months from issue.
BB.timeline: Allow at least 21 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 35 days before travel) travelling from the USA (Category 1): import permit, heartworm test within 30 days, vet exam and dog treatments within 7 days, official endorsement, and 3 working days' notice of arrival. From scratch, plan at least 2 months: permit, microchip and rabies vaccination (35-day wait), then the steps above. From Category 2 countries (e.g. UAE), add the FAVN step.
BB.private_aviation: Give at least 3 working days' notice of arrival (246-427-5492 / 427-5073, vetservices@caribsurf.com) with the owner, customs broker and flight details. Animals go directly from the aircraft to the Animal Reception Centre; cabin pets are handed to handling agents, and customs treats pets as cargo. Government hours are Mon–Fri 8:15 am–4:30 pm; arrivals outside these hours, on weekends or on holidays incur overtime inspection fees.
BB.authority: Veterinary Services Department, Ministry of Agriculture, Food, Fisheries and Water Resource Management, Barbados

BE.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
BE.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
BE.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Belgium does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
BE.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
BE.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
BE.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the FASFC before travel.
BE.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Belgium and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Belgium's points of entry are published by the FASFC; confirm with the FASFC before travel that the arrival airport is on the list. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
BE.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
BE.authority: FASFC/AFSCA (Federal Agency for the Safety of the Food Chain) and FPS Public Health

BF.microchip: Required for dogs and cats (France Diplomatie, Sep 2026). The APHIS certificate identifies the animal by microchip number and/or name.
vaccinations: Rabies: animals must be vaccinated; certificate records vaccination date, vaccine name, batch number and end of validity (no minimum wait stated on the APHIS certificate).
BF.parasite_treatment: Not required on the APHIS certificate (optional section for other vaccinations/treatments/tests).
documents: APHIS bilingual health certificate for Burkina Faso, issued by a USDA-accredited vet (electronic signature via VEHCS accepted), valid 30 days after issuance
Clinical exam on date of issue: free of infectious/contagious disease incl. rabies; from an area not quarantined for rabies
USDA APHIS endorsement with original ink signature and embossed seal (can be returned by mail with prepaid label); original must travel with the animal
International vaccination booklet and individual pet passport (France Diplomatie)
BF.import_permit: Not mentioned by APHIS. Confirm with the Direction des Services Vétérinaires (Ouagadougou) before travel whether an import permit is needed.
BF.quarantine: None ('Il n'y a pas de quarantaine au Burkina Faso' — France Diplomatie); none mentioned by APHIS.
BF.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: confirm current rabies vaccination → vet exam and certificate within 30 days of arrival → APHIS ink endorsement (allow mailing time) → travel with original.
BF.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources animales et halieutiques — Direction des Services Vétérinaires; USDA APHIS (US export)

BG.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
BG.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
BG.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.

Young animals: Bulgaria accepts non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks that are unvaccinated, or 12–16 weeks old and vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with the owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals, or accompanied by the vaccinated mother. Never allowed from outside the EU.
BG.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
BG.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
BG.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the BFSA before travel.
BG.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Bulgaria and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airports on Bulgaria's point-of-entry list: Sofia, Varna, Burgas and Plovdiv. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
BG.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.

BH.microchip: Required (the microchip number field on the certificate is mandatory).
vaccinations: Rabies: fully vaccinated. The animal must be at least 3 months old.
Dogs: canine distemper, hepatitis (adenovirus), parainfluenza, parvovirus, leptospirosis.
Cats: feline herpesvirus (rhinotracheitis), calicivirus, panleukopenia.
The US-origin certificate requires a first dose, a booster 2 weeks to 1 month later, and 1 month after the booster before export.
BH.rabies_titer: Required on the US-origin certificate: serum antibody of at least 0.5 IU/ml from an accredited laboratory; no sample timing is set. From other origins, confirm with Bahrain Veterinary Quarantine before travel.
documents: Bahrain Veterinary Quarantine import permit (permit number and expiry date are recorded on the certificate)
Official health certificate endorsed by the exporting country's government (US version valid 30 days after issuance)
Vaccination and titre records
BH.import_permit: Required: Bahrain Veterinary Quarantine import permit. The government e-service is 'Import Permit Live Animal (Personal)' on services.bahrain.bh; the permit number and expiry date are recorded on the health certificate.
BH.timeline: Plan at least 3 months before travel: microchip → rabies and core vaccines (booster schedule) → titre test → import permit → endorsed health certificate (within 30 days).
BH.private_aviation: Confirm with the Bahrain veterinary quarantine office and the FBO before the flight how the pet will be cleared on arrival (cabin or cargo).
BH.authority: Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture – Animal Wealth / Veterinary Quarantine

vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory. The international rabies vaccination certificate must be dated more than 15 days and less than 180 days before import (Law of Dec 2009, Art. 91). This is stricter than the usual 1–3-year validity: a pet vaccinated more than 6 months ago needs a booster at least 15 days before arrival.
documents: Health certificate from an official veterinarian of the country of origin, attesting the animals come from a region not declared infected with a transmissible disease for more than 42 days (Art. 91)
International rabies vaccination certificate dated >15 and <180 days before import (Art. 91)
Advance notice to the veterinary inspection services at least 24 hours before arrival (Art. 86)
BI.import_permit: Not stated in the 2009 law. No pet import permit is mentioned. Confirm with Burundi's veterinary services whether any implementing ordinance adds one.
BI.quarantine: 15 days at the entry control post, at the owner's expense, for animals arriving without the Art. 91 health certificate (Art. 98). Compliant animals may be held at the entry post for the time needed for examination, for a few days at most.
BI.timeline: Allow at least 16 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: if the last rabies vaccination is more than about 5 months old, give a booster at least 15 days before arrival → official health certificate → notify Burundi's veterinary inspection at least 24 h before arrival → daytime arrival for inspection.
BI.private_aviation: Arrival must go through an official entry control post (the list is fixed by ministerial ordinance). The mandatory veterinary inspection happens in daytime only, and inspectors need at least 24 hours' notice. Plan a daytime arrival at Bujumbura and pre-notify the veterinary services.
BI.authority: Ministry in charge of livestock — official veterinary services, Burundi

vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory; given more than 1 month and less than 1 year before entry, shown in the pet's vaccination booklet (France Diplomatie). A 3-year vaccine given more than a year ago would not meet this rule, so plan a booster at least 30 days before travel.
documents: Vaccination booklet or certificate showing rabies vaccination 1–12 months old (France Diplomatie)

For US-origin pets (APHIS): Benin is on APHIS's 'Unknown Requirements' list. APHIS advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) plus proof of current rabies vaccination.
BJ.import_permit: Confirm with the Direction de l'Élevage before travel whether an import permit is needed.
BJ.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: if the rabies vaccination is over 1 year old, revaccinate at least 30 days before arrival → vet health certificate (government-endorsed) shortly before departure → confirm with the Direction de l'Élevage whether a permit is needed.
BJ.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Élevage et de la Pêche — Direction de l'Élevage

BL.export: Pets going from Saint-Barthélemy to France or the EU that do not meet EU pet rules require an owner's veterinary-surveillance undertaking (DAAF form).
BL.authority: DAAF Guadeloupe (covers Saint-Barthélemy) / Collectivité de Saint-Barthélemy

BM.microchip: Required, readable by a standard reader (ISO, FECAVA or AVID).
vaccinations: Rabies: first vaccine NOT before 3 months of age; second vaccine 6–12 months after the first; no significant lapses; most recent vaccine at least 30 days and no more than 12 months before arrival (per the US certificate, protocol Sep 2015).
Vaccines must have been given by, or under the supervision of, a vet. Owner- or breeder-given vaccines are not accepted.
BM.parasite_treatment: On the day of the examination (within 10 days of arrival), treat with an acaricide that has residual action against ticks.
documents: Import permit (faxed or emailed back by Veterinary Services, usually within about 1 business day). Valid only 10 days from the date of the vet certificate.
Original health certificate from a licensed vet, inspection within 10 days before arrival. NO USDA endorsement required.
Original rabies certificates.
BM.import_permit: Required for each dog and cat. Your vet faxes or emails the documents to Bermuda Veterinary Services (fax 441-232-0046, animals@gov.bm). Valid 10 days from the vet certificate date.
BM.timeline: Plan at least 10–12 months ahead for a young or unvaccinated pet, because 2 rabies vaccines 6–12 months apart are needed and the pet must be at least 10 months old. For a fully vaccinated pet: vet exam and tick treatment within 10 days of arrival, then the permit.
BM.restricted_breeds: Bermuda prohibits or restricts certain dog breeds. See the list on gov.bm; restricted breeds need prior permission.
BM.authority: Government of Bermuda, Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Veterinary Services

vaccinations: Rabies: at least 60 days and no more than 1 year before departure. Not needed under 3 months of age (CFIA). For UK (rabies-free) origin, rabies vaccination is optional (APHA notes, revised Dec 2023).
BN.rabies_titer: Required for Canada origin (and expected for other non-rabies-free origins such as the USA): approved lab, at least 30 days after vaccination, at least 0.5 IU/ml, valid 1 year from sampling. Confirm against the permit.
documents: Brunei import permit, obtained before export, with transport arrangements and ETA notified
Official export health certificate. UK version: exam no more than 48 hours before export
Rabies vaccination certificate and titer report
Carrier declaration that the animals were carried separately and, if transhipped, kept isolated (UK notes)
BN.import_permit: Yes. From the Department of Agriculture and Agrifood (Veterinary Public Health and Animal Import Management Unit, upa.jpt@agriculture.gov.bn, +673 2388 048). The permit sets the exact conditions.
BN.quarantine: Veterinary inspection on arrival. Suspect animals may be quarantined at the authority's discretion. If documents or shipment rules are not met, quarantine of up to 6 months from arrival (APHA notes).
BN.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (vaccine at least 60 days old): apply for the permit → titer blood draw → result → health certificate and exam shortly before departure.
BN.private_aviation: The permit requires notice of transport arrangements and ETA, and transit landings must keep animals isolated.
BN.authority: Department of Agriculture and Agrifood (DAA), Brunei

vaccinations: Rabies: required for animals over 3 months (SENASAG third-country requirements, 2017 document).
Dogs: distemper, canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (canicola, icterohaemorrhagiae), parvovirus and coronavirus, parainfluenza.
Cats: feline panleukopenia.
The 2017 SENASAG text says vaccinations are to be given within 60 days before shipment, with product, type and date stated; confirm the timing with SENASAG before travel.
BO.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasites treated within 30 days before shipment (SENASAG 2017 document).
documents: Individual zoosanitary certificate from the origin country's official veterinary authority, in Spanish (EU pet passports accepted in place of it per SENASAG regulation)
Inspection and identification by an official vet at embarkation (no tumours, fresh wounds, ectoparasites or signs of transmissible disease)
From the US: APHIS 7001 issued no more than 3 months before arrival, APHIS-endorsed, then legalized at a Bolivian consulate (per USDA APHIS)
BO.import_permit: SENASAG Permiso Zoosanitario de Importación (PZI) listed on VUCE: form SENASAG-IMP-FOR-001, letter to the SENASAG departmental head, origin certificate copy, payment proof; certification issued on arrival at destination customs. Confirm with SENASAG before travel whether it applies to accompanied personal pets.
BO.quarantine: SENASAG may require supervised quarantine of at least 30 days after entry if deemed necessary.
BO.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: confirm PZI need with SENASAG → vaccinations and parasite treatment → official origin certificate (and consular legalization from the US) → SENASAG inspection on arrival.
BO.private_aviation: Confirm with SENASAG that an inspector will attend the private arrival; certification is issued at destination customs.
BO.export: Confirm the export procedure with SENASAG before travel.
BO.authority: SENASAG (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agropecuaria e Inocuidad Alimentaria)

vaccinations: Rabies: valid proof of vaccination required for dogs and cats (Besluit invoer kleine dieren BES, art. 2(2)). If proof is missing, the authority may have the animal vaccinated at the carrier's expense (art. 6).
BQ.rabies_titer: Not required by the BES decree.
documents: Valid health certificate (gezondheidsverklaring), required by art. 2(1); the decree sets no validity window, so confirm the timing with the Bonaire veterinary service.
Valid proof of rabies vaccination (art. 2(2)).
Per Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland, small animals without valid papers are prohibited goods and must be declared to customs on arrival.
BQ.import_permit: No veterinary import permit is set by the BES decree. Pets imported as tax-exempt removal goods need a customs permit from Douane Caribisch Nederland.
BQ.quarantine: None if the conditions are met. If they are not, the animal is quarantined immediately and the carrier must re-ship it at the first opportunity, paying all costs. The animal may be destroyed after quarantine (art. 3). Transit without rabies proof is allowed only in quarantine, for up to 6 weeks (art. 4).
BQ.timeline: Before travel: check the rabies vaccination is valid, then get the health certificate shortly before departure; confirm the certificate timing with the Bonaire veterinary service. Declare the pet to customs on arrival.
BQ.private_aviation: The ban applies to dogs and cats coming from mainland South and Central America (except Suriname), which matters for jets routing through Colombia, Venezuela or Panama. If the conditions are not met, the carrier (operator) must re-ship the animal and pay quarantine costs (art. 3). Declare the pet to customs on arrival at Flamingo Airport (BON).
BQ.authority: Openbaar Lichaam Bonaire veterinary department and Douane Caribisch Nederland, under the Besluit invoer kleine dieren BES (Dutch Ministry of LVVN)

BR.microchip: Not mandatory under Mercosur rules; if electronic ID is used it must be ISO 11784/11785 and its anatomical location stated on the CVI.
vaccinations: Rabies: all animals aged 90 days or more, with a vaccine authorized in the country of application and within its validity; primary vaccination must be at least 21 days before embarkation (animals not revaccinated before expiry count as primary).
Under 90 days: may enter unvaccinated if the CVI certifies age and no contact with urban rabies in the last 90 days.
Animals from WOAH-recognised rabies-free countries/zones are exempt if Brazil recognises the status and it is certified on the CVI.
BR.parasite_treatment: Broad-spectrum treatment against internal AND external parasites within 15 days before CVI issue (date, lab, brand, active ingredient recorded separately for each).
documents: Original CVI on the Mercosur/Portaria 741 model (old-format certificates may be refused), valid 60 days from issue while rabies vaccination is valid
Clinical exam by a registered vet within 10 days before CVI issue (certified on CVI)
Or: official passport valid in the issuing country, containing all CVI data
From the US: APHIS-endorsed certificate valid 60 days from accredited vet signature, valid on arrival (per USDA APHIS)
BR.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats. Other pets (rabbits, ferrets, rodents, etc.) need MAPA import authorization from the SFA of the destination state.
BR.quarantine: None routinely. Non-compliance may lead to refusal, re-export, retention or other measures at the owner's cost. Brazil may refuse animals previously diagnosed with leishmaniasis.
BR.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: antiparasitic treatment within 15 days of the CVI, vet exam within 10 days of the CVI, official CVI/endorsement, then the VIGIAGRO check on arrival. From scratch, plan at least 4 weeks (a primary rabies dose at least 21 days before travel).
BR.private_aviation: Present the pet and original CVI to VIGIAGRO (MAPA) at the international point of entry; confirm VIGIAGRO coverage at the arrival airport/FBO in advance.
BR.export: Leaving Brazil: VIGIAGRO (MAPA) issues the CVI per destination requirements. Request online via gov.br (Bronze/Silver/Gold account), with vaccination record and destination-specific documents; free; review about 48 h; digitally signed PDF. Brazilian pet passport exists (IN MAPA 54/2013). A Brazil-issued CVI allows re-entry to Brazil within 60 days if rabies is valid. Queries: cvi.vigiagro@agro.gov.br.
BR.authority: MAPA – Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária / VIGIAGRO

BS.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip required (dogs), implanted before the rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies (dogs): most recent vaccine given at 12 weeks or older. 1-year vaccine: no less than 1 month and no more than 10 months before import. 3-year vaccine: no less than 1 month and no more than 34 months before import.
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, leptospirosis, hepatitis and parainfluenza, at least 10 days before export.
BS.parasite_treatment: Within 10 days before export: external parasite treatment and a broad-spectrum internal dewormer (licensed in the US).
documents: BAHFSA veterinary import permit.

US export health certificate for pet dogs or cats (VEHCS forms dated Sep 2026). Inspection within 10 days before export. Includes New World screwworm statements if the animal comes from an APHIS-defined NWS-infested zone.
From 1 Jan 2027: electronically signed by the accredited vet AND electronically endorsed by APHIS.
BS.import_permit: Required. Apply through the Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA) e-permitting portal at least 4 weeks before travel.
BS.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: check the rabies vaccine falls within the allowed window, apply for the BAHFSA permit at least 4 weeks ahead, then do the vet exam, deworming and tick treatment within 10 days before departure, followed by the APHIS endorsement. For other origins, confirm the conditions with BAHFSA when applying for the permit.
BS.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including crosses): Pit Bull, Presa Canario, Cane Corso, American Bully, Dogo Argentino, Staffordshire Terrier.
BS.private_aviation: BAHFSA conditions for other regulated animals (Sep 2026) require 24 hours' notice of arrival to Veterinary Services and a separate inspection fee for landings after 5 pm Mon–Fri, on weekends or on public holidays. Confirm the same applies to dogs and cats when the permit is issued.
BS.authority: Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA), Veterinary Services Unit

documents: BFDA import permit (application fee Nu 100–300)
Supporting health and vaccination documents submitted for BFDA verification
BT.import_permit: Yes. Permit issued by BFDA after document verification.
BT.quarantine: 15 days for all imported pets (clinical observation, testing, vaccination). Personal pets are quarantined at the owner's home under official monitoring. Commercial imports pay Nu 500 per pet.
BT.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel and contact BFDA first. Paro (PBH) is the only international airport.
BT.private_aviation: Paro is the only international airport. Coordinate the BFDA inspection in advance.
BT.authority: Bhutan Food and Drug Authority (BFDA, formerly BAFRA)

BW.microchip: Microchip number required on the US-origin certificate. The UK certificate accepts any identification including tattoo. An ISO 11784/11785 chip is recommended.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export (UK EHC 3893). US certificate: current at export; animals under 3 months may travel if the dam was vaccinated.
Other vaccinations: the UK OV must be satisfied that 'necessary vaccinations' were done (core vaccines advisable).
documents: Botswana veterinary import permit (DVS)
Official health certificate (UK: OV exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days; US: APHIS Botswana certificate, USDA-endorsed)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Owner declaration: not imported into the exporting country in the past 6 months (UK)
South African in-transit permit if routed via South Africa
BW.import_permit: Required: 'No dog or cat may be imported into Botswana except in accordance with the terms of an import permit' (UK NFG 3893). Issued by the Director of Veterinary Services, Private Bag 0032, Gaborone. gov.bw lists the import permit service as free, processed in about 1 working day, through District Veterinary Offices (help: DVSpermits@gov.bw, +267 368 9510/9513).
BW.quarantine: No routine quarantine for compliant pets. Non-compliant animals may be quarantined, re-exported or euthanised at the owner's cost.
BW.timeline: Allow at least 14 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: apply for the DVS import permit (about 1 working day per gov.bw) → South African transit permit if needed → vet exam within 48 hours (UK model) or USDA-endorsed certificate → travel.
BW.private_aviation: A direct private flight into Botswana avoids the South African transit permit; arrange DVS inspection at the arrival airport in advance.
BW.export: Namibia accepts Botswana-origin pets with a state-vet health certificate and rabies vaccination.
BW.authority: Ministry of Lands and Agriculture – Department of Veterinary Services (DVS), Botswana

BY.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules (strongly recommended; required in practice to match documents)
vaccinations: Rabies: all dogs/cats ≥3 months, given ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within the last 12 months (multi-year vaccine accepted while valid, or titer ≥0.5 IU/ml)
Dogs: distemper, infectious hepatitis (adenovirus), parvovirus, leptospirosis (or dihydrostreptomycin prophylaxis) — ≥20 days and ≤12 months before travel
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days and ≤12 months before travel
BY.rabies_titer: Not required; only an alternative to a lapsed vaccination (≥0.5 IU/ml)
BY.parasite_treatment: Not mandatory (any treatment given should be recorded)
documents: ≤2 pets: international veterinary passport with vaccinations and competent-authority mark of clinical exam within 14 days before dispatch, OR
EAEU Veterinary Certificate Form 15 (APHIS: vet exam and issue within 5 days, APHIS-endorsed); cats examined clinically for ringworm
BY.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal dogs/cats (EAEU). More than 2 / unaccompanied may need a permit and quarantine. APHIS states up to 5 pets total without special permission on Form 15
BY.quarantine: None for compliant personal pets (≤2 under EAEU passport rule; ≤5 under APHIS/Form 15 guidance)
BY.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: rabies + core vaccines ≥20 days before travel → clinical exam/certificate within 5 days (Form 15) or 14 days (passport mark)
BY.private_aviation: Heavily restricted: EU bans Belarusian carriers and EU operators avoid Belarus airspace; US export controls restrict flights of US-origin aircraft to Belarus. Check with Elysium Jet operations
BY.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Food of Belarus — Department of Veterinary and Food Supervision (EAEU rules)

vaccinations: Rabies: pets under 4 months are home-quarantined in Belize until 30 days after a registered vet vaccinates them. Rabies timing for older pets is set in the BAHA permit conditions.
Strongly recommended: dogs (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus); cats (rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia).
BZ.parasite_treatment: Strongly recommended: internal and external parasite treatment within 30 days of export.
documents: BAHA import permit (application and current requirements on the BAHA website).
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet. USDA APHIS endorsement NOT required.
BZ.import_permit: Required for all dogs and cats. Belize Agricultural Health Authority (animalhealthbz@gmail.com, +501 824-4872/99).
BZ.quarantine: Home quarantine for pets under 4 months (until 30 days after rabies vaccination).
BZ.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: BAHA permit, vet certificate, 2 days' notice.
BZ.private_aviation: Notify BAHA of the date, time and flight at least 2 days before arrival. A BAHA official inspects every pet; the crate must be new or disinfected.
BZ.export: Return to the US: Belize IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country. US dogs need the USDA-endorsed Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination before leaving the US; foreign-vaccinated dogs must arrive at an airport with a CDC-registered facility. A screwworm certificate (official vet, inspection within 5 days) is also required.

CA.microchip: Not specifically required by CFIA for personal pets. The certificate must clearly identify the animal.
vaccinations: Dogs and cats 3 months or older: valid certificate showing current rabies vaccination, issued in English or French by a licensed vet. The APHIS Canada page says the vaccination must be current within 3 years of import.
Alternatives to vaccination: proof the animal comes from a CFIA-recognized rabies-free country where it lived for the past 6 months, OR a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml.
Animals under 3 months: no rabies requirement (proof of age may be requested).

Personal dogs under 8 months travelling unaccompanied: also need a vet certificate issued within 72 hours of import (dog at least 8 weeks old, vaccinated for distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and parainfluenza at 6 weeks or older).
CA.rabies_titer: Optional alternative to vaccination: RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/ml (drawn at least 30 days, or 3–4 weeks for dogs, after any prior vaccination).
documents: Rabies vaccination certificate (English or French) identifying the animal, or a rabies-free-country certificate, or a titer result.
Unaccompanied personal dogs under 8 months: vet health certificate within 72 hours of import (no APHIS endorsement needed from the US).
Assistance dogs accompanying their user: not subject to import restrictions.
CA.import_permit: Not required for personal pets. Commercial dogs under 8 months need CFIA import permits and kennel-of-origin and quarantine-facility conditions. Commercial dogs from high-risk countries are prohibited (no permits issued).
CA.quarantine: None. Pet dogs from any country are not subject to post-import quarantine. An inspector may order vaccination at the owner's expense if the paperwork is deficient.
CA.timeline: Allow at least 3 days for a pet already rabies-vaccinated: carry the rabies vaccination certificate in English or French that identifies the pet; no permit and no titre. From scratch, plan at least 1 month: rabies vaccination by a licensed vet (no minimum wait is stated, but the vaccination must be valid on arrival); for the titre route instead of vaccination, add 30+ days.
CA.restricted_breeds: None federally. Provincial or municipal rules apply (e.g. Ontario's pit bull ban), so check locally.
CA.private_aviation: Pets are presented to CBSA at the arrival airport with the rabies certificate; CFIA sets no separate rule for private aircraft.
CA.export: Leaving Canada: the destination's certificate is issued by a licensed vet and endorsed by CFIA where the destination requires it. Dogs going to the US follow CDC low-risk rules (Canada isn't a CDC high-risk country): CDC Dog Import Form, age 6 months or older, microchip.
CA.authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA); border inspection by CBSA

CG.microchip: Not required by the Congolese arrêté; APHIS certificate identifies by microchip number and/or name (vet verifies any listed microchip).
vaccinations: Rabies: per Congolese Arrêté (1968, art. 5), certificate showing vaccination given more than 1 month and less than 6 months before travel; dogs/cats under 3 months exempt from formalities. APHIS certificate records date, vaccine, batch and validity end date.
documents: Certificate of origin and health issued shortly before departure (the 1968 order, art. 5, indicates 3 days; confirm with the veterinary services)
Rabies vaccination certificate

US origin: APHIS bilingual 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to the Republic of Congo' by USDA-accredited vet, valid 30 days; APHIS digital endorsement accepted — printed endorsed certificate must accompany the animal
CG.import_permit: Not required for carnivores under the 1968 arrêté (permit regime applies to live animals other than carnivores); APHIS mentions none.
CG.quarantine: None for dogs/cats in the arrêté; veterinary inspection on arrival — animals showing contagious disease or lacking documents may be refused entry.
CG.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination 1–6 months before arrival → vet exam and health certificate a few days before departure (US: within 30-day validity) → government endorsement → travel with originals.
CG.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Élevage et de la Pêche — Direction des services vétérinaires

CH.microchip: Microchip required, implanted before rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: first dose from 12 weeks of age, valid 21 days later; must follow microchipping.
CH.rabies_titer: Required from rabies high-risk third countries: antibody titration test at an EU-designated laboratory with long waiting periods (EU standard: sample ≥ 30 days after vaccination, travel ≥ 3 months after sample). Animals under 7 months may not enter from high-risk countries. Not required from EU or listed/low-risk countries.
documents: From EU: Swiss or EU pet passport.
From third countries: Swiss/EU passport if already compliant, otherwise health certificate issued by exporting country's authorities.
From high-risk countries by direct flight: FSVO import authorisation (application form on blv.admin.ch).
Owner travelling separately: authorised person, owner within 5 days, written declaration in passport.
Max 5 pets per private vehicle unless for events (registered, >6 months old; third-country animals need FSVO authorisation).
CH.import_permit: FSVO import authorisation required for direct air arrivals from rabies high-risk countries; otherwise none.
CH.quarantine: None if requirements met; pets with missing documents are refused entry.
CH.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA (not a rabies high-risk country): health certificate endorsed by the exporting authority. From the EU: pet passport only. From scratch (EU/low-risk origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination at ≥ 12 weeks → 21 days. High-risk origin: at least 4 months and pet ≥ 7 months old (vaccination → titer test → waiting period → FSVO authorisation → certificate).
CH.restricted_breeds: Import of dogs with docked ears and/or tails is prohibited. Cantonal dog-breed rules exist; check with the destination canton before travel.
CH.private_aviation: Direct flights from third countries (including the UK, USA and UAE): accompanied pets (cabin or excess baggage) may only land at Basel, Geneva or Zurich; unaccompanied pets (air waybill) only Geneva or Zurich. The pet must be presented at the red customs exit for a mandatory entry control. Sion, Lugano, Bern, Samedan (St. Moritz) and other regional airports are NOT listed for direct third-country arrivals with pets: clear at Geneva/Zurich/Basel first, or enter Schengen at a designated EU point of entry and then continue. From EU/Schengen states: no border veterinary check, but documents are required. Rabies high-risk countries: FSVO import authorisation needed for direct flights.
CH.export: Destination rules apply; veterinary certificates for leaving are issued by the responsible cantonal veterinary service. Ensure Swiss re-entry conditions are met before departure.
CH.authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV)

CI.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): the certificate verifies any microchip listed for identification.
vaccinations: Rabies: must be current. For US-origin pets (APHIS): if primary vaccination, or a booster given after the previous vaccine's validity expired, wait at least 21 days before import; a booster given within validity needs no wait.

French MFA travel advice (Sep 2026): rabies vaccination must be at least 1 month and less than 1 year old. Apply this stricter window: a 3-year vaccine given over a year ago needs a booster at least 30 days before travel.
CI.parasite_treatment: For US-origin pets (APHIS certificate): vet certifies animals free of mange for at least the last 6 months; no specific treatment mandated.
documents: Prior import authorization (autorisation préalable d'importation) from the DSV, Ministry of Animal and Fish Resources
Official veterinary health certificate (US: APHIS 'ivory-coast-cat-dog' form, valid 10 days, original ink USDA endorsement and embossing required)
Rabies vaccination certificate / vaccination record
Owner declaration of 6-month residency (UK-origin guidance only)
Health and identification booklet (microchip or tattoo). Per France Diplomatie, pets are admitted 'with the special permission of customs'.
CI.import_permit: Required. Apply to the DSV using the bilingual DSV application form; send the completed form and a copy of the rabies certificate by email (APHIS lists carv.dsvci@gmail.com and dsv.sdsa2017@gmail.com). An endorsed health certificate is not needed for the application. The DSV form asks for a copy of the international veterinary certificate and vaccination record.
