CI.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: make sure the rabies vaccine is 1–12 months old (booster ≥30 days before travel if needed) → email the permit application to the DSV → health certificate and government endorsement within 10 days of travel → carry the original permit and certificate.
CI.restricted_breeds: Pets are not allowed in national parks and reserves (France Diplomatie).
CI.authority: Direction des Services Vétérinaires (DSV), Ministère des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques, Côte d'Ivoire

vaccinations: Dogs from NZ: distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus 1-3 months before export (parvovirus at 17+ weeks of age).
CK.parasite_treatment: Dogs from NZ: praziquantel (5 mg/kg) and a roundworm/whipworm anthelmintic within 3 days of departure; two insecticidal washes 7 days apart, the last within 3 days of departure; free of ectoparasites (especially ticks) at the exam within 3 days of departure.
documents: Biosecurity import permit (Application Form for Live Animal)
Exporter's statutory declaration: 6 months' residence (or since birth), at least 4 months old, disease-free for 30 days
International animal health certificate signed by a full-time government vet of the exporting country
Dogs: Police import permit
CK.import_permit: Yes: from the Director of Biosecurity, Ministry of Agriculture (biosecurity@cookislands.gov.ck, +682 28710). Dogs also need a Police permit.
CK.quarantine: The pet is inspected and treated on arrival and held in the biosecurity area until a Permit to Land is issued. No fixed quarantine period is stated.
CK.timeline: Plan at least 3 months: permits (Biosecurity and Police), vaccines 1-3 months before export, treatments and government vet exam within 3 days of departure, and flight details to Biosecurity at least 1 working day before shipping.
CK.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs (Police, Dogs Registration Amendment Act 1991): Doberman, Pit Bull Terrier, Bull Dogs, Rottweiler, plus any breed the Police specify. All imported dogs must be neutered or spayed and registered with the Police.
CK.private_aviation: The conditions require import only by air as manifested cargo. Confirm private-aircraft arrangements with Biosecurity.
CK.authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Biosecurity Service, Cook Islands

CL.microchip: Mandatory permanent individual ID: microchip (ISO 11784/11785) or tattoo; number must match the CVI.
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory. Primary-vaccinated animals (first dose, or last dose given after the previous one expired), regardless of age, must be vaccinated at least 21 days before entry to Chile.
Non-primary animals: CVI must certify the last 2 rabies doses (otherwise treated as primary).
Exemption: animals that lived since birth or ≥6 continuous months in a country free of dog-transmitted rabies recognised by Chile, certified by the origin authority.
CL.parasite_treatment: Broad-spectrum treatment effective against internal AND external parasites between 5 and 30 days before CVI issue; CVI must state date, trade name, active ingredient and dose of each product.
documents: Original CVI from the origin country's competent veterinary authority, in Spanish plus origin language or English; valid 10 days from issue, extendable max 5 days depending on travel
Clinical exam by a vet within 10 days before CVI issue
CVI must include species, breed, sex, age, ID number, neutered status, owner details, transport mode, whether accompanied, last 2 rabies vaccinations (serial, lab, validity), antiparasitic details
From EU countries: EU pet passport (Spanish or English) accepted if it shows compliance
CL.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats (ferrets need a SAG wildlife import authorization).
CL.quarantine: No fixed quarantine in the resolution; if requirements are not met SAG may apply sanitary measures at any authorised entry point at the importer's cost, plus sanctions.
CL.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: antiparasitic treatment 5–30 days before the CVI, vet exam within 10 days of the CVI, official CVI (valid 10 + 5 days), then SAG inspection on arrival. From scratch, plan at least 4–5 weeks (microchip, then a primary rabies dose at least 21 days before entry).
CL.restricted_breeds: None for import (SENASA Argentina destination page: not contemplated).
CL.private_aviation: Pets must be presented at an authorised border control point with SAG presence; confirm SAG inspection at the arrival airport/FBO in advance. Note the very short 10-day CVI window.
CL.export: Leaving Chile: SAG issues a Certificado Zoosanitario de Exportación (CZE). Pets returning to Chile may re-enter within 60 calendar days of CZE issue with the original/official copy, if rabies is valid and the animal has permanent ISO microchip or tattoo; trips longer than 60 days require full import requirements.

CM.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip number must be listed and verified by the vet. UK certificate allows identification incl. tattoo.
vaccinations: Rabies (US origin, APHIS): current at time of export; certificate records date, vaccine, batch and end of validity.
Rabies (UK origin, EHC 3038): given not less than 30 days and not more than 12 months before export; copy of vaccination certificate attached.
documents: US origin: APHIS 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to Cameroon' (form dated Aug 2025) by USDA-accredited vet, valid 30 days; original USDA ink-signed and embossed endorsement must accompany the animal
UK origin: Export Health Certificate 3038 signed by an Official Veterinarian, exam within 48 h of export, valid 10 days from signature
CM.import_permit: The UK certificate has a field 'Import permit no. (if applicable)'; APHIS does not mention a permit. Confirm with MINEPIA before travel whether an import authorisation is needed.
CM.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: microchip + rabies vaccination (≥30 days before for UK route) → ask MINEPIA whether an import permit is needed → vet exam/certificate (US: within 30 days; UK: within 48 h, valid 10 days) → government endorsement → travel with originals.
CM.authority: Ministère de l'Élevage, des Pêches et des Industries Animales (MINEPIA)

CN.microchip: ISO 11784/11785, 15-digit, required for the quarantine-exempt route. Bring a reader for non-ISO chips.
vaccinations: Rabies: official rabies vaccination certificate, current at arrival. The quarantine-exempt route requires at least two lifetime doses (per APHIS).
CN.rabies_titer: Pets from non-designated countries/regions: rabies antibody result of at least 0.5 IU/ml from a GACC-recognised lab. Sample taken on or after the 2nd vaccination. Valid up to 1 year from sampling (per APHIS). Not required from GACC-designated countries/regions (e.g. Hawaii and Guam per APHIS; check the current GACC list).
documents: Official health/quarantine certificate from the exporting country's veterinary authority, one per pet, naming the traveller, who must match the passport. For US origin: issued within 14 days of arrival and USDA-endorsed.
Original rabies vaccination certificate
Rabies titer report (non-designated origins, quarantine-exempt route)
Passport copy and a printed photo of the pet (per APHIS)
CN.import_permit: No import permit for personal pets. On the quarantine route, notify Chinese Customs in advance.
CN.quarantine: None if fully compliant (on-site customs inspection only). Otherwise 30 days in a customs-designated isolation facility at a designated port, at the owner's cost. Guide, hearing and search-and-rescue dogs have their own route.
CN.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel: microchip → rabies #1 → rabies #2 → titer blood draw → result → health certificate within 14 days before arrival (US) → government endorsement. Dogs must be registered with local police within about 1 month of arrival (per APHIS).
CN.private_aviation: A fully compliant pet (chip, 2 vaccinations, titer) may enter through any port, including business-aviation arrivals at an open international port. A non-compliant pet must enter through a designated port with quarantine facilities. APHIS lists Beijing Capital, Shanghai Pudong, Shanghai Hongqiao, Guangzhou Baiyun, Urumqi Diwopu, plus several rail and sea ports; the full GACC list is longer. The one-pet-per-person limit still applies.
CN.export: Local customs (GACC) issues the export animal health certificate after inspection, based on the destination's requirements. Arrange with customs at the departure port in advance.
CN.authority: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (GACC)

CO.microchip: Not mentioned in ICA entry requirements.
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccine name, lot, date and validity certified; primary vaccination at least 21 days before embarkation. If the origin country does not vaccinate against rabies, home quarantine and vaccination in Colombia.
Dogs: distemper, canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (canicola, icterohaemorrhagiae), parvovirus, coronavirus, parainfluenza.
Cats: panleukopenia, viral rhinotracheitis, calicivirus.
Minimum age for entry: 15 weeks.
CO.parasite_treatment: Internal and external antiparasitic treatment within 60 days before the trip; product name, active ingredient and date on the certificate.
documents: Health certificate issued or endorsed by the origin country's official veterinary authority (original seal/signature or electronic signature), dated ≤10 calendar days before entry, stating animal is free of infectious/parasitic disease and fit to travel
Current vaccination certificate
Pre-CIS request and payment receipt (if done in SISPAP); one request per species, up to 10 animals
From the US: APHIS-endorsed health certificate within 10 days of travel plus rabies certificate; no consular stamp needed (per USDA APHIS)
CO.import_permit: No ICA import permit for personal pet dogs and cats; ICA issues the CIS on arrival after documentary and physical inspection. Fee paid online via SISPAP (Colombian bank account) or by card at the ICA office (no cash).
CO.quarantine: Only if non-compliant: retention, home quarantine, re-shipment or euthanasia at owner's cost.
CO.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: deworming within 60 days, official health certificate within 10 days before entry, SISPAP Pre-CIS and payment, then ICA inspection on arrival. From scratch, plan at least 4 weeks (a first rabies dose at least 21 days before).
CO.private_aviation: ICA offices operate at international airports, border crossings and seaports; for arrivals outside ICA hours, Sundays or holidays, tick 'Servicio Especial' in the SISPAP Pre-CIS request.
CO.export: Leaving Colombia: ICA issues an export CIS only at its airport/port/border offices; the request is filed in SISPAP (by the owner or private vet) with health and vaccination certificates plus destination-specific annexes. Framework: ICA Res. 100164 of 2021. Five or more animals per user are treated as commercial.

vaccinations: Rabies: dogs and cats over 3 months, vaccine valid on the day of entry.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and leptospirosis.
Cats: rhinotracheitis, calicivirus and panleukopenia.
CR.parasite_treatment: Endo- and ectoparasite treatment within 15 days before export (product, active ingredient and lot recorded); free of ticks.
documents: US health certificate for dogs and cats to Costa Rica (exam within 2 weeks of departure), endorsed by APHIS (digital via VEHCS).
CR.import_permit: Required only for unaccompanied pets (MAG/SENASA importer process).
CR.timeline: Plan at least 3 weeks before travel: vaccines current, parasite treatment within 15 days, vet exam within 14 days, APHIS endorsement.
CR.export: Return to the US: Costa Rica is NOT on the CDC high-risk list. It is screwworm-affected, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
CR.authority: Servicio Nacional de Salud Animal (SENASA), Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería

vaccinations: Rabies: required (Res. 165/2026, art. 18.1a).
Other vaccines 'established in import requirements' are not listed in the regulation. Confirm with CENASA.
documents: Veterinary certificate issued in the country of origin (art. 18.1a). Its content is harmonised between CENASA and the origin authority (art. 20).
CU.import_permit: Not specified for accompanied pets. CENASA's director publishes a resolution, after risk analysis, listing countries and products eligible for travellers' imports (art. 17).
CU.quarantine: Arrival inspection is mandatory at ports and airports (art. 16). Dogs and cats may do home quarantine under the territorial animal-health department's supervision, if CENASA's requirements are met (arts. 13 and 43). Duration is not published. Non-compliant animals may be held, confiscated or re-shipped (art. 24).
CU.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: get CENASA's current requirements in writing (vaccines, certificate validity), then vaccinate, then get the origin veterinary certificate. Expect inspection and home quarantine on arrival.
CU.private_aviation: Aircraft arriving from abroad may not arrive with live animals unless authorised by CENASA, nor release animals, including pets, without animal-health control (Res. 165/2026, art. 42.3). The inspector briefs the captain on arrival. Get prior CENASA clearance for a private arrival. US sanctions and travel restrictions on Cuba also apply.
CU.export: Return to the US: Cuba is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country. US dogs need the USDA-endorsed CDC rabies certification before leaving the US, and Cuba is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list.
CU.authority: Centro Nacional de Sanidad Animal (CENASA), Ministerio de la Agricultura, Cuba

CW.microchip: ISO microchip; number and implant date on the certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine at 12 weeks or older, at least 21 days before departure, within the manufacturer's 12–36-month validity.
CW.parasite_treatment: Ectoparasites: treatment 14 days before departure with a product giving at least 28 days' persistent efficacy. Endoparasites: registered treatment within 14 days before departure. Record dates and products.
documents: Official international health certificate by an accredited vet, endorsed by USDA with an original ink signature and embossing, valid at most 2 weeks.
CW.import_permit: None listed on the APHIS page.
CW.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies (21 days), parasite treatments and certificate within 14 days, USDA ink endorsement (allow mail time).
CW.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier-type dogs may not be imported.
CW.authority: Ministry of Health, Environment and Nature (GMN) – Veterinary Service, Curaçao

CY.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
CY.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
CY.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.

documents: Import permit, sent by fax or email once the requirements are met.

Under the Animals Diseases (Importation) Control Regulations (Chap. 61:02, reg. 10, as amended 1990), the certificate must be by a government veterinary officer of the exporting country. Reg. 10(1) (as amended 1990) allows dogs and cats only directly from Great Britain, Northern Ireland, Ireland and Commonwealth Caribbean territories. EE.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Agriculture and Food Board before travel.
EE.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Estonia and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry: Tallinn, Tartu, Pärnu, Kuressaare, Kärdla and Ämari (the Tax and Customs Board performs the checks). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
EE.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.

EG.microchip: Not required for entry (per the USDA–Egypt certificate). Listed if present.
vaccinations: Rabies: given at least 30 days before entry and no more than 11 months before arrival: the pet must arrive at least 30 days before the 12-month anniversary of the vaccination (USDA–Egypt certificate).
documents: Health certificate from a licensed or government veterinarian in the origin country, valid 14 days from issue (US version endorsed by APHIS)
Rabies vaccination record
EG.quarantine: No quarantine stated. Inspection on arrival by the Ministry of Agriculture veterinary service.
EG.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination at least 30 days and no more than 11 months before arrival → health certificate within 14 days → arrival inspection.
EG.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation – General Organization for Veterinary Services (GOVS)

ES.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
ES.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
ES.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Spain does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
ES.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
ES.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
ES.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Ministry of Agriculture (MAPA) before travel.
ES.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories) must enter through a travellers' point of entry on MAPA's list (updated 2 Jun 2026). Airports listed: Madrid-Barajas (check at the Air Cargo Centre), Barcelona-El Prat (owner collects the animal's documents at the cargo warehouse, WFS or Swissport, then goes to the Animal Health office), Palma de Mallorca (Son Sant Joan), Málaga, Valencia, Alicante, Sevilla, Girona, Reus, Jerez, Santiago de Compostela, Vitoria, Santander, Bilbao, Gran Canaria, Tenerife Norte, Tenerife Sur, Lanzarote, Fuerteventura and La Palma, plus several ports. Ibiza, Menorca and Madrid-Torrejón are not on the list: a private jet arriving there from outside the EU with a pet is not compliant, so route the first EU landing via a listed airport (e.g. Palma, Barcelona, Madrid). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no border check, documents must be carried. Non-compliant animals face re-dispatch, isolation or euthanasia.
ES.export: To EU: EU pet passport. To non-EU: destination rules; export certificates are issued/legalised by the Government 'Áreas de Agricultura' (appointment required for legalisation).
ES.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAPA)

ET.microchip: Microchip identification listed and verified on the official certificate (APHIS July 2026 certificate; UK certificates identify by microchip number).
vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (APHIS). UK-origin: given at least 30 days before export and still valid.
Leptospirosis: UK-origin dogs, at least 30 days before export (UK EHC 6543).
Slovenia/EU-origin certificate (2024): primary rabies 6–12 months before shipment (given at 3+ months of age) or booster within the last year, unless from a rabies-free country.
ET.parasite_treatment: Certificates require animals clinically free of external parasites (UK) / internal and external parasites (Slovenian certificate, exam within 72 hours); Slovenian certificate also requires screwworm inspection within 5 days before shipment.
documents: Ethiopian import permit from Ministry of Agriculture (Animal & Plant Health Regulatory Directorate) — must accompany the animal (UK guidance)
Official veterinary health certificate (US: APHIS 'pet-dogs-cats-ethiopia' form, July 2026, valid 30 days, digital VEHCS endorsement accepted; UK: valid 10 days, exam within 48 hours)
Rabies vaccination certificate
ET.import_permit: Required per UK official guidance (dogs: Veterinary Public Health, Inspection and Quarantine Team; cats: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal & Plant Health Regulatory Directorate, Addis Ababa). Not mentioned on the APHIS page; confirm with the Ministry.
ET.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 30 days before export): apply for the Ethiopian import permit → vet exam (48–72 h before) and government-endorsed certificate (US certificate valid 30 days) → carry the permit and originals. From scratch, plan at least 6–8 weeks.
ET.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal & Plant Health Regulatory Directorate (Ethiopia)

FJ.microchip: Required: readable by AVID, TROVAN, DESTRON or an ISO-compatible reader.
vaccinations: As specified in the permit, by origin country.
FJ.rabies_titer: Set by the permit according to origin; not stated on the BAF page.
FJ.parasite_treatment: Treatments and their intervals are specified in the permit.
documents: Original BAF import permit (valid 6 months)
Home-country health certificate
Veterinary certificates with all lab results
Vaccination records
Microchip proof
FJ.import_permit: Yes. Apply to BAF (animalimports@baf.com.fj) and pay the fee on lodgement. Processing takes about 5 working days and the permit is valid 6 months.
FJ.quarantine: Mandatory PEQ at Koronivia, Nausori. The minimum period is set by BAF/permit (not stated on the page). Book at least 1 month before arrival. Guide and service dogs may be exempt case by case.
FJ.timeline: Plan at least 2-3 months (longer if origin requires rabies serology): apply for the permit, book PEQ 1+ month ahead, complete tests and treatments per the permit, notify BAF Nadi and the Chief Veterinary Officer before arrival.
FJ.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terriers (including American Pit Bull Terrier and crosses); serval cats and serval hybrids within 5 generations. Pets under 4 months and females more than 21 days pregnant are not allowed.
FJ.private_aviation: BAF requires the most direct route, intact crate seals, and confirmation that the aircraft carries no animals from other countries. Notify BAF Nadi Airport (+679 6720053) and the CVO (+679 3312512) in advance. Confirm private-aircraft arrangements with BAF.

FK.parasite_treatment: Not published for imports. Note: all dogs on the Islands are dosed with praziquantel every five weeks under the hydatid control programme.
documents: Import licence from the Veterinary Service (Department of Agriculture)
Veterinary health certification from the exporting country as specified in the licence
FK.import_permit: Required: import licence from the Veterinary Service (tel. +500 27366).
FK.quarantine: All live animals undergo a period of quarantine after arrival; duration not published.
FK.timeline: Plan at least 3 months before travel: contact Veterinary Service → obtain import licence and its specific conditions → health certification in origin country → quarantine on arrival.
FK.private_aviation: Confirm with the Department of Agriculture how quarantine/inspection is handled for private arrivals before booking.
FK.export: Contact the Department of Agriculture Veterinary Service for export certification.
FK.authority: Falkland Islands Government – Department of Agriculture, Veterinary Service / Biosecurity

FO.microchip: Required: ISO 11784 microchip (HDX or FDX-B, readable with ISO 11785). The number must appear on the permit application, the permit and the health certificate.
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, canine distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, parvovirus, parainfluenza, leptospirosis
Cats: rabies, feline panleukopenia, feline viral rhinotracheitis, feline calicivirus, feline leukaemia virus (FeLV)

All vaccinations at least 4 weeks old on arrival and within the manufacturer's validity. On-time boosters need no waiting period. Puppies/kittens must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated and arrive no earlier than 4 weeks after the last required vaccination.
FO.rabies_titer: Group A countries (Denmark excl. Greenland, Finland, Ireland, Iceland, Norway excl. Svalbard, UK, Sweden): not required. Group B countries (most other EU states, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Greenland, Svalbard): required, ≥0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved lab, sample at least 4 weeks after rabies vaccination; entry no earlier than 12 weeks after the sample. Other countries (e.g. USA): conditions set case by case by the Chief Veterinary Officer (§11).
FO.parasite_treatment: Required, within the product's validity when travel begins. Dogs: roundworm, French heartworm (Angiostrongylus vasorum), tapeworm incl. Echinococcus granulosus and E. multilocularis, scabies, lice, fleas, Ixodes ricinus ticks. Cats: same list except French heartworm. Must be certified in the health certificate.
documents: HFS import permit application on the official form (a copy of the pet passport is not enough), with receipt for the fee (minimum DKK 750)
Veterinary health certificate on the HFS form (clinical exam and parasite treatments). It must reach HFS (hfs@hfs.fo) 2 business days before departure and be no more than 2 days old at departure
Import permit signed by an HFS official veterinarian, carried with the animal and shown to customs on arrival
FO.import_permit: Required for every dog/cat, issued by the Faroese Food and Veterinary Authority (HFS). Only for permanent residents or people moving to the Faroes. Apply at least 6 business days before departure. Carriers must refuse to transport a pet without a valid permit.
FO.quarantine: None for compliant pets. Non-compliant pets may be quarantined under HFS supervision, returned to the country of dispatch or euthanised at the owner's expense.
FO.timeline: Visitors: not possible. Residents and people moving to the Faroes, from group A countries: apply at least 6 business days before departure → health certificate no more than 2 days before departure, sent to HFS 2 business days ahead (so departures are only possible Wednesday–Saturday; HFS publishes special dates around holidays). From group B: add a titer test and 12 weeks from the blood sample. From other countries: case-by-case conditions.
FO.restricted_breeds: Dog breeds deemed dangerous are prohibited (list on hfs.fo). Hybrids are prohibited regardless of percentage, e.g. wolfdogs, Bengal and Savannah cats.
FO.private_aviation: Executive Order 82/2021 §6(3): dogs and cats taken on board aircraft or ships abroad may not be landed in the Faroes, and the crew must ensure they stay on board. This does not apply to approved transport units of an authorised carrier. §45: carriers transporting dogs/cats to the Faroes must hold an animal-transport authorisation, carry the valid permit and have a reception facility. §6(2): the owner or a designated escort must accompany the animal. Transit with a pet through the Faroes is prohibited.
FO.export: Faroese residents travelling abroad and returning need an HFS travel permit (ferðaloyvi), with separate forms for group A and group B countries. EU lists the Faroes as an Annex I territory for entry into the EU.
FO.authority: Heilsufrøðiliga Starvsstovan (HFS, Faroese Food and Veterinary Authority), Smyrilsvegur 7, FO-100 Tórshavn, +298 55 64 00, hfs@hfs.fo

Otherwise commercial rules apply.

Young animals: France does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU. (French Customs: dogs under 16 weeks are not admitted.)
FR.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.

From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
FR.restricted_breeds: Category 1 (attack dogs, import banned, including in transit): dogs of Staffordshire Terrier / American Staffordshire Terrier ('pit-bull'), Mastiff ('boerbull') or Tosa type WITHOUT registration in a recognised pedigree book. Category 2 (import allowed with proof of pedigree registration; leash, muzzle and owner obligations apply): pedigree Staffordshire Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier and Tosa, and ALL Rottweilers or Rottweiler-type dogs with or without pedigree. Bengal and Savannah cats without proof of breed (pedigree/birth certificate) are treated as hybrids and need a prior import permit from the regional DREAL. Wolf-dog hybrids likewise. Any dog imported from a third country must have at least one adult tooth (Code rural L236-1), which in practice excludes very young puppies.
FR.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must present the pet to French Customs (red channel) for documentary and identity checks before leaving the international zone; no appointment is needed. French Customs carry out these checks at all points open to international passenger traffic, so customs-staffed international airports such as Paris-Le Bourget (LFPB) and Nice (LFMN) can receive pets travelling with their owners; ask the FBO to pre-notify the customs post at the airport. A small airfield without permanent customs does not qualify. More than 5 pets per person, or pets travelling more than 5 days apart from the owner, are commercial movements and must go through a border control post (Le Bourget is not one; Paris-CDG, Nice, Lyon, Marseille, Toulouse and Deauville are). EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliant animals can be re-exported, isolated at the owner's cost or, as a last resort, euthanised.
FR.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
FR.authority: Ministry of Agriculture (DGAL) and French Customs (DGDDI)

GB.microchip: Microchip before (or at the same time as) rabies vaccination; otherwise revaccination needed.
vaccinations: Rabies: pet ≥12 weeks; wait at least 21 full days after the first vaccination (or last dose of primary course); boosters within validity need no wait.
GB.rabies_titer: Great Britain: required only from unlisted countries (not EU and not listed): sample ≥30 days after vaccination, EU-approved lab, ≥0.5 IU/ml, wait 3 months from sample date; exception if vaccinated, tested and documented in the EU before going to the unlisted country. Northern Ireland: same (Category 3 = unlisted).
GB.parasite_treatment: Dogs: tapeworm (Echinococcus) treatment by a vet not less than 24 hours and not more than 5 days before arrival in GB (not needed for dogs coming directly from Ireland, Finland, Malta, Northern Ireland or Norway). Northern Ireland: dogs 24–120 h before arrival; not required from the Republic of Ireland.
documents: GB from EU: EU pet passport, or GB AHC issued within previous 6 months, or GB pet health certificate (or GB pet passport issued before 1 Jan 2021).
GB from listed non-EU countries: GB pet health certificate (some listed territories, e.g. AD, IS, NO, CH, GI, also accept pet passport/AHC).
GB from unlisted countries: GB pet health certificate + rabies blood test result.
Pet travel declaration (non-commercial).
From Northern Ireland, Channel Islands, Isle of Man: no pet passport or health certificate needed for GB.
More than 5 pets (not for event), pet travelling >5 days apart from owner, or sale/rehoming: Balai commercial import rules.

NORTHERN IRELAND: from GB, UK-resident pets can use the NI Pet Travel Scheme (free NI Pet Travel Document + declaration not to travel on to EU); otherwise EU rules – EU pet passport or AHC (10 days from issue for entry); Part 2 listed countries (incl. GB not using NIPTS) and unlisted countries must enter via a Travellers' Point of Entry.
GB.quarantine: None if compliant. Non-compliant pets may be quarantined for up to 4 months (or refused entry if arriving by sea), at owner's expense.
GB.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU (listed countries): GB pet health certificate (or EU pet passport / AHC), dog tapeworm treatment 1–5 days before arrival, and a charter operator approved for the arrival airport. From scratch (EU/listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination at ≥ 12 weeks → 21 days → document → dog tapeworm 1–5 days before. Unlisted origin: at least 4 months (add blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3-month wait).
GB.restricted_breeds: Banned types (by appearance): Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, XL Bully. Cannot be brought into GB without a valid Certificate of Exemption. Northern Ireland has its own XL Bully rules.
GB.private_aviation: GREAT BRITAIN: pets normally must travel as cargo by air, EXCEPT on a chartered private plane, but only with operators on the APHA 'approved air routes – charter airlines' list for the specific arrival airport (pets carried in the cabin). Charter-listed GB airports include Biggin Hill, Farnborough, London Luton, London Stansted, London Gatwick, London Heathrow, London Oxford, Blackbushe, Birmingham, Manchester, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Bristol, Cambridge, Cardiff, Bournemouth, Southampton, Liverpool, Newcastle, Leeds Bradford, East Midlands, Lydd, Blackpool, Gloucestershire, Humberside, Sheffield, often via named pet-check providers. Northolt, Doncaster and Prestwick are NOT on the list (gov.uk list updated 9 Oct 2026). No approved route needed from Ireland or within the UK. Check the operator/airport pairing on the gov.uk list before each flight. NORTHERN IRELAND: air points of entry Belfast International, Belfast City, City of Derry; for air arrivals notify DAERA at least 10 days before travel (daeratradeimports@daera-ni.gov.uk).
GB.export: Great Britain to EU (and to Northern Ireland outside NIPTS): Animal Health Certificate (AHC) issued by an Official Veterinarian, new AHC for each trip, used within 10 days of issue for EU entry; then valid 6 months for onward EU travel and re-entry to GB (if rabies vaccination stays valid). EU pet passports issued in GB cannot be used by GB residents to enter the EU. Northern Ireland residents can use EU pet passports. Max 5 pets in a private vehicle unless for events.
GB.authority: Defra / Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) – Great Britain; DAERA – Northern Ireland

vaccinations: Rabies: within 12 months before arrival (Ministry of Agriculture instructions).
documents: Import permit (Pet Permit form): applicant name and country of residence, pet's age, sex, colour and breed, Grenada port or airport of landing, and expected arrival date. Fax it to (473) 440-4191 with the health certificate for approval and signature at least 2 weeks before arrival.
Health certificate issued by a veterinarian within 2 weeks before arrival. USDA APHIS says it must be APHIS-endorsed and issued no earlier than 3 weeks before arrival.
Rabies vaccination certificate.
GD.import_permit: Required: issued by the Veterinary Officer, Veterinary Department, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministerial Complex, Botanical Gardens, Tanteen, St George's. Tel. (473) 440-2708/3386/3078; agriculture@gov.gd; fax (473) 440-4191. It must be presented at the port of entry.
GD.timeline: Allow at least 14 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: have the vet issue the health certificate (and APHIS endorsement from the US) about 14 days before arrival, fax the permit and certificate to the Veterinary Department at least 14 days before arrival, then notify the Veterinary Officer of the port and ETA.
GD.private_aviation: The permit names the port or airport of landing and the expected arrival date. The Veterinary Officer must be notified of the port of entry and arrival time, so give the FBO airport (e.g. Maurice Bishop International, GND) and ETA.
GD.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Grenada: Veterinary Department (Veterinary Officer)

GE.microchip: Identification required on the model certificate (microchip)
vaccinations: Rabies: current; ≥21 days after primary vaccination (else Annex No. 2 for pets <12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12–16 weeks with <21 days unless accompanied by vaccinated mother)
GE.rabies_titer: Not required when travelling directly or only via Article 7-listed countries. If transiting a non-listed country: titer ≥3 months before export and >30 days after last rabies vaccination, OR owner signs Annex No. 3
GE.parasite_treatment: Dogs: internal (anthelmintic) and external (flea/tick) treatment before travel
documents: International health certificate for pet dogs, cats and ferrets (valid 10 days from issue; US: APHIS-endorsed)
Annex No. 5 non-commercial declaration (all pets)
Annex No. 2 / No. 3 where applicable
GE.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: rabies (21 days) → dog parasite treatments → certificate within 10 days of travel
GE.authority: National Food Agency of Georgia (Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture)

GF.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
GF.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
USDA APHIS (US origin) states a maximum of 3 animals per family, only one of them under 6 months old.
GF.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
GF.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
GF.restricted_breeds: French national dangerous-dog rules (categories 1 and 2) apply; confirm with DAAF Guyane before travel.
GF.private_aviation: Pets from outside the EU must pass documentary and identity checks at a travellers' point of entry. Confirm with DAAF Guyane (SALIM) before routing that the arrival airport can carry out the check for a private arrival.
GF.export: Leaving French Guiana: requirements depend on destination; travel to mainland EU is intra-EU (EU pet passport). Contact DAAF Guyane.
GF.authority: DAAF Guyane (French Ministry of Agriculture) under EU legislation

GG.microchip: Required for entry directly from the EU. From UK/Crown Dependencies, no Guernsey document check, but UK law requires dogs over 8 weeks to be microchipped and registered.
vaccinations: From UK/Crown Dependencies: none required
Directly from the EU: valid rabies vaccination
GG.rabies_titer: Only for pets coming from a country that is not 'listed' (entry directly via the EU route).
GG.parasite_treatment: Dogs entering directly from the EU: tapeworm treatment by a vet before arrival; confirm the timing with the States Veterinary Officer before travel. None from the UK/Crown Dependencies.
documents: From UK/Crown Dependencies: none (minimum age 8 weeks; operators may ask for a fitness-to-travel certificate)
Directly from the EU: valid pet passport (part 1 listed country), or AHC issued in GB/Channel Islands/Isle of Man (valid up to 4 months), or GB pet health certificate
Animal Import Notification to the Office of Environmental Health and Pollution Regulation at least 24 h before arrival (not required for pets with owners from UK/NI/Crown Dependencies)
GG.import_permit: Not needed for pets with owners from the UK/Crown Dependencies. EU arrivals: written pre-notification ≥24 h. Listed restricted breeds and dog/cat hybrids: specific import licence. Commercial movements/re-homing: separate rules.
GG.quarantine: Pets that do not follow the rules may be quarantined for up to 4 months or refused entry, at the owner's expense.
GG.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: there is no direct route, so the pet first enters Great Britain with a GB pet health certificate, then continues to Guernsey. From the EU, allow at least 2 days: pre-notify at least 24 h ahead and give dogs tapeworm treatment shortly before arrival. From the UK/Crown Dependencies: no preparation.
GG.restricted_breeds: Need a specific licence: Akbash Dog, American Bulldog, American Bully (incl. XL Bully), American Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Anatolian Shepherd, Bandog type, Boerboel Mastiff, Cane Corso, Caucasian Shepherd, Central Asian Shepherd, Czechoslovakian Wolfdog, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa/Tosa Inu, Kangal Shepherd, Moscow Guard Dog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Perro de Presa Canario, Perro de Presa Mallorquin, Pit Bull Terrier type, Šarplaninac, South Russian Ovcharka, Spanish Mastiff, Tornjak, Yugoslavian Shepherd Dog, Wolf hybrids F1–F4; also dog/cat hybrids.
GG.private_aviation: Pets may enter only via St Peter Port Harbour and Guernsey Airport. Pets may fly in with their owners on a private plane without approval only from the UK, Crown Dependencies, Ireland or Northern Ireland, with no foreign stop (other than Ireland/NI) en route. From elsewhere (e.g. the EU), entry must be via an approved carrier; at the airport this means handling through the Aiglle or ASG hangars (carriers can apply to the States Vets for approval). Direct arrival from outside the UK/EU is not provided for.
GG.export: Bailiwick residents can no longer use EU pet passports: an animal health certificate (AHC) is needed for each trip to the EU/Northern Ireland (valid 10 days for EU entry, 4 months onward travel in the EU, 4 months for re-entry to the Bailiwick). Dogs travelling to FI, IE, NI, NO or MT also need tapeworm treatment.
GG.authority: States of Guernsey – States Veterinary Officer (svo@gov.gg) / Office of Environmental Health and Pollution Regulation

GH.microchip: Not stated by VSD. APHIS certificate records microchip numbers if present; recommended for identification.
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, canine distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, Leptospira canicola and L. icterohaemorrhagiae, parainfluenza — each at least one month old and valid for 12 months before departure (VSD).
Cats: rabies, feline panleukopenia, calicivirus, rhinotracheitis (VSD).
UK-origin guidance (APHA NFG 3901, revised 12/2023) says rabies not more than 6 months before export — conflicts with VSD; follow the stricter if UK-origin.
GH.parasite_treatment: Dogs: negative tests required before permit — Brucella canis, Trypanosoma evansi, Babesia gibsoni, Dirofilaria immitis (microfilaria/Knott), Leishmania spp.; original lab reports, valid 31 days.
documents: Veterinary Import Permit (VSD, via ICUMS)
MOFA ministerial approval letter
Official veterinary health certificate signed by the exporting country's official vet (US: APHIS 'ghana-dog-cat' form, valid 30 days, digital VEHCS endorsement accepted)
Original lab reports (dogs) and vaccination records; health attestation report (cats)
Proof of fee payment
UK-origin: owner declaration of residency for prior 6 months
GH.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Chief Veterinary Officer (P.O. Box M161, Accra); Minister of MOFA approves; approval letter submitted on ICUMS to Director of VSD; processing about 72 working hours. UK guidance asks for notice at least 4 weeks before arrival. Airlines are told pets can only be carried on a signed permit. Contact: vsd@mofa.gov.gh, Import Desk +233 242649497.
GH.quarantine: Not stated for domestic dogs/cats; inspection and possible sampling at port of entry. (30-day quarantine listed for felids/wild cats.)
GH.timeline: Allow at least 28 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 1 month before departure): dog lab tests (reports valid 31 days) → apply to CVO/MOFA and VSD via ICUMS at least 4 weeks before arrival → official health certificate → inspection on arrival at KIA. From scratch, plan at least 8 weeks.
GH.authority: Veterinary Services Department (VSD), Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA), Ghana

GI.microchip: Microchip required; vaccination must follow microchipping.
vaccinations: Rabies: after microchipping, completed at least 21 days before entry (even if already up to date).
GI.rabies_titer: Not required from EU, UK or listed countries (e.g. CH, NO, AD, AU, CA, US, JP). From other third countries: titer ≥0.5 IU/ml, sample by authorised vet about 3 months before the move, tested at an EU-approved laboratory.
documents: EU-model pet passport from an authorised vet, or equivalent certificate.
From the UK: health certificate detailing up-to-date vaccinations is accepted instead of a pet passport.
GI.import_permit: No licence for dogs/cats (licensing applies to non-pet animals).
GI.quarantine: Not stated on the official page.
GI.timeline: At least 4 weeks (microchip → rabies → 21 days); about 4 months from unlisted countries (titer test ~3 months before move).
GI.restricted_breeds: Not stated on the official page.
GI.private_aviation: Not covered by the official page; contact the Environmental Agency (admin@eag.gi, +350 20070620) before a private arrival at Gibraltar airport. Note that onward travel into Spain (EU) is an EU entry from an Annex I territory (no titer or point-of-entry requirement).
GI.export: EU lists Gibraltar in Annex I (pets enter EU without titer or point-of-entry checks). For GB, Gibraltar-origin pets may use pet passport, AHC or GB pet health certificate per gov.uk.

GL.microchip: Not mentioned by the Greenland Representation's requirements (recommended, and an EU pet passport makes return to Denmark easier).
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and no more than 12 months old at the time of application/travel (an older multi-year vaccination does not qualify). Puppies/kittens under 3 months may be exempt if the mother was rabies-vaccinated before birth.
Dogs: a vaccination certificate is also required (Norden/Info Norden lists it separately; diseases not specified)
GL.parasite_treatment: Cats: owner's declaration of tapeworm treatment and 14 days of isolation before departure. Dogs: none specified.
documents: Application (letter or email, no set form)
Written permission to keep a dog/cat from the municipality of residence in Greenland (each municipality has its own dog and cat bylaws)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Veterinary health certificate no older than 14 days, plus owner's declaration (Danish Veterinary and Food Administration forms)
Female dogs: proof of sterilisation (Info Norden: dispensation possible for stays under 3 months). Cats: proof of sterilisation/neutering (Info Norden)
Cats: owner's declaration on tapeworm treatment and 14-day isolation
Import permit from the Greenland Representation, which must accompany the animal during the journey
GL.import_permit: Required: issued by the Greenland Representation in Copenhagen (Strandgade 91, DK-1401 Copenhagen K, +45 3283 3800, info@ghsdk.dk), after the municipality has approved the application. Apply well before departure. Without the permit the animal can be refused at departure.
GL.timeline: Get the municipality's written approval → rabies vaccination (≥30 days, ≤12 months old) → health certificate ≤14 days before travel → send everything to the Greenland Representation → permit issued. Processing times are not published, so allow several weeks.
GL.restricted_breeds: Fighting and 'muscle' dog breeds may not be imported (Info Norden). At sheep-farming sites only Border Collie, Kelpie and their crosses are allowed. No dogs at all in the sled-dog districts (north of 66°N on the west coast and all of East Greenland), except sled, police or service dogs by dispensation from the Greenland Veterinary and Food Authority.
GL.private_aviation: Dogs cannot be imported to the sled-dog districts, which include Kangerlussuaq, Ilulissat and all of East Greenland (e.g. Kulusuk/Constable Pynt). A private jet carrying a dog must therefore use an airport in south-west Greenland (Nuuk, Narsarsuaq) and the dog must remain there. The import permit must travel with the animal.
GL.export: EU lists Greenland as an Annex I territory for entry into the EU. An EU pet passport makes return to Denmark easier (Info Norden). The same permit procedure applies to re-import after a stay abroad.
GL.authority: Greenland Representation in Copenhagen (import permits); Veterinary and Food Authority of Greenland (Veterinær- og Fødevaremyndigheden i Grønland, dispensations); Greenland municipalities (permission to keep dogs/cats)

GM.microchip: UK-origin dogs: identified by microchip or tattoo number plus full description (UK NFG 6544, 2006).
vaccinations: UK-origin dogs: rabies, distemper, leptospirosis and parvovirus per manufacturer's instructions (UK EHC 6544, 2006). The guidance covers dogs only; confirm cat requirements with the Department of Livestock Services.
GM.parasite_treatment: Certificate states dog free of external parasites at exam within 72 hours of export.
documents: Import permit from Department of Livestock Services, Abuko
Official health certificate (UK EHC 6544: exam within 72 h, valid 10 days)
Vaccination records
GM.import_permit: Advised (UK guidance): Department of Livestock Services, Abuko, The Gambia.
GM.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip and vaccinations → request import permit from Department of Livestock Services → vet exam within 72 h and official certificate (valid 10 days).
GM.authority: Department of Livestock Services, Abuko (Ministry of Agriculture), The Gambia

GN.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip verified if listed; not explicitly mandatory.
vaccinations: Rabies: required per APHIS certificate (date, vaccine, batch and validity recorded); no minimum interval stated.
documents: For US-origin pets: APHIS 'guinea-pet' health certificate (English/French), valid 30 days, digital VEHCS endorsement accepted
Rabies vaccination certificate
GN.import_permit: Not mentioned by APHIS; confirm with Guinea's Direction Nationale des Services Vétérinaires.
GN.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination → confirm with Guinea's veterinary services whether a permit is needed → health certificate and endorsement within 30 days of travel.
GN.authority: Direction Nationale des Services Vétérinaires, Ministry of Livestock (Guinea)

vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory, with boosters every year (France Diplomatie). Treat a vaccine given more than 12 months ago as expired for Equatorial Guinea.

Vet health certificate issued shortly before travel (recommended; UK-origin EHC 4798 from 1999 required an exam within 48 hours of export and was valid 7 days)
GQ.quarantine: None stated. UK guidance (1999): on arrival the dog must be taken to the Veterinary Services (Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Stockfarming) for official registration and identification.
GQ.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: make sure the rabies vaccination is under 12 months old (booster at least 30 days before travel is prudent) → vet exam and health certificate a few days before departure → register the pet with Veterinary Services on arrival.
GQ.authority: Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Forests (Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Stockfarming per UK guidance)
