From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
GR.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Ministry of Rural Development and Food before travel.
GR.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories) must enter at a designated point. The published Greek list (hosted by the European Commission) names Athens International Airport, Thessaloniki airport and port, Piraeus port, several land borders, and the island points Rhodes, Kos, Kalymnos, Mytilene, Limnos (Myrina), Chios, Samos, Syros (Ermoupolis), Argostoli (port), Heraklion, Chania and Corfu. Mykonos, Santorini, Zakynthos and other popular private-jet islands are not listed. For a non-EU departure with a pet, clear first at Athens (or another listed airport) and continue domestically, or confirm in writing with the Ministry of Rural Development and Food before routing directly to an unlisted island. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no border check.
GR.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
GR.authority: Ministry of Rural Development and Food – Veterinary Directorates

GT.microchip: Not required in the MAGA requirements sheet.
vaccinations: Rabies: current, with validity shown and signed by the vet. Animals under 3 months are exempt. A 2021 government news item (AGN) cites vaccination at least 1 month and at most 1 year before travel. Confirm with MAGA.
GT.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming recorded on the health certificate. No timing window is published by MAGA.
documents: Health certificate stamped and signed by a practising veterinarian: pet details (name, age, sex, breed, colour), exam, healthy and free of infectious or parasitic disease signs, vaccinations with validity, and deworming. From the US, the bilingual 'US health certificate for dogs and cats to Guatemala', signed by an accredited vet and endorsed by USDA, may be used instead.
Rabies vaccination record.
Spanish translation of documents in other languages.
GT.import_permit: Not listed for dogs and cats in the MAGA requirements sheet.
GT.quarantine: Not listed. Inspection by SEPA/OIRSA staff at the point of entry (air, sea or land). A 2021 AGN item cites a fee of US$14 per pet.
GT.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: deworm, have the vet issue the certificate, get the USDA endorsement (from the US), then SEPA/OIRSA inspection on arrival.
GT.private_aviation: SEPA/OIRSA inspection applies at any point of entry, so arrange an inspector for the FBO arrival.
GT.export: If the pet leaves Guatemala more than 30 days after entry, a sanitary or international zoosanitary export certificate from MAGA is needed. Return to the US: Guatemala is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country, and a screwworm certificate is required.
GT.authority: Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería y Alimentación (MAGA): VISAR, Departamento de Protección y Sanidad Pecuaria (cuarentenaanimal@maga.gob.gt; tel. 1557 ext. 7426)

GU.microchip: Required, except for the full 120-day quarantine. It must be readable by an AVID universal scanner, and its number must appear on the FAVN result and health certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 2 lifetime vaccinations at least 30 days apart, using an inactivated (not modified-live) vaccine. The latest must be current at release, and must not be given after the FAVN draw.

Dogs: distemper, hepatitis/adenovirus-2, leptospirosis, parainfluenza, parvovirus, Bordetella. Cats: panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus. These must be given at least 10 days before departure (CQA, 2019 revision).
GU.rabies_titer: FAVN drawn at least 10 days after a rabies vaccination, within 12 months of arrival, at an approved lab (e.g. KSU), with results sent directly to DOAG. The 5-day/home-quarantine program needs at least 1.0 IU/ml. 'Calculated' quarantine needs at least 0.5 IU/ml, and the pet stays quarantined until 120 days after the lab received the sample.
GU.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment within 14 days of arrival, with products and dates on the health certificate.
documents: Guam entry permit application. The fee is US$65 per pet per the DOAG brochure (2024 rev.); CQA's 2019 page says US$60. Pay by money order or cashier's cheque to 'Treasurer of Guam'.

Current and prior rabies certificates, FAVN result, health certificate from an accredited vet within 10 days of arrival (English, specific breed, microchip number), flight itinerary, and CDC Dog Import Form receipt (dogs).
Confirmed quarantine-facility reservation where applicable, including layovers over 4 hours.
GU.import_permit: Required for every animal, including service animals. Arriving without one can bring a fine of up to US$1,000 and penalties for the transporter. DOAG recommends submitting documents 2–3 months before arrival (quarantine@doag.guam.gov; tel. 671-300-7964/66).
GU.quarantine: 120 days by default. 'Calculated' quarantine runs to 120 days from FAVN lab receipt. Pets from the mainland US with a FAVN of at least 1.0 IU/ml get 5 days or less, then home quarantine. Pets are exempt from quarantine after at least 120 days' residence in the British Isles, Australia, NZ, Japan or Hawaii, arriving direct.
GU.timeline: Allow at least 60 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (two lifetime shots) travelling from the US mainland: FAVN draw if not current, permit documents to DOAG 2–3 months ahead, quarantine reservation, parasite treatment within 14 days and the health certificate within 10 days of arrival. Other origins face the default 120-day quarantine unless exempt.
GU.restricted_breeds: Animals over 45 days pregnant are refused for quarantine, and permits are refused for pets under 5 months needing the 120-day quarantine. Ferrets and most other vertebrates are generally prohibited.
GU.private_aviation: A licensed quarantine facility collects non-exempt pets at the airport, where the quarantine vet examines them and verifies the microchip. Any flight change must be approved by DOAG and the facility. Exempt-area pets need clearance scheduled with Guam Customs & Quarantine (671-642-8071/2). Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries cannot enter the US via Guam or any other US territory (CDC).
GU.authority: Guam Department of Agriculture: Division of Animal Health / Animal Quarantine Program (163 Dairy Road, Mangilao), with Guam Customs and Quarantine Agency

GW.microchip: Identification required (France Diplomatie). A microchip is the practical standard.
vaccinations: Rabies: required (animal must be 'protected against rabies'). No timing rule published.
documents: International health certificate issued about one week before departure (France Diplomatie)
Rabies vaccination certificate
GW.import_permit: Confirm with the veterinary services before travel whether an import permit is needed.
GW.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 weeks before travel: check that identification and rabies vaccination are valid → international health certificate about 7 days before departure (with government endorsement if the origin country requires it).
GW.authority: Direção Geral de Pecuária / veterinary services, Ministry of Agriculture (Guinea-Bissau)

vaccinations: Vaccination status (records) assessed for the permit; specific vaccines/timing not published officially.
documents: Import permit application form
Health and vaccination records of the animal
Health certificate as specified on the permit
GY.import_permit: Required: issued by the Guyana Livestock Development Authority within about 3 working days, signed by a Senior/designated Veterinary Officer and CEO/Deputy CEO; decision considers species, origin disease status and vaccination.
GY.quarantine: Confirm with the Guyana Livestock Development Authority (GLDA) before travel.
GY.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: apply for GLDA import permit → meet permit conditions (health certificate, vaccinations) → inspection on arrival.
GY.authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Guyana Livestock Development Authority (GLDA), Veterinary Services

HK.microchip: ISO or AVID-compatible chip, all groups. Group IIIA: implanted before rabies vaccination and titer. If the chip is unreadable, the owner must supply a reader or the pet may be returned. Dogs aged 5 months or older must get a Hong Kong dog licence on arrival (HK-compliant chip implanted and rabies vaccination if needed).
vaccinations: Group I: no rabies vaccine in the import terms. Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus. Cats: panleucopaenia and cat flu. Given 14 days to 1 year before export.
Group II: rabies 30 days to 1 year before export (primary dose at age 90 days or older), plus the same core vaccines 14 days to 1 year before export.
Group IIIA: inactivated or recombinant rabies vaccine 30 days to 1 year before export (primary at age 90 days or older), plus full core vaccination 14 days to 1 year before.
Group IIIB: rabies certificate optional. Full core vaccination 14 days to 1 year before export.
HK.rabies_titer: Group IIIA only: FAVN or RFFIT result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an AFCD-recognised lab, sample taken 90 days to 1 year before export (at least 30 days after a primary vaccination). Not required for Groups I, II or IIIB.
documents: AFCD Special Permit (form AF240 + UN110 + ID copy). Fee HK$432 for the first animal and HK$102 for each additional animal. Normally issued in 5 working days, valid 6 months for one consignment.
Animal Health Certificate (VC-DC1 / VC-DC2 / VC-DC3A or equivalent), government-signed or endorsed. Dated within 14 days of export (Group IIIA: within 7 days).
Groups I and II: residence certificate. Group I: 180 days or since birth. Group II: 180 days or since birth, and no rabies within 10 km for 180 days.
Groups I and II: Airline Certificate / Captain's Affidavit (PC101) stating the pet stayed crated with no animal contact
Vaccination certificates; rabies antibody report (IIIA)
HK.import_permit: Yes. AFCD Special Permit is mandatory for all dogs and cats (also for transit). Do not book transport until it is issued. Notify AFCD at the airport at least 24 hours before arrival.
HK.quarantine: Groups I and II: normally none if fully compliant. Group IIIA: at least 30 days (Chinese Mainland since 3 June 2025). Group IIIB: at least 120 days at an AFCD Animal Management Centre or a licensed quarantine centre. Any group can be extended to at least 6 months for doubtful history or non-compliance. Government quarantine space has long waiting lists, so book early.
HK.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the continental USA or Western Europe (e.g. France, Germany: Group II) or the UK (Group I): AFCD Special Permit (about 5 working days), health certificate within 14 days of export, and notice to AFCD at least 24 h before arrival. From scratch (Group I/II), plan at least 6–8 weeks. Group IIIA: at least 4–5 months because of the 90-day titre window plus quarantine booking. Group IIIB (e.g. UAE): at least 120 days' quarantine; book quarantine space months ahead.
HK.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Pit Bull Terrier (incl. American Staffordshire Terrier), Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro and their crosses. Staffordshire Bull Terrier needs a statutory breed declaration. Bengal cats need proof of 5th generation or later domestic ancestry. Savannah cats are not covered by the standard permit terms. Age minimum: 60 days (Group I/IIIB), 5 months (Group II). No pets more than 4 weeks pregnant.
HK.private_aviation: AFCD permit terms (Group II) require pets arriving by air to be MANIFESTED CARGO; excess or hand baggage is not permitted, and the Captain's Affidavit must state the animal travelled the entire journey without leaving its crate. AFCD's import guide says arrivals 'by other routes' must contact AFCD well in advance for special arrangement. Confirm with AFCD (airport office +852 2182 1001, foii_airport@afcd.gov.hk) and the FBO before booking; notify at least 24 hours before arrival.
HK.export: Contact AFCD to arrange an export health certificate for the destination. Pets that leave Hong Kong need a new Special Permit to return and are subject to the same import rules on re-entry.
HK.authority: Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), Import & Export Division

HN.microchip: Not required. The certificate must give full identification of the pet.
vaccinations: Rabies (dogs and cats over 4 months): preferably given 30 days before the shipment date (art. 4.2.3).

The vaccination record must show the application date, expiry, vaccine type, brand and duration of protection (art. 4.2.1). If 1 or 2 non-rabies vaccines are missing, the owner signs an Acta de Compromiso to have them given within 5 days (art. 3.9).
HN.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming, preferably within 30 days before shipment, recorded with date, expiry, product type and brand (art. 4.2.2).
documents: Certificado Veterinario Internacional de Exportación from the exporting country's competent authority, following WOAH model content. It must state the consignor and consignee, full identification of the pet, and an exam at embarkation by a veterinarian (healthy, no tumours, wounds, disease signs or ectoparasites), with the vet's name and date (art. 4.1).
Current vaccination record (cartilla de vacunación) including deworming.
For guide or emotional-support animals: a supporting document from the prescribing medical professional (art. 3.11).
Per USDA APHIS, Honduras does not require APHIS endorsement of US health certificates.
HN.import_permit: Required only when 3 or more pets are imported (art. 3.15c). For 1–2 pets, no permit is needed.
HN.quarantine: None if compliant. A healthy pet arriving by air or sea without health documents may enter only after a licensed Honduran vet issues a 'Constancia de Cuarentena Fiduciaria' committing to supervise at least 10 days of quarantine and then report to SENASA (art. 3.7).
HN.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: deworm (within 30 days), get the vet exam and an official export certificate from the origin authority, then present the pet and documents at the SENASA quarantine post on arrival.
HN.private_aviation: The owner must present the pet and documents to the SENASA Agricultural Quarantine post at the customs office of entry (art. 3.1). Arrange an officer for the FBO arrival.
HN.export: To leave Honduras, report to Agricultural Quarantine with the SENASA-issued Veterinary Export Certificate (art. 3.12–3.13). Short stays of 20 days or less with vaccines still current are exempt from the export certificate (art. 3.15). Return to the US: Honduras is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country, and a screwworm certificate is required.
HN.authority: SENASA Honduras (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad e Inocuidad Agroalimentaria): Dirección Técnica de Cuarentena Agropecuaria / Salud Animal

HR.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
HR.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
HR.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.

Young animals: Croatia accepts non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks that are unvaccinated, or 12–16 weeks old and vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with the owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals, or accompanied by the vaccinated mother. Never allowed from outside the EU.
HR.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
HR.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
HR.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Ministry of Agriculture before travel.
HR.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Croatia and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Croatia's points of entry are published by the Ministry of Agriculture (veterinarstvo.hr); confirm with the Ministry before travel that the arrival airport is on the list. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
HR.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
HR.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries – Veterinary and Food Safety Directorate

HT.export: Return to the US: Haiti is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country. US-vaccinated dogs need the USDA-endorsed CDC certification before leaving the US; foreign-vaccinated dogs may arrive only at an airport with a CDC-registered animal care facility. A screwworm certificate is also needed (APHIS).
HT.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources Naturelles et du Développement Rural (MARNDR)

Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
HU.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
HU.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Hungary does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
HU.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
HU.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
HU.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the National Food Chain Safety Office (Nébih) before travel.
HU.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Hungary and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry: Budapest Liszt Ferenc (24 h), Debrecen and Sármellék (08:00–20:00). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
HU.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.

ID.microchip: Microchip number is recorded on the USDA certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: killed vaccine, pet at least 3 months old (USDA certificate for Indonesia).
Cats only: negative COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) PCR result before export (USDA Indonesia page).
ID.rabies_titer: FAVN result of 0.5 IU/ml or more (USDA certificate). The USDA certificate sets no sample timing or waiting period.
documents: USDA-endorsed 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to Indonesia'. It covers the microchip check, the exam (within 5 days of departure), 6 months' residence, no rabies in the area for 6 months, killed rabies vaccine, and FAVN of 0.5 IU/ml or more.
FAVN laboratory report
Cats: negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR report
Barantin import documents via PTK Online
ID.import_permit: Barantin (Indonesian Quarantine Agency) handles pet entry through its PTK Online system. Confirm the permit procedure with Barantin before travel.
ID.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: FAVN blood draw and result, Barantin pre-notification/permit, then the exam and USDA endorsement within 5 days of departure (and PCR for cats).
ID.private_aviation: Confirm the entry airport with Barantin in writing before routing. Bali (rabies-affected) has been closed to dogs, cats and monkeys under Governor Regulation 88/2008, so do not route pets to Denpasar (DPS) without written confirmation from Barantin and the Bali authorities.
ID.authority: Indonesian Quarantine Agency (Badan Karantina Indonesia, Barantin)

Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
