Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
IE.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: treatment against Echinococcus multilocularis (praziquantel or proven equivalent) given by a vet 24–120 hours before scheduled entry and recorded in the passport or certificate. Not required for dogs coming directly from Finland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland. Cats: none.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Non-EU arrivals (incl. GB): complete DAFM Advance Notice Portal (www.pettravel.gov.ie) before travel; for assistance dogs at least 24 h before departure.
Young animals: Ireland does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
IE.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
IE.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued). Dogs: tapeworm treatment 24–120 hours before arrival. From outside the EU (including Great Britain): complete the DAFM Advance Notice Portal before travel.
IE.restricted_breeds: Restricted breeds (and crosses) under Control of Dogs Regulations must be muzzled and on a strong lead (max 2 m) held by a person over 16 in public: American Pit Bull Terrier, English Bull Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Bull Mastiff, Dobermann, German Shepherd, Rhodesian Ridgeback, Rottweiler, Japanese Akita, Japanese Tosa, Bandog. XL Bully type: import, breeding, sale and rehoming banned since 1 Oct 2024; ownership requires a Certificate of Exemption since 1 Feb 2025.
IE.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Ireland and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Travellers' points of entry: Dublin Airport, Cork Airport and Shannon Airport (plus Dublin Port, Rosslare and Ringaskiddy). Advance notice via the DAFM Advance Notice Portal is required before bringing a pet from a non-EU country (including Great Britain); a compliance check is done on arrival. DAFM may facilitate the landing of pets by private aircraft where possible: contact the chosen point of entry in advance to ask whether a private arrival can be facilitated. Pets that do not comply must not disembark. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
IE.export: To EU: EU pet passport from your vet (no tapeworm needed to leave, but dogs returning need tapeworm treatment from a vet abroad 24-120 h before re-entry). To non-EU: destination requirements; certificate endorsed by the DAFM Regional Veterinary Office – contact the RVO at least 2 months before travel. Dublin Airport (DAA) does not accept pets outbound as excess baggage since 19 July 2021.
IE.authority: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM)

IL.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or tattoo), implanted before the rabies vaccine and blood test. If the chip is non-ISO, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccinated at 3 months or older, not more than 1 year and not less than 30 days before arrival. No 30-day wait if the pet has had more than one vaccination and is still within validity.
Pets born in rabies-free countries (Australia, New Zealand, Sweden, Cyprus, Singapore, Japan, UK, Ireland): if not vaccinated, dogs must be vaccinated within 5 days of arrival.
IL.rabies_titer: Required at 0.5 IU/ml or more from a WOAH- and/or EU-approved lab. The sample must be taken at least 30 days after vaccination, or 14 days if the pet has had multiple vaccinations and more than 30 days have passed since the first. Per the 2020 USDA guidance, the result stays valid for life while rabies vaccinations remain current. Exempt: pets born in the rabies-free countries listed above.
documents: Veterinary health certificate on the Israeli model, signed or endorsed by a government veterinarian of the origin country, issued within 10 days before departure (USDA: no more than 10 days before arrival)
Owner declaration that the pet has been in their possession for at least 90 days (Annex C)
Notification of Pet Arrival (Annex B) plus a copy of the certificate, sent to the port's Veterinary Services
Import permit only for more than 2 animals, unaccompanied or cargo shipments, or restricted breeds
IL.import_permit: Not required for up to 2 dogs or cats accompanying the owner on the same flight, provided the pet stays with the owner. Otherwise an import licence from the Director of Veterinary Services is required, and permit animals arrive as manifested cargo only (cargo inspections Sunday to Thursday, 06:00–24:00).
IL.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU: titre test on a currently vaccinated pet (no waiting period after the result), health certificate within 10 days of departure, and the Annex B notification at least 2 working days before departure. Pets born in listed rabies-free countries need about 10 days. From scratch, plan at least 2–3 months: microchip → rabies vaccination at 3 months or older → titre at least 30 days later → health certificate within 10 days of departure → Annex B notification → arrive at an approved port.
IL.restricted_breeds: Prohibited unless a case-by-case import permit is granted (vs-ie@moag.gov.il): American Staffordshire Terrier, Bull Terrier, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Pit Bull Terrier, Fila Brasileiro, Rottweiler, plus crosses and look-alikes. Minimum age 4 months on arrival (3 months for pets from rabies-free countries).
IL.private_aviation: Approved ports of entry: Ben Gurion Airport, Haifa, Ashdod and Eilat seaports. Private jets with pets must arrive at Ben Gurion (TLV); other airports (e.g. Ramon/ETM) are not approved ports of entry. A pet travelling with its owner on the same private flight fits the 'accompanied' route (2 pets or fewer, no permit). Send the pre-arrival notification to vs-airport@moag.gov.il at least 2 working days before departure. Shipments are not released until the Veterinary Services authorise them.
IL.export: Israel is on the CDC high-risk list and is not EU-listed: for return to the US or EU, prepare the US rabies certification / EU titer before leaving. Contact Israel's Veterinary Services for export certification.
IL.authority: Israeli Veterinary Services and Animal Health (IVSAH), Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security

IM.microchip: Required for routes via GB/EU per GB/EU rules; not required for GB-IoM movement.
vaccinations: Rabies: required for pets coming from the EU/other countries via GB under GB rules; not for GB-IoM movement.
IM.rabies_titer: Only as required by GB rules for unlisted countries (pets must clear GB first).
IM.parasite_treatment: Dogs from the EU: tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before arrival in the UK/IoM (per GB rules).
documents: GB/NI to IoM: none.
From Ireland direct: pre-notify DEFA.
EU via GB: GB entry documents (pet passport/AHC) and DEFRA-authorised pet transporter by prior arrangement with DEFA.
IM.import_permit: Direct import from non-EU countries prohibited.
IM.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU: the pet first enters Great Britain under GB rules (GB pet health certificate or EU pet passport/AHC, dog tapeworm treatment 1–5 days before), then moves freely to the Isle of Man. gov.im advises contacting your vet at least 4 months before travel.
IM.restricted_breeds: Prohibited from import: XL Bully, Pit Bull Terrier, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa (by appearance); UK exemption certificates are not valid on IoM.
IM.private_aviation: Animals cannot be landed directly from an EU country to IoM by private aircraft (exception: Republic of Ireland with DEFA pre-notification). Non-EU origin: prohibited directly; enter GB via a Border Control Post first. GB to IoM by private jet: free movement for non-banned dogs/cats.
IM.export: To EU and Northern Ireland: Animal Health Certificate from a vet for each journey (Official Veterinarian), microchip, rabies, dog tapeworm, entry via Travellers' Point of Entry; EU pet passports issued to GB/IoM residents no longer valid from 22 Apr 2026. To Dublin Port: advance notice at least 24 h before arrival.
IM.authority: Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture (DEFA), Isle of Man

IN.microchip: Required. Microchip number goes on the NOC application, and a vaccination and microchip certificate is submitted.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and not more than 1 year before travel (Indian consulate guidance). US 3-year vaccines older than 1 year must be repeated.

Other vaccinations per the AQCS veterinary health certificate (Annexure 1.1.1). The certificate covers freedom from rabies and distemper, and for dogs also Aujeszky's, leishmaniasis and leptospirosis.
documents: Advance NOC from AQCS through the ATITHI 2.0 portal (application Annexure 1.1). Fee Rs 1000. Airlines will not carry the pet without it.
Official veterinary health certificate in AQCS format (Annexure 1.1.1), signed by the exporting country's competent authority
Vaccination and microchip certificate / pet passport
Air ticket or airway bill, passport copy
Proof of eligibility: transfer of residence (2-year overseas stay, relocation proof), re-import (earlier AQCS export certificate), or a DGFT licence for short stays
Final NOC issued by AQCS at the port after inspection, then customs clearance
IN.import_permit: Advance NOC (AQCS) for all pets. A DGFT import licence for pets not on transfer of residence or re-import (short stays). More than 2 pets needs a DAHD sanitary import permit or DGFT licence.
IN.quarantine: None if the pet is healthy and documents are in order (Final NOC at the port). Pets failing the examination or showing disease signs: 15 days at the AQCS quarantine station at the owner's cost.
IN.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel (longer if a DGFT licence is needed, about 1 month): rabies vaccine ≥30 days before → health certificate and endorsement → ATITHI 2.0 application ≥7 working days before embarkation → Advance NOC (about 1 working day) → arrival inspection → Final NOC.
IN.private_aviation: The arrival airport must be one of the six notified ports (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad), and the AQCS officer must examine the pet on arrival. Coordinate with AQCS and customs at that airport.
IN.export: Apply to AQCS for the export veterinary health certificate / NOC (fee Rs 500). Keep the AQCS export certificate, because it is required for later re-import.
IN.authority: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (AQCS), Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD)

IQ.microchip: Listed if present (the certificate verifies microchips but does not explicitly require one).
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination with date, vaccine name and validity period recorded on the certificate.
documents: Veterinary health certificate (US version: issued by a licensed vet, valid 30 days after issuance, USDA endorsement not required)
IQ.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccination → health certificate within 30 days of travel. For Kurdistan Region (Erbil) arrivals, confirm the procedure with the regional authorities before travel.
IQ.authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Iraqi Veterinary Hospital / veterinary quarantine

IR.microchip: Microchip number to be stated on the international health certificate (Micor citing Tehran veterinary quarantine regulations)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination must be documented on the animal's health/vaccination card
documents: International health certificate issued by the official veterinary organisation of the origin country, with microchip number, issued no more than 7 days before presentation
Animal health identification card / vaccination record (especially rabies), original + copy
First page of the owner's passport, original + copy
Approval from the Iran Veterinary Organization (IVO)
IR.import_permit: IVO approval required (IATA Timatic). Procedure not published.
IR.timeline: Obtain IVO approval → health certificate within 7 days before arrival. Contact IVO 1–2 months ahead.
IR.export: Leaving Iran: domestic animals need a health certificate from the Iran Veterinary Organization (IATA Timatic).

IS.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip; number verified at every veterinary procedure for import.
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination; per MAST overview given at least 45-60 days before import (titer sample at earliest 30 days after vaccination).
Dogs: leptospirosis, distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, parvovirus, parainfluenza – last dose at least 14 days before import.
Cats: feline panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus – last dose at least 14 days before import.
Dogs from category 2 countries USA, Canada or Singapore: canine influenza vaccination also required (per certificate form).
IS.rabies_titer: Required from all origins: sample at least 30 days after vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml, EU-approved laboratory; valid while vaccination is kept up to date. For category 2 countries (e.g. Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Greenland, USA, Canada) travel only 90 days or more after sampling; animals qualify at earliest ~7 months old (category 1: ~4.5 months).
IS.parasite_treatment: Internal + external parasite treatment twice: 21-28 days and 5-10 days before import (products registered for roundworm, tapeworm, lice, fleas, ticks). Dogs: Angiostrongylus vasorum test within 30 days OR preventive imidacloprid+moxidectin treatment 5-10 days before.
documents: MAST import permit (apply at least 30 days before; valid 1 year; fee payable).
MAST certificate of health and origin (D1/D2 dogs, C1/C2 cats by country category), completed by authorised vet 5-10 days before import after health exam.
Lab reports: rabies titer; dogs Brucella canis (within 30 days) and Leishmania (intact dogs, within 30 days); cats FeLV and FIV (within 30 days).
Scanned certificate + lab results to petimport@mast.is no later than 5 days before arrival (later submission may be rejected).
Originals travel with the animal; customs declaration (VAT if owned < 12 months).
IS.import_permit: Yes – MAST import permit required before import. Animal must have lived in an approved category 1 or 2 country since birth or for the last 6 months. Category 1 includes all EU states except HU, PL, RO, SK (category 2), plus NO (excl. Svalbard), CH, LI, FO, GB, AU, JP, SG, AE.
IS.quarantine: Minimum 14 days at an approved quarantine station (Reykjanesbær/Hafnir or Mósel/Hella), booked in advance; admissions only in set 3-day windows about 3 weeks apart; arrival at Keflavík 06:00-17:00 on admission dates; no overnight stays at the airport. Service dogs may apply for home quarantine.
IS.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA (category 2): titer blood sample, then travel no earlier than 90 days after sampling; meanwhile apply for the MAST import permit (at least 30 days before), book a quarantine slot, complete the other vaccinations, tests within 30 days of arrival and parasite treatments at 21–28 and 5–10 days before arrival, and send the certificate to MAST at least 5 days before arrival. From category 1 countries (most of the EU), the 90-day wait does not apply. From scratch, plan at least 4–6 months (category 2: pet at least about 7 months old): import permit application (≥ 30 days before) → book quarantine slot → rabies vaccination → titer test ≥ 30 days later → other vaccinations → tests within 30 days of arrival → parasite treatments → health exam and certificate 5–10 days before → send to MAST ≥ 5 days before → fly to Keflavík on an admission date.
IS.restricted_breeds: Banned: wolf hybrids (10 generations); Pit Bull Terrier/Staffordshire Bull Terrier (service-dog form also lists American Staffordshire Terrier and American Bulldog), Fila Brasileiro, Tosa Inu, Dogo Argentino, Cane Corso, Presa Canario, Boerboel and crosses (5 generations), plus dogs MAST assesses as comparable. Pregnant/lactating animals not accepted.
IS.private_aviation: Pets may only arrive by air at Keflavík Airport (only approved entry port; ferry arrival not permitted). Animals must be in a hard IATA-compliant crate (soft carriers not allowed); flight number and arrival time are recorded on the certificate; arrival must match a quarantine admission date and 06:00-17:00 window. Confirm with MAST and the quarantine station before planning a private-jet arrival.
IS.export: Leaving Iceland: destination-country rules apply (EU treats Iceland as an Annex I listed territory – EU pet passport/certificate, no titer). Contact MAST for export certification.

IT.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
IT.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
IT.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Italy does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
IT.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
IT.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
IT.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Ministry of Health before travel.
IT.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Italy and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Italy's list (updated September 2026) designates about 40 airports, including Rome Fiumicino and Ciampino, Milan Malpensa and Linate, Bergamo, Venice, Treviso, Florence, Pisa, Bologna, Naples, Olbia, Cagliari, Alghero, Catania, Palermo, Genoa, Turin, Verona, Rimini, Bari, Brindisi, Lampedusa, Pantelleria, Salerno, Comiso, Cuneo, Brescia, Parma, Perugia, Pescara, Trieste and Bolzano, plus ports. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
IT.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
IT.authority: Ministry of Health – Directorate General for Animal Health

JE.microchip: Microchip (or qualifying tattoo) before rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: pet ≥12 weeks at vaccination, after microchipping, at least 21 days before travel.
JE.rabies_titer: Unlisted non-EU countries only: titer test passed, taken at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before travel into Jersey.
JE.parasite_treatment: Dogs: tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before scheduled arrival, recorded by the vet (product, date, time, stamp/signature). Exempt if travelling directly from Republic of Ireland, Malta, Finland or Norway.
documents: From EU: EU pet passport, or AHC issued in GB/Channel Islands/IoM within last 4 months (per gov.je), or GB pet health certificate, or GB pet passport issued before 1 Jan 2021.
Non-commercial declaration.
Australia (cats): Hendra certificate; Peninsular Malaysia: Nipah certificate.
JE.import_permit: Not for non-commercial pets; XL Bully type dogs need a licence to be imported/exported (since 24 Feb 2024, per gov.je).
JE.timeline: Allow at least 5 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the EU: valid EU pet passport, dog tapeworm treatment 24–120 hours before arrival, and a booking with an approved carrier and route (not a private aircraft). From the UK, Isle of Man or other Channel Islands: no preparation. From scratch (EU/listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks; unlisted origins at least 4 months.
JE.restricted_breeds: Certain dog types are illegal to bring into Jersey (see gov.je 'Dogs not allowed in Jersey'); dogs showing banned-breed characteristics may be seized. XL Bully types require a licence.
JE.private_aviation: Pets CANNOT enter Jersey on a private aircraft or private boat (except private boats from the Republic of Ireland). Only approved air/sea carriers and routes may be used.
JE.export: To EU: AHC (UK pet passports not accepted for EU entry). To UK/IoM/Guernsey: no official health requirements, though carriers may ask for documents.
JE.authority: Government of Jersey – Animal Health and Welfare (States Veterinary)

JM.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 microchip, implanted before rabies vaccination (otherwise revaccinate). The number must match on all documents.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine given at 90 days of age or older and valid at export. Primary vaccination 6–12 months before shipment, or a booster no more than 1 year before shipment (per the 2017 US guidelines).
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, hepatitis/adenovirus-2 and parainfluenza at least 2 weeks before export. Leptospira canicola vaccination up to date, or treatment within 30 days.
Cats: FHV-1, calicivirus, panleukopenia (FeLV for kittens) at least 2 weeks before export.
JM.rabies_titer: FAVN at an OIE/WOAH-approved lab, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. The pet is eligible for entry no less than 3 months and no more than 12 months after the successful blood draw. Send a copy to the Permit Unit at least 72 hours before export.
JM.parasite_treatment: Internal: fecal exam plus 2 broad-spectrum dewormings at least 14 days apart, the last within 7 days of export. External: 2 treatments, the first about 30 days before shipment and the second within 7 days of export. Dogs: heartworm prevention within 7 days.
documents: Approved Preliminary Application Form, then a Veterinary Import Permit (applied online via MOA trade system).
Official model veterinary health certificate for Jamaica, completed or endorsed by an official vet (USDA), every page signed and stamped. Exam within 7 days of export.

Dogs: negative heartworm antigen (6 months or older, within 30 days); Babesia, Lyme and Ehrlichia ELISA within 16 days; Leishmania within 45 days; Brucella canis within 45 days (intact dogs); coccidia test.
Animal Landing Notification Form; customs broker details.
JM.import_permit: Required, or the pet is refused entry. Submit the Preliminary Application at least 1 month before travel (6 months if requirements aren't yet met), to vsdpermits@moa.gov.jm. Don't start tests (except rabies and FAVN) before approval. Fee J$5,000, valid up to 3 months.
JM.quarantine: At least 14 days of post-entry quarantine at the National Quarantine Facility, Plumb Point, unless the inspector permits otherwise (e.g. service dogs or approved pet travel schemes at an approved place).
JM.timeline: Plan at least 6 months before travel: microchip and rabies, FAVN, then a 3-month wait, preliminary application, permit; tests and treatments in the final 45 days; 3 weeks' notice plus a 72-hour confirmation.
JM.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terrier, and wolf or other hybrids.
JM.private_aviation: Pets must arrive directly into Kingston (Norman Manley/Palisadoes) unless the Chief Veterinary Officer authorizes another port. Pets normally travel as manifested cargo and are checked at the freight terminal (service dogs excepted), so obtain CVO approval for a private-jet or FBO arrival in advance. Arrive Mon–Thu 8:30 am–5:00 pm or Fri 8:30 am–4:00 pm; other times, weekends and holidays attract extra fees.
JM.export: Leaving Jamaica: follow the Ministry's 'Protocol for export of dogs and cats'. A pet that leaves loses its Jamaican health status, so discuss re-entry with the Veterinary Officer before departure, as a new import permit is needed. Jamaica isn't a CDC high-risk country, but it is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs going to the US need a screwworm certificate.
JM.authority: Veterinary Services Division, Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Mining (Permit Unit)

JP.microchip: ISO 11784/11785, 15-digit. Must be implanted BEFORE the first rabies vaccination, or that vaccine is invalid. Chips starting '900 202' are currently not accepted. Other '900'-prefix chips may be duplicates, so tell AQS early.
vaccinations: Rabies (non-designated regions): at least 2 doses of inactivated or recombinant vaccine. RNA and live vaccines are not accepted. Dose 1 at 91 days of age or older and after the microchip. Dose 2 at least 30 days after dose 1 and within dose 1's validity. Immunity must still be valid on arrival (booster if needed).
Designated regions: no rabies vaccination required.
JP.rabies_titer: Non-designated regions: FAVN at an AQS-designated laboratory, blood drawn after the 2nd vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml. Valid 2 years from sampling. Arrival must be at least 180 days after the blood draw. Not required from designated regions.
documents: Advance notification to AQS at the port of entry (NACCS or email), at least 40 days before arrival, and the resulting approval

Health certificate Form AC (plus ATTACH if needed): completed by a vet and endorsed by the exporting country's government. Original in ink. E-certificates accepted only from USA, Brazil and Spain (designated regions: only Hawaii and Guam).
Clinical exam within 10 days before departure: no signs of rabies (dogs also no leptospirosis)

Designated regions: certificate of residence (since birth, 180+ days, or since import from Japan). Direct flight required, or an official crate seal plus a transport certificate if transiting a non-designated region.
JP.import_permit: No permit, but the 40-day advance notification and AQS approval are mandatory. Late notifications are generally refused. You cannot move the arrival date earlier or add or swap animals.
JP.quarantine: If fully compliant, released after arrival inspection, within about 12 hours. If not compliant (including certificate errors or an early arrival before the 180 days are up), detained at an AQS facility for up to 180 days at the owner's cost, or returned.
JP.timeline: Allow at least 190 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU, if it already has two valid rabies doses given after the microchip: FAVN blood draw, then a 180-day wait, with the AQS notification at least 40 days before arrival inside that window. With only one prior dose, allow about 220 days. From scratch (non-designated regions), plan at least 7–8 months: microchip → rabies #1 → rabies #2 (≥ 30 days later) → FAVN blood draw → wait 180 days → notify AQS ≥ 40 days before arrival → vet exam ≤ 10 days before departure → government endorsement → fly. Designated regions: at least 2 months (40-day notice plus certificates).
JP.private_aviation: AQS has no separate rule for private or business aircraft. Dogs may enter only through 19 designated ports. The 11 airports are New Chitose, Narita, Haneda, Chubu, Kansai, Osaka-Itami, Kobe, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, Kagoshima and Naha. Cats arriving elsewhere need advance contact with AQS. Coordinate the AQS arrival inspection with the airport's AQS office and the FBO in advance. Full requirements apply as for commercial flights.
JP.export: Apply to AQS in advance and present the pet for export inspection at the date and time AQS sets. AQS issues the export quarantine certificate after meeting the destination's rules. For pets that will return, AQS recommends doing Japan's import requirements (microchip, 2 rabies shots, FAVN) before departure so re-entry is possible without detention.
JP.authority: Animal Quarantine Service (AQS), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF)

KE.microchip: Required for pets not from a rabies-free country (permanent mark such as a microchip; number stated on the certificate) per the Ministry of Livestock Development permit conditions. The UK certificate also records the microchip number.
vaccinations: Rabies (pets not from a WOAH rabies-free country): inactivated or recombinant vaccine. A primary vaccination must be given at 3+ months of age and 6–12 months before shipment; a booster no more than 1 year before shipment (Ministry of Livestock Development permit conditions, published by the Kenya Embassy Spain, 2024).
The certificate must state vaccine name, manufacturer, batch number, date and the animal's age at vaccination (UK NFG 2913, revised 11/2023).
The US-origin APHIS certificate asks for rabies vaccination within 12 months before export; the permit conditions above are stricter, so follow the permit.
KE.rabies_titer: Required for pets not kept since birth or for 6 months in a WOAH rabies-free country: antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/ml, sample taken 3–24 months before shipment (permit conditions). Without it, Kenya may quarantine the pet for up to 6 months at the owner's cost.
KE.parasite_treatment: The certificate (dated within 48 hours of embarkation) must attest the pet is free of internal and external parasites. No specific treatment window is stated.
documents: Kenyan import permit (Director of Veterinary Services). Valid 30 days maximum, one consignment, and must accompany the animal.

International veterinary health certificate: exam within 48 hours of embarkation (permit conditions). The UK certificate requires an exam within 5 days and is valid 7 days. The US APHIS certificate is valid 30 days.
Rabies vaccination certificate and rabies titer lab report (non-rabies-free origins)

Certificate from the captain of the aircraft or ship stating the animal did not leave the aircraft between embarkation and Kenya and was isolated from other dogs and cats (permit conditions; UK master's declaration 2913MAS)
For the permit: formal request letter and copy of the owner's passport (Kenyan missions). Embassy pages say applications go through the Kenya TradeNet platform via accredited agents.
KE.import_permit: Required. Issued by the Director of Veterinary Services (State Department for Livestock Development), Kabete, Nairobi, or via Kenyan missions (UK: Kenya High Commission, London). Valid 30 days maximum, single consignment, must accompany the animal. Recent embassy pages say applications go through the Kenya TradeNet (KenTrade) platform via accredited agents. Mission fees vary (e.g. USD 50 per animal).
KE.quarantine: None if compliant. Pets not meeting the microchip, vaccination and titer conditions may be quarantined for up to 6 months at the owner's expense. UK guidance says the same may apply if the animal lands in an intermediate country other than Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden or Ireland without rabies vaccination in the past 6 months.
KE.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated from a non-rabies-free origin (the USA and most of the EU): titer blood sample at least 3 months before shipment → apply for the permit via KenTrade, an agent or a mission → vet exam within 48 hours of departure and government endorsement → captain's certificate on arrival. Primary-vaccinated pets need at least 6 months after vaccination.
KE.private_aviation: The Ministry of Livestock Development permit conditions say animals must travel as manifest cargo in the aircraft freight compartment, not as baggage or in passenger cabins. They also require a captain's certificate that the animal stayed on board and was isolated. The ports of entry are named on the permit (normally JKIA or Mombasa). Get written confirmation from DVS before booking a cabin-carriage private flight, and pre-arrange veterinary inspection at the arrival airport.
KE.authority: Directorate of Veterinary Services (State Department for Livestock Development), Kenya

KG.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules; recommended
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within last 12 months (multi-year vaccine OK while valid)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
documents: International pet passport with clinical exam mark ≤14 days (≤2 pets), or EAEU Form 15 certificate (APHIS: issued and endorsed within 5 days of travel)
KG.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal pets (EAEU); APHIS states up to 5 without special permission
KG.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → exam/certificate within 5 days
KG.authority: Veterinary authority of the Kyrgyz Republic, Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry (EAEU common veterinary requirements)

KN.microchip: ISO-compatible microchip (e.g. AVID, HomeAgain). The number must appear on the application, certificates, blood sample and titer result.
vaccinations: Rabies: current (1- or 3-year), approved monovalent killed vaccine, not given before 3 months of age. The health certificate lists the last 2 rabies vaccinations.
Core vaccines (dogs and cats) up to date.
KN.rabies_titer: From rabies-endemic countries: one FAVN of at least 0.5 IU/ml at a WOAH-approved lab (in the US: Kansas State or Auburn), drawn at least 30 days after the most recent rabies vaccine and at least 3 months before that vaccine expires. The lab emails results directly to Veterinary Services (St Kitts: skbvet12@gmail.com; Nevis: ambi.james@gmail.com). If it fails, give a booster and retest after 30 days.
KN.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment (broad-spectrum anthelmintic, product named) within 5 days of arrival, on a health certificate by an accredited vet.
documents: Import permit application (fee EC$55 or US$20 per animal, by international money order to 'Accountant General', or paid on arrival).
Government-issued international health certificate (USDA-endorsed) within 30 days of arrival. Required for first entry only.
Cats (first entry): FIV and FeLV negative within 30 days of arrival.
Rabies certificate; FAVN report with the microchip number.
KN.import_permit: Required. Apply to Veterinary Services, Department of Agriculture, La Guerite, Basseterre (tel. 869-465-2110). The application states the arrival date, flight and time.
KN.quarantine: 14 days of home confinement for new entrants, with 3 home visits; a completion certificate is issued at the end.
KN.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN at least 30 days later, permit application, health certificate within 30 days, parasite treatment within 5 days of arrival.
KN.private_aviation: Non-compliance can lead to deportation or euthanasia (APHIS). Confirm the arrival port and inspector availability for private flights with Veterinary Services.
KN.authority: Veterinary Services, Department of Agriculture, St. Kitts (and Nevis office)

KR.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 compliant, number on the health certificate. If missing, it can be implanted after arrival during quarantine at the owner's cost.
vaccinations: Rabies (age 90 days or older, non-rabies-free origin): current at arrival. The APQA FAQ indicates at least 30 days since vaccination and still within immunity. If under 30 days, the pet is held until 30 days have passed.
Pets under 90 days or from APQA-listed rabies-free countries: rabies vaccination not required, but chip and certificate still required.
KR.rabies_titer: Non-rabies-free origin, age 90 days or older: rabies-neutralising antibody result of at least 0.5 IU/ml, from an internationally approved lab or the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 24 months from blood draw. No waiting period after the result. If missing or under 0.5, the test is done in quarantine after arrival.
documents: Health certificate issued or endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority, stating the microchip number, birth date, rabies vaccination and titer result. For US origin, USDA-endorsed within 30 days of export.
Rabies vaccination certificate
Rabies antibody test report (where required)
Cats from Australia and dogs/cats from Malaysia: extra Hendra/Nipah freedom certificate, otherwise quarantine is extended 21 days (older official guidance)
KR.import_permit: No import permit for personal pets. Larger groups need advance notification to APQA and prior approval of a quarantine facility. Confirm the threshold with APQA.
KR.quarantine: None if compliant (arrival inspection only). Pets missing the chip or titer, with a mismatched chip, or with a titer under 0.5 IU/ml are held at the owner's expense until it is resolved, typically about 10 days, sometimes longer. A missing health certificate can mean return to origin.
KR.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: titer blood draw → lab result (usually 2–4 weeks) → Korea-specific health certificate (valid 30 days) and USDA/official endorsement. A titer result from the last 24 months can be reused.
KR.restricted_breeds: Korea has domestic 'dangerous dog' rules (e.g. Tosa, Pit Bull types, Rottweiler) that impose owner obligations after entry; confirm with APQA before travel.
KR.private_aviation: Arrange the APQA arrival inspection at the arrival airport (e.g. Incheon or Gimpo) in advance through the handler or FBO.
KR.export: APQA issues an export quarantine certificate after inspection at its airport or port office, based on the destination's requirements.
KR.authority: Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (APQA / QIA), Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

KW.microchip: Microchip number (10 to 15 digits) recorded on the PAAF certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: required for animals from rabies-infected countries, using a WOAH-compliant vaccine given per the manufacturer's recommendations.
Dogs: canine parvovirus, canine distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (icterohaemorrhagiae and canicola).
Cats: feline panleukopenia, feline rhinotracheitis, feline calicivirus.
KW.rabies_titer: Required: an antibody titration of at least 0.5 IU/ml per the WOAH Manual, with the sample taken not less than 3 months and not more than 12 months before entry into Kuwait.
KW.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment within 14 days before export.
documents: PAAF veterinary health certificate for dogs, cats and ferrets, endorsed by the official government veterinarian of the exporting country. For US pets, confirm with APHIS whether APHIS endorsement is needed.
Rabies vaccination and titre details on the certificate
Clinical examination statement (free of infectious disease, fit to travel)
KW.import_permit: Not stated on the official PAAF certificate or the USDA page. Confirm with PAAF (info@paaf.gov.kw) before travel whether an import permit is needed.
KW.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated. Animals are held in the Kuwait quarantine station if certificate conditions are not met.
KW.timeline: Plan at least 4 months before travel: microchip → rabies vaccination → titre blood draw (at least 3 months before entry) → core vaccines → parasite treatment within 14 days → PAAF-format health certificate → arrival.
KW.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including any mixes): Pit Bulls, American Pit Bull Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bully, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bulldog, Mastiff, Tibetan Mastiff, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Neapolitan Mastiff, Dogue de Bordeaux, Perro de Presa Canario/Dogo Canario, Cane Corso, Tosa, Bully Kutta/Alangu, Bullmastiff, Boerboel, Rottweiler, Central Asian Shepherd (Alabai), Wolf Dog, Caucasian Shepherd (Ovcharka), Doberman Pinscher, Anatolian Shepherd/Kangal.
KW.authority: Public Authority of Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAF)

KY.microchip: ISO-compliant 15-digit chip if implanted on or after 1 Mar 2019 (older chips: 10 or more characters), implanted BEFORE rabies vaccination, otherwise revaccinate. Scanned at each step.
vaccinations: Rabies: first vaccine at 12 weeks or older; booster 9–12 months later; 2- or 3-year intervals only after that second dose. Valid for entry 30 days after vaccination for 'no-risk' origins.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus mandatory. Cats: panleukopenia, herpesvirus and calicivirus mandatory.
KY.rabies_titer: Required unless coming from a 'no rabies-risk' territory (official 2026 list includes e.g. UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Italy, Spain incl. Balearics/Canaries, Portugal, Greece, Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, Monaco, Austria, Bahamas, Barbados, Bermuda, Jamaica, Hawaii, Australia, New Zealand). Blood drawn at least 30 days after vaccination at a Cayman-approved lab, result at least 0.5 IU/ml with the microchip number, repeated every 12 months. Earliest entry after the draw: 2 months for 'low risk' origins (US mainland, Canada, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Latvia, Estonia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Grenada, Trinidad & Tobago) and 3 months for 'high risk' origins (e.g. Mexico, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, Poland, Romania, Lithuania, Serbia, Montenegro, Greenland). Pets must have resided in the origin country for at least 3 months. Animals arriving by sea are treated as high risk.
KY.parasite_treatment: On the day of the vet examination, within 14 days before travel: praziquantel at 5 mg/kg (tapeworm) plus a systemic tick product with residual action. Shampoos, collars and flea-only products are not accepted.
documents: Cayman Islands import permit (single entry, valid 14 days from the health-certificate exam date).

Veterinary health certificate completed within 14 days of travel. The new US VEHCS certificate (Sep 2026) includes a USDA endorsement block, and APHIS indicates endorsement applies from 1 Oct 2026; previously Cayman needed no APHIS endorsement for dogs and cats. Original presented on arrival.
FAVN report, rabies and routine vaccination certificates, signed breed declaration and full-body colour photo (dogs).
KY.import_permit: Required. Email the application and documents to ci.agriculturevs@gov.ky, up to 6 months before travel. Fee CI$50 / US$61 per animal. Decision within 3 working days of a complete file. The health certificate must be added within 14 days before entry.
KY.quarantine: None available. Non-compliant animals are refused and returned immediately, or destroyed, at the importer's expense. Dogs staying more than 30 days must be licensed.
KY.timeline: Allow at least 65 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the US mainland: FAVN blood draw on a currently vaccinated pet, then a 2-month wait before entry. From 'no-risk' EU countries or the UK, allow about 3 weeks (permit, vet exam and treatments within 14 days). From scratch, plan at least 3 months (US mainland) or 4 months (higher-risk origins): microchip → rabies vaccine → FAVN at least 30 days later → wait 2–3 months; apply for the permit; vet exam and treatments within 14 days of travel; give 48 hours' notice of arrival. From the UAE there is no direct route (the flight must route via a non-Asian country).
KY.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Pit Bull Terrier types, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, and dogs bred for fighting. Crosses are allowed only if spayed or neutered (proof required) and not pregnant. Purebreds not originating in Cayman are never admitted.
KY.private_aviation: Travel by the most direct route. No animal may be imported DIRECTLY from Asia (including the UAE/Dubai), Africa, or Central or South America. Transit through such a country requires a government-sealed crate. Give 48 hours' notice of arrival time and flight. DoA office hours are Mon–Fri 8:30 am–5:00 pm, so confirm inspector availability for FBO arrivals outside these hours.
KY.export: Leaving Cayman: DoA export permit/health certificate (fee CI$20 / US$25 per animal). Pets abroad for less than 14 days can re-enter on the export certificate plus a tick and tapeworm treatment.
KY.authority: Cayman Islands Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Services

KZ.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules; recommended
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within last 12 months (multi-year vaccine OK while valid)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
documents: International pet passport with clinical exam mark ≤14 days (≤2 pets), or EAEU Form 15 certificate (APHIS: issued and endorsed within 5 days of travel)
KZ.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal pets (EAEU); APHIS states up to 5 without special permission
KZ.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → exam/certificate within 5 days
KZ.authority: Committee of Veterinary Control and Supervision, Ministry of Agriculture of Kazakhstan (EAEU common veterinary requirements)

LA.microchip: Required in practice: the certificate records a microchip (or ID) number scanned before export that matches the vaccination certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated or recombinant vaccine acceptable to DLF, at least 1 month before export, and a valid primary or booster course.
Dogs: distemper, infectious hepatitis and parvovirus, at least 14 days before export.
Cats: calicivirus, rhinotracheitis and panleukopenia, at least 14 days before export.
LA.rabies_titer: Rabies neutralising antibody of at least 0.5 IU/ml by a WOAH-prescribed test. Blood drawn at least 30 days after rabies vaccination and within 6 months before export. The test report must go with the certificate. The form says 'whenever require'; if the rabies conditions are not met, the pet is vaccinated on arrival and confined separately at home for at least 21 days.
LA.parasite_treatment: External (fleas and ticks) and internal (nematodes and cestodes) treatment between 2 and 7 days before export, with product, active ingredient and date recorded.
documents: DLF import licence (number shown on the certificate)

Animal Health Certificate for the Import of Dogs and Cats into Lao PDR (Form 3). Sections I–III by a government-approved or official vet; Section IV endorsed by the official government vet of the exporting country (USDA for the US). Valid 7 days.
Rabies vaccination certificate and titer report
Present the import licence and health certificate to customs and quarantine officers at the port of entry
LA.import_permit: Yes. A valid Department of Livestock and Fisheries (DLF) import licence must be obtained before shipment. Confirm the processing time and fees with the DLF before travel.
LA.quarantine: No routine quarantine for compliant pets. Pets not meeting the rabies conditions are vaccinated on arrival and confined at home for at least 21 days.
LA.timeline: Allow at least 30 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (vaccine at least 30 days old): titer blood draw → result → DLF licence → parasite treatments, exam and official endorsement within 7 days of export.
LA.restricted_breeds: Banned with crosses: Pit Bull types (incl. American Pit Bull Terrier), American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Tosa, Akita, Dogo Argentino, Boerboel, Fila Brasileiro, Perro de Presa Canario. Also Bengal and Savannah cat crosses of 4th generation and below. Pregnant females are not accepted.
LA.private_aviation: Clearance needs customs and quarantine officers at the port of entry, so arrange this in advance for a GA arrival (e.g. Vientiane Wattay).
LA.authority: Department of Livestock and Fisheries (DLF), Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Lao PDR

vaccinations: Rabies: valid rabies vaccination certificate required (timing not specified).
documents: Valid health certificate issued in the country of origin
Valid rabies vaccination certificate
Customs declaration of the pet on arrival
LB.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccination → health certificate from the origin country → declare at customs. Confirm with the Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture.

LC.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 microchip, or a non-ISO chip with the owner providing a reader. Implanted before rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated and adjuvanted, at 12 weeks or older, after the microchip, no less than 30 days before export.
Dogs: distemper, leptospirosis, hepatitis/adenovirus, parainfluenza and parvovirus at least 14 days before export.
Cats: FeLV, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia and pneumonitis at least 14 days before export.
LC.rabies_titer: FAVN at an approved lab, blood drawn at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. Entry not allowed until 3 months after the successful blood draw. The original lab report accompanies the certificate.
LC.parasite_treatment: Endoparasites (including tapeworm) and ectoparasites (including ticks) treated 'not less than 14 days prior to export' (US certificate wording); confirm the exact window with VLSD before travel. The pet must be free of external parasites at the exam.
documents: Veterinary Import Permit.
US health certificate for Saint Lucia (exam within 14 days before export), endorsed by APHIS (digital via VEHCS).
Dogs: negative heartworm and Lyme tests sampled within 14 days before export.
LC.import_permit: Required. Email the application form and documents to vlsdsec.agriculture@govt.lc. Processing about 2 business days; fee EC$45 paid on entry. Animals without a permit are refused or euthanized.
LC.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN at least 30 days later, then a 3-month wait. In parallel, get the permit; vaccines and tests within 14 days; give 3 days' notice.
LC.restricted_breeds: Saint Lucia publishes a separate 'Prohibited Dog Breeds' list (govt.lc). Check it before booking.
LC.private_aviation: Notify the Veterinary and Livestock Services Division of the port of entry (Hewanorra UVF or George F.L. Charles SLU), date, time and flight at least 3 days before arrival. Office hours are 8:00 am–4:30 pm. Pets must travel directly and not contact other animals on the flight.
LC.authority: Veterinary and Livestock Services Division, Ministry of Agriculture, Saint Lucia

LI.microchip: Microchip required before rabies vaccination (Swiss/EU rules).
vaccinations: Rabies: pet ≥ 12 weeks at vaccination, valid 21 days after primary vaccination (Swiss/EU rules).
LI.rabies_titer: Per Swiss rules: required only from rabies high-risk third countries.
documents: EU/Swiss pet passport (from EU/CH), or health certificate meeting Swiss rules from third countries.
LI.import_permit: See Switzerland (FSVO authorisation for direct flights from high-risk countries).
LI.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA, as for Switzerland (health certificate endorsed by the exporting authority); from the EU, pet passport only. From scratch, plan at least 4 weeks from EU/low-risk origins and 4+ months from high-risk origins.
LI.private_aviation: No airport in Liechtenstein. Private jets land in Switzerland or Austria, and the landing country's entry rules apply. Direct flights from third countries with pets may land in Switzerland only at Zurich, Basel or Geneva (the Swiss pet entry airports), so regional airports such as St. Gallen-Altenrhein are not available for these arrivals; from the EU/Schengen area no veterinary border check applies.
LI.export: The EU treats Liechtenstein as an Annex I listed territory (pet passport, no titer). Contact the Office of Food Safety and Veterinary Affairs (ALKVW) for export certification.
LI.authority: Office of Food Safety and Veterinary Affairs (ALKVW), Liechtenstein; Swiss FSVO for border controls

LK.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip, number shown on all documents (vaccination records, blood test reports).
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, canine distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis, leptospirosis (fully vaccinated and up to date)
Cats: rabies, feline calicivirus, feline herpesvirus 1, feline panleukopenia
Under 3 months old: the dam must be fully vaccinated. Minimum import age 1.5 months.
LK.parasite_treatment: Ecto- and endoparasite treatment within 14 days before departure, certified in writing by a registered vet.
documents: DAPH import permit (application via the DAPH Google form; enquiries vraanim@gmail.com)
Vaccination records (submitted with the permit application)
Dogs only: negative leishmaniasis (PCR/ELISA/IFAT), heartworm antigen and microfilaria tests within 1 month of departure. Waived for a disease the exporting country is officially free of.
International Veterinary Health Certificate from the exporting country's competent authority, issued within 10 days before export
LK.import_permit: Yes. Import permit from the Director General, Department of Animal Production and Health (Animal Diseases Act No. 59 of 1992).
LK.quarantine: The permit application commits the importer to quarantine and inspection or sampling by DAPH; confirm the length with DAPH before travel.
LK.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: vaccinations up to date → apply for the DAPH permit → dog blood tests within 1 month of departure → parasite treatment within 14 days → health certificate within 10 days → fly.
LK.private_aviation: Arrange the DAPH quarantine officer inspection at the arrival airport in advance.
LK.authority: Department of Animal Production and Health (DAPH)

vaccinations: Vaccination history required with the permit application (official gov.ls listing); confirm the specific vaccines and timing with the Ministry.
documents: Completed import application form
Laboratory reports for the animal(s)
Vaccination history
Proof of registered establishment (as listed generically for live animals)
Transit/removal permit if passing through a third country
Veterinary health certificate from origin country (expected; not detailed on official page)
LS.import_permit: Required: 'Import and export of live animals' service, Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition. Fee for pets M200; processing 3–5 days; apply online via gov.ls e-service. Contact: +266 8001 0100, contact.centre@gov.ls.
LS.timeline: Allow at least 14 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: confirm the health requirements with the Ministry → gather vaccination history and lab reports → apply for the permit (3–5 days) → origin health certificate shortly before departure.
LS.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition (Lesotho) – livestock/veterinary services

LT.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
LT.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
LT.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.

documents: Morocco health certificate (French/English model, Dec 2017, for US origin): pet kept in rabies-free premises since birth or for the last 6 months. Issued within 5 business days and APHIS-endorsed within 3 calendar days of travel. Valid 3 days after endorsement.
Addendum: clinical exam within 24 hours of departure
MA.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: health certificate within 5 business days, APHIS ink endorsement within 3 days of travel, and a final clinical exam within 24 hours of departure. MA.private_aviation: Arrange the ONSSA veterinary inspection at the arrival airport with the handler before the flight.
MA.export: Morocco is on the CDC high-risk list and is not EU-listed: for return to the US, get the CDC/USDA rabies certification before leaving the US; for return to the EU, do the rabies titer before leaving the EU to avoid the 3-month wait.
MA.authority: ONSSA (Office National de Sécurité Sanitaire des Produits Alimentaires)

MC.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted), as required by France on arrival. Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid.

documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.
MC.quarantine: None if EU requirements are met.
MC.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA via Nice: EU animal health certificate within 10 days before arrival. From the EU: pet passport only. From scratch, plan at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origins and 4+ months from unlisted origins.
MC.restricted_breeds: Arrival through France means France's category 1 dog import ban applies.
MC.private_aviation: No airport in Monaco (heliport only). Private jets land at Nice Côte d'Azur (LFMN), where French/EU entry rules apply: pets from third countries are presented to French Customs on arrival (customs check pets at points open to international passenger traffic; Nice is also a live-animal border control post). MC.export: Leaving: the EU treats Monaco as an Annex I listed territory (pet passport or certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement).
MC.authority: Direction de l'Action Sanitaire (Monaco); at entry, the French authorities at Nice

vaccinations: Rabies: given by an official veterinarian of the origin country, pet ≥12 weeks old at vaccination, at least 21 days before departure (IATA Timatic / Moldovan Customs). Under 3 months only if the dam was vaccinated (APHIS certificate)
Compliance with other preventive sanitary measures for diseases other than rabies (Customs)
MD.rabies_titer: Required per Moldovan Customs (IATA Timatic) and ANSA: ≥0.5 IU/ml, sample ≥30 days after the last rabies vaccination, result recorded in the pet passport. The older ANSA guide also says the test must be ≤24 months old and done ≥3 months before shipment; confirm with ANSA whether the 3-month wait still applies under Government Decision 660/2022. Not mentioned on the APHIS US-origin certificate.
documents: Veterinary health certificate from the origin country (APHIS US version: valid 30 days after issuance)
Pet passport with microchip, rabies vaccination and titer result
Declaration of the animal at the border to the border veterinary inspector
MD.timeline: Microchip → rabies vaccination (≥21 days before departure) → titer blood sample ≥30 days after vaccination → (possibly 3-month wait per older ANSA guide) → health certificate. Allow up to 4 months to be safe if no prior titer.

MD.export: ANSA 'Certificate for non-commercial movement of pets', applied for online (servicii.gov.md / EVO app) at least 3–5 days before travel. Requires ID, pet passport (microchip, rabies details), official titer lab report and clinical exam record; issued on paper by the ANSA territorial office.
MD.authority: National Food Safety Agency of Moldova (ANSA); Customs Service of Moldova

Owner declaration that the movement is non-commercial (pet accompanies the owner within 5 days)

ME.private_aviation: Certificate names the Montenegro border inspection post of entry; arrange entry at an airport with veterinary border control (e.g. Podgorica/Tivat)
ME.authority: Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Affairs of Montenegro

vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export; vaccination certificate (completed by the vaccinating vet) attached to health certificate (UK official guidance)

MM.microchip: Not specified in the LBVD regulation. The certificate must fully identify each animal; a microchip is advised.
vaccinations: Rabies: official approved vaccine at least 21 days before departure, unless the origin region has been rabies-free for at least 12 months (LBVD regulation; UK certificate 7961EHC).

documents: Myanmar import licence issued by a Government authority
Health certificate signed by an authorised official vet, describing each animal (UK version valid 7 days from signature)
Vaccination records
MM.import_permit: Yes. A valid Myanmar import licence must accompany the consignment (LBVD regulation). The pet application route and processing time are not published.

MM.private_aviation: The 30-day post-arrival quarantine at approved premises still applies.
MM.authority: Livestock Breeding and Veterinary Department (LBVD), Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Irrigation

vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (vaccine name, batch and validity recorded)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to Mongolia (US: accredited vet + APHIS endorsement; valid 30 days after issuance)
MN.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: microchip → rabies vaccination (current) → certificate within 30 days of arrival
