MO.microchip: Required. Implanted before the rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: 30 days to 1 year before export (per APHIS summary of IAM requirements).
MO.rabies_titer: At least 0.5 IU/ml at an IAM-approved lab. Sample taken at least 30 days after the latest rabies vaccine and at least 3 months before export (US-origin rules per APHIS; rabies-free origins may differ, so confirm with IAM).
documents: IAM import licence. The importer named on the health certificate must match the licence holder.
Official health certificate for Macao (one per animal), valid 10 days from issue, government-endorsed
Rabies vaccination record and titer lab report
MO.import_permit: Yes. Import licence from the Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM) before travel.
MO.quarantine: From 12 June 2026: none for compliant pets from rabies-affected countries that pass IAM vet inspection on arrival (previously a mandatory 30 days). Non-compliant pets: expect quarantine or refusal.
MO.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 months before travel: microchip → rabies vaccine → titer sample ≥30 days later → wait ≥3 months → IAM licence → health certificate within 10 days of travel → government endorsement.
MO.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Tibetan Mastiff, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa and their crosses. Bengal cats need 5th generation or later domestic ancestry stated on the certificate. Domestic dogs and cats only.
MO.private_aviation: Arrange the IAM vet inspection at Macau International Airport in advance. Note: Macao is in Hong Kong's Group IIIA, so onward travel to Hong Kong means at least 30 days of HK quarantine.
MO.export: IAM issues export health certificates. Contact IAM in advance and meet the destination's requirements.
MO.authority: Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM / Instituto para os Assuntos Municipais)

MP.microchip: Required. The health certificate must show the microchip number and implant date. International dogs: ISO-compatible microchip.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least two lifetime vaccinations (primary + booster), each with a formal vet-signed certificate. Do not re-vaccinate after the FAVN draw before import.
Dogs: DHPP (DHLPP), Leptospirosis and Bordetella current.
Cats: FVRCP current.
MP.rabies_titer: FAVN required unless the pet comes from a recognised rabies-free area (Hawaii, Guam, Japan). Use a CDC-approved lab, with the result greater than 1.0 IU/mL and destination listed as 'CNMI'. Draw blood at least 30 days after the second rabies vaccine. Non-US, non-rabies-free origin: at least 120 days from the FAVN draw before entry.
MP.parasite_treatment: Internal (helminths, heartworm) and external (fleas, ticks) treatment within 14 days of arrival, with date, product and method on the health certificate.
documents: CNMI Entry Permit Application (Cat/Dog) with travel itinerary (note foreign layovers). Fee USD 50 per sterilised animal, USD 500 per unsterilised animal. Permit valid 60 days.
Two rabies certificates, FAVN report, and core vaccine records
Health certificate within 10 days of travel (microchip, rabies details, parasite treatment)
Rabies-free origins: vet certificate of origin showing at least 6 months' residence
International dogs: CDC Dog Import Form; dog at least 6 months old
MP.import_permit: Yes. CNMI Entry Permit from DLNR Division of Agriculture (cnmianimalhealth@gmail.com, +1 670 256-3319/20). Submit documents at least 14 days before arrival; they need at least 1 week to prepare the permit.
MP.quarantine: None for compliant pets from the USA or rabies-free areas. Cats from international high-risk rabies areas: quarantine on Guam before arriving in the CNMI, plus re-vaccination with a US-made rabies vaccine. Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries cannot enter the US through a US territory (CDC).
MP.timeline: Allow at least 120 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (two lifetime shots) travelling from the EU or another non-US, non-rabies-free origin: FAVN blood draw, then at least 120 days before entry. From the USA, about 4–6 weeks (FAVN result in 2–4 weeks; permit documents at least 14 days before arrival).
MP.private_aviation: The entry permit and itinerary (including foreign layovers) must be approved in advance. US CDC dog-import rules apply to dogs coming from abroad: foreign-vaccinated dogs that were in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months cannot enter the US through a US territory, because no territory has a CDC-registered animal care facility.
MP.export: For export to New Zealand, MPI treats the Northern Mariana Islands as Category 3 (same as the US mainland), per USDA.
MP.authority: CNMI Department of Lands and Natural Resources, Division of Agriculture (Animal Health)

MQ.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
MQ.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
MQ.import_permit: Not required under EU non-commercial rules. Ask DAAF Martinique before travel whether a prior declaration is needed.
MQ.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
MQ.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
MQ.restricted_breeds: French dangerous-dog law: category 1 attack-type dogs cannot be imported. Confirm with DAAF Martinique before travel.
MQ.private_aviation: Pets from outside the EU must pass documentary and identity checks at a travellers' point of entry. Confirm with DAAF Martinique before routing that the arrival airport can carry out the check for a private arrival.
MQ.authority: DAAF Martinique / French Ministry of Agriculture

vaccinations: Not specified in the regulations; confirm vaccination requirements with the Department of Agriculture before travel.
documents: Import permit from the Inspector (reg. 3).

For quarantine exemption (origins in the First Schedule only): a certificate from the exporting country's appropriate authority (reg. 20) stating good health and no rabies among unquarantined animals there for the past 6 months. The pet must not have contacted uncertified dogs or cats in transit (reg. 8(2)).
MS.import_permit: Required (reg. 3), from the Inspector, Department of Agriculture, Brades (tel. 664-491-2075).
MS.quarantine: Per the regulations, at least 6 months in an approved quarantine depot, at the consignee's cost and risk, for dogs and cats not imported directly from a First Schedule country: GB, Northern Ireland, Ireland, Jamaica, St Kitts-Nevis, Barbados or Anguilla (reg. 8). The USA, Canada and the EU mainland are not on that list. Confirm current practice with the Department of Agriculture before travel.
MS.timeline: Plan at least 3 months before travel: contact the Department of Agriculture for written permit conditions and to confirm quarantine treatment for your origin.
MS.private_aviation: Animals may land only at a customs port or airport, unless the Inspector gives a written permit. Each animal must be inspected before landing, and no animal may be landed without the Inspector's prior written permission (reg. 4). Aircraft carrying animals are subject to inspection and disinfection (reg. 5). A direct flight from a First Schedule country is required to avoid quarantine.
MS.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Lands, Housing & the Environment: Department of Agriculture (Veterinary Services / Inspector)

MT.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
MT.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
MT.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: treatment against Echinococcus multilocularis (praziquantel or proven equivalent) given by a vet 24–120 hours before scheduled entry and recorded in the passport or certificate. Not required for dogs coming directly from Finland, Ireland, Norway or Northern Ireland. Cats: none.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Mandatory 'Pets Arrival Notification' (pre-notification of arrival) to the VRD for commercial and non-commercial movements; entry is denied if not done. Submit it well ahead of travel.
Young animals: Malta does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
MT.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
MT.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued). Dogs: tapeworm treatment 24–120 hours before arrival. Send the Pets Arrival Notification to the VRD before travel.
MT.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Veterinary Regulation Directorate (VRD) before travel.
MT.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Malta and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Air point of entry: Malta International Airport (Luqa). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
MT.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.

MU.microchip: Required (checked on the certificate). ISO 11784/11785 recommended.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine per manufacturer. US-origin certificate: at least 3 months of age, more than 2 months before export for a primary vaccination, or at least 30 days for a booster.
Dogs: distemper, infectious hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus – up to date, given more than 14 days before dispatch
Cats: feline enteritis (panleukopenia), rhinotracheitis, calicivirus – between 14 days and 12 months before export
MU.rabies_titer: Required for dogs and cats: FAVN or RFFIT ≥0.5 IU/ml at a lab approved by the exporting country, or a WOAH reference lab. Blood sample at least 4 weeks after vaccination. Travel no earlier than 3 months after sampling, and the test must be no more than 12 months before shipment. The lab must also send results directly to the Mauritius veterinary services. Alternative: 6 months in an approved quarantine station in the exporting country.
MU.parasite_treatment: External parasite treatment, within coverage at export (US certificate).
documents: Import permit (number and date shown on the veterinary certificate)
International veterinary certificate from the exporting country's competent authority (US: APHIS-endorsed)
Rabies vaccination certificate and RNATT lab report (endorsed by the competent authority)
Dogs: Ehrlichia canis (IFAT, negative at 1:40) within 45 days before departure, and a negative Brucella canis test
Sterilisation certificate (except breeding animals with a pedigree and breeder's licence)
Application form per animal, motivation letter to the Principal Veterinary Officer, owner's passport copy, copy of the vaccination book
MU.import_permit: Mandatory: 'No animal should be embarked for Mauritius without an import permit.' Apply to petimport@govmu.org at least 3 months before departure. Issue depends on quarantine kennel availability. Fees: Rs 500 import fee plus Rs 500 veterinary clearance per animal.
MU.quarantine: Minimum 5 days at the government Quarantine Facility, Réduit, at the owner's cost (kennel Rs 15/day; the owner supplies food and litter).
MU.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: titer test (at least 4 weeks after vaccination), then travel no earlier than 3 months after sampling; apply for the permit at least 3 months ahead; dog Ehrlichia/Brucella tests within 45 days; health certificate and endorsement; email flight details at least 4 days before arrival. From scratch, plan at least 4–5 months.
MU.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (Animal Welfare Act 2013, 4th Schedule): American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Terrier, Blue Nose Pit Bull, Red Nose Pit Bull, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Boerboel. Other 'dangerous' breeds (e.g. Rottweiler, Doberman, Cane Corso, Bull Mastiff, Rhodesian Ridgeback, Alaskan Malamute, Kangal) are allowed only if pure-bred.
MU.private_aviation: Official guidelines: all pets must arrive as manifest CARGO ONLY (not in cabin, not as excess luggage), with a local customs broker present at the airport. Without a broker, the animal may be sent back at the owner's cost. A private flight must manifest the pet as cargo and arrange the broker and veterinary pickup at SSR International.
MU.authority: Ministry of Agro-Industry, Food Security, Blue Economy and Fisheries – Division of Veterinary Services / Livestock and Veterinary Division (petimport@govmu.org)

vaccinations: Cats: rabies 30 days to 12 months before export
Cats: feline calicivirus, feline viral rhinotracheitis, feline panleukopenia
MV.parasite_treatment: Cats: internal and external parasite treatment between 1 month and 14 days before expected arrival (UK DEFRA export guidance).
documents: Import permit (application with pet passport or vaccination card showing rabies, FCV, FVR and FPL vaccinations)
Official export health certificate. The UK version requires a clinical exam within 72 hours of export.
On arrival: commercial invoice approved by Maldives Customs, plus airway bill or bill of lading, given to the port quarantine officer
MV.import_permit: Yes for cats (per UK DEFRA export guidance for Maldives). Dogs: import prohibited.
MV.timeline: Allow at least 21 days for a cat already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (rabies 30 days to 12 months before export): import permit from the Ministry of Fisheries and Agriculture, internal and external parasite treatment between 30 and 14 days before arrival, then the clinical exam and official health certificate shortly before export. From scratch, allow at least 6 weeks: vaccinations (rabies at least 30 days before export) → import permit → parasite treatment → exam and certificate. Dogs cannot enter.
MV.restricted_breeds: All dogs prohibited ('import of dogs and dangerous animals is strictly prohibited', Velana airport customs guide).
MV.private_aviation: The dog ban applies to all arrivals, including private jets and resort transfers. Cats are cleared by the quarantine officer at the arrival port (Velana International Airport), who needs a commercial invoice approved by Maldives Customs plus the airway bill or bill of lading.
MV.authority: Ministry of Fisheries and Agriculture (live animal imports); Maldives Customs Service

vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export; certificate must show animal description, vaccine batch number and production laboratory (UK official guidance). Cats must be vaccinated before export; dogs from rabies-free Great Britain may instead be vaccinated on arrival.
documents: Import permit from Chief Veterinary Officer, Malawi
Official export health certificate (exam ≤14 days before export, UK model)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Owner declaration of no contact with a rabid animal in the 6 months before export
MW.import_permit: Required for all animals under the Animal (Import) Rules (Control and Diseases of Animals Act). Written permit from the Chief Veterinary Officer, P O Box 30372, Lilongwe; the CVO may attach conditions.
MW.timeline: Allow at least 14 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 30 days before export): apply to the CVO for the permit → official health certificate within 14 days of export → notify the CVO of the arrival date and flight. From scratch, plan at least 6 weeks.
MW.private_aviation: UK guidance: for air travel, report the arrival date and flight number to the Chief Veterinary Officer, Lilongwe, before departure. For a private flight, give the aircraft registration/flight details and arrival airport.
MW.authority: Chief Veterinary Officer, Department of Animal Health and Livestock Development (Malawi)

vaccinations: No rabies certificate is listed as an entry requirement on the APHIS Mexico page (Sep 2026). Carry rabies proof anyway for the US return.
MX.parasite_treatment: The pet must be free of ectoparasites at the SENASICA inspection. If ticks are found, they are sampled and removed, and the pet is held at OISA until cleared, at the importer's cost. Other ectoparasites must be treated by a vet of the owner's choice.
documents: Dogs: NWS (New World screwworm) Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs, issued no more than 5 days before entry by a USDA-accredited vet. No APHIS endorsement. Don't list cats on the dog form, or the form becomes invalid.
Cats: none.
Carriers must be clean; bedding, toys and food beyond the arrival day are removed.
MX.import_permit: Not required for personal pets. A 'Pet Program – Frequent Traveler' registration is available.
MX.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a dog already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: a USDA-accredited vet signs the NWS inspection certificate within 5 days before entry (no endorsement). Cats from the US need no certificate. Arrange the Mexican-side screwworm certificate for the return to the US. From other origins, confirm the conditions with SENASICA before travel.
MX.private_aviation: SENASICA/OISA inspects at the point of entry, so confirm with the FBO and handler that SENASICA inspection is available at the arrival airport and time.
MX.export: Returning or entering the US from Mexico: dogs need a screwworm-freedom certificate. For Mexico, a SENASICA-authorized clinical vet (MVRA directory) may sign it, with inspection within 5 days. Mexico is NOT on the CDC high-risk list, so the CDC Dog Import Form route applies.
MX.authority: SENASICA (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad, Inocuidad y Calidad Agroalimentaria), OISA inspection offices

MY.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip required under the DVS regulations for non-scheduled countries.
vaccinations: Rabies (non-scheduled countries): approved vaccine before export. The DVS pet portal says at least 30 days before entry.
Other core vaccines given within 12 months before export, as recommended by a licensed vet.
MY.rabies_titer: Not required in the DVS regulations for Peninsular Malaysia (antibody levels may be tested at random during quarantine). Sabah and Sarawak may apply different rules; confirm with their veterinary services before travel.
documents: MAQIS import permit (ePermit)
Pet passport or certificate with full description and identification

Veterinary health certificate from the exporting country's government veterinary authority: examination within 7 days before export, no rabies in the country for the previous 6 months, not imported into the country within the previous 6 months
Rabies vaccination certificate
Scheduled countries: Malaysian veterinary certificate and airline captain's affidavit (per DVS portal)
MY.import_permit: Yes: MAQIS import permit. Restricted dog breeds also need prior written approval from the MAQIS Director General.
MY.quarantine: Non-scheduled countries: at least 7 days in quarantine, which can be extended up to 6 months case by case. Scheduled countries: no quarantine per the DVS pet portal. Scheduled list (DVS notice of 11 Dec 2025): United Kingdom, Eire, Northern Ireland, New Zealand, Japan, Sweden, Brunei, Singapore, Greece, Luxembourg, Czech Republic, Malta, Slovenia, Estonia, Bahrain, Austria, Belgium, Germany, Portugal, Montenegro, Bulgaria, Lithuania. Australia appeared in the older list but is not in the Dec 2025 list; confirm with DVS.
MY.timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies vaccine (30+ days before entry), MAQIS permit, government-endorsed health certificate within 7 days of export, then quarantine on arrival unless from a scheduled country.
MY.restricted_breeds: Banned dogs: Akita, American Bulldog, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Neapolitan Mastiff, Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier). Restricted dogs (need MAQIS approval, pedigree, premises inspection, personal pet or security use only): Bull Mastiff, Bull Terrier, Doberman, German/Belgian/East European Shepherd, Perro de Presa Canario, Rottweiler. Minimum age 3 months.
MY.private_aviation: The DVS regulation says pets must be carried by aircraft or other transport directly to the prescribed landing place or any other airport in Malaysia. No rule specific to private aircraft was found. Confirm the arrival airport and the quarantine officer's attendance with MAQIS/DVS.
MY.authority: Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services (MAQIS). Sabah and Sarawak: state veterinary departments (Sarawak: dvs@sarawak.gov.my)

vaccinations: Rabies: within 12 months before export (US/APHIS); UK guidance: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export. US certificate allows pups/kittens under 3 months travelling with the mother's rabies certificate.
Routine vaccinations/treatments up to date (APHIS certificate)
MZ.parasite_treatment: For US-origin pets (APHIS): animal must be free of external parasites at exam; routine treatments up to date.
documents: Official export health certificate: For US-origin pets (APHIS): USDA-endorsed certificate (April 2024 form) valid 30 days after issuance, attesting no rabies on premises of origin for 12 months; UK: OV exam within 48 h of export
Rabies vaccination certificate
Authorization from National Director of Livestock Development for dangerous breeds (where allowed)
MZ.import_permit: General pet import permit not stated in APHIS/UK guidance. Dangerous-breed dogs need prior authorization from the National Director of Livestock Development (MADER).
MZ.timeline: Allow at least 28 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 30 days before export): check the breed list and apply for any authorisation → official health certificate (US: within 30 days; UK: exam within 48 h). Listed breeds need longer.
MZ.restricted_breeds: April 2024 MADER measure (announced via the state news agency AIM) bans import of potentially dangerous breeds and crosses, including Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Pit Bull, Rottweiler, American Staffordshire Terrier, Tosa Inu, Saint Bernard, Bull Terrier, Akita Inu, Doberman, Kangal, Bullmastiff, and others. Exceptions need authorization, e.g. assistance dogs, security dogs, and sterilized companion dogs over 2 years. Dogs must be at least 3 months old and registered within 10 days of entry. Sterilization is required.
MZ.authority: National Directorate of Livestock Development (DNDP), Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MADER)

NA.microchip: Not mandated by the DVS portal (microchip if transiting a country requiring it). The US dog certificate uses tag/tattoo/description.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and no more than 12 months before travel. Under 3 months old: the dam's vaccination is accepted and the pet must be vaccinated at 3 months in Namibia.
Full vaccination status expected (EU/USA origin)
NA.parasite_treatment: US-origin dogs: heartworm treatment (ivermectin, milbemycin, moxidectin, selamectin or DEC) from the negative test until export, and continued for 6 months after arrival. The owner must bring 6 months of supply because it is not easily available in Namibia.
documents: Namibian veterinary import permit (number on the health certificate)
Health certificate from the exporting country's state vet (US: USDA-endorsed, exam within 10 days of export)
Rabies vaccination record
Dogs (US/EU and other origins): negative tests within 30 days of export for Brucella canis, Babesia gibsoni, Dirofilaria immitis, Leishmania (and T. evansi for non-US origins)
Landing permit from the Namibian state vet (send the endorsed permit, pet passport and lab results before travel)
From South Africa: inter-territorial movement permit from the local state vet. From Botswana: Veterinary Certificate of Identity, Rabies Vaccination and Movement Permit.
NA.import_permit: Required except for South Africa-origin pets (residence of 3+ months). Apply via Vet.Permits@mawlr.gov.na. Fee N$150 (or €50 at a Namibian mission). Processed within a maximum of 3 working days. Valid 4 months, single use.
NA.quarantine: None for EU/USA, South Africa and SADC origins. 30-day quarantine on arrival for pets from other countries (per the Namibia Trade Portal).
NA.timeline: Allow at least 42 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 30 days ahead): apply for the permit (up to 3 days) → courier the permit to the exporting vet → dog blood tests within 30 days of export → health certificate and endorsement within 10 days → email documents to obtain the landing permit before departure.
NA.private_aviation: The permit names the state veterinary office responsible for inspection. Arrange inspection at the arrival airport (normally Hosea Kutako International) in advance.
NA.export: To South Africa: inter-territorial movement permit from a local state vet. To Botswana: health certificate from a state vet. To the EU: state vet health certificate, microchip and rabies titer. Others: destination permit required.
NA.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform – Directorate of Veterinary Services (Vet.Permits@mawlr.gov.na)

vaccinations: Per the country-specific health certificate.
NC.rabies_titer: Required per the certificate where applicable, and only at a DAVAR-listed approved laboratory (results from other labs are refused). Timing not stated on the page.
documents: Import permit (form I.DPA.NC.15/12)
Country-specific dog or cat health certificate
Rabies antibody result from an approved lab where required
Brachycephalic breeds: vet fitness-to-fly certificate and larger crate
NC.import_permit: Yes, for every dog or cat import (SIVAP/DAVAR).
NC.quarantine: 10 days in public quarantine (CPZP, Païta) on arrival for domestic carnivores from France or Pacific countries. For other origins the length is set by species and origin; confirm with SIVAP (+687 41 25 36, davar.sivap-qsa@gouv.nc).
NC.timeline: Plan at least several months (6+ months for non-listed countries routed via France): permit, certificate, approved-lab titre where required, book quarantine.
NC.restricted_breeds: No breed ban was listed on the DAVAR page. A brachycephalic breed list carries flight-welfare conditions.
NC.authority: DAVAR – Service d'inspection vétérinaire, alimentaire et phytosanitaire (SIVAP)

NG.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): all pets must be microchipped. UK certificate accepts a microchip or permanent tattoo.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine, record not more than 1 year old (FMARD); For US-origin pets (APHIS): within one year of departure with a US-approved inactivated vaccine; UK certificate: given at ≥3 months of age, ≤1 year before export
NG.rabies_titer: FMARD lists a laboratory rabies serology result as a permit document. UK certificate requires ≥0.5 IU/ml, with the sample taken 3–24 months before export. The APHIS US certificate does not include a titer statement. Plan for a titer regardless of origin.
documents: Import permit (DVPCS/FMARD)
Health certificate signed by attending vet and endorsed by official vet of exporting country (US: APHIS ink endorsement, valid 30 days; UK: exam ≤48 h, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination record
Rabies serology lab result
Proof of permit fee payment
NG.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Director, Dept of Veterinary and Pest Control Services, FMARD Abuja (hard copy or vpcs@fmard.gov.ng) using the application form with travel date. Fee: N5,000 per dog/cat via Remita. Processing ~3 working days; permit valid 14 days from issue.
NG.quarantine: NAQS inspects imported dogs/cats at the port of entry and verifies the permit and veterinary certificate. Under the NAQS SOP, live animals may be held for quarantine observation (NAQS or owner's facility); animals suspected of disease may be held 2–3 weeks; non-compliant or illegal animals may be seized or destroyed.
NG.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated when a titer is needed (UK model: sample at least 3 months before export): titer → apply for the FMARD permit (about 3 days, valid 14 days) → endorsed health certificate → notify NAQS of the permit and arrival date.
NG.private_aviation: NAQS SOP: notify NAQS of the import permit details and arrival date, and declare the animal for NAQS inspection at the point of entry. Arrange NAQS presence at the arrival airport/FBO in advance.
NG.authority: Federal Department of Veterinary and Pest Control Services (FMARD) and Nigeria Agricultural Quarantine Service (NAQS)

vaccinations: Rabies: animals over 4 months, no more than 365 days before embarkation. The rabies certificate accompanies the health documents.
NI.parasite_treatment: Treated for endo- and ectoparasites with approved products (no timing stated).
documents: Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, exam within 2 weeks of departure, endorsed by APHIS (original ink signature and embossing). Present the original plus 1 photocopy on arrival. No notary or consular stamp.
Rabies certificate.
NI.import_permit: Not required for personal pets (commercial shipments need one). A quarantine permit is obtained at the port of entry on arrival.
NI.timeline: Plan at least 3 weeks before travel: rabies within 365 days, vet exam within 2 weeks, USDA ink endorsement (allow mail time).
NI.export: Return to the US: Nicaragua is NOT on the CDC high-risk list (Apr 2026). It is screwworm-affected, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
NI.authority: Instituto de Protección y Sanidad Agropecuaria (IPSA)

NL.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
NL.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
NL.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: The Netherlands does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
NL.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
NL.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
NL.restricted_breeds: Ear cropping and tail docking are banned in the Netherlands; owners of cropped or docked dogs should confirm any conditions with the NVWA before travel.
NL.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by the Netherlands and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry (NVWA list v1.0.4): Amsterdam Schiphol, Eindhoven, Rotterdam, Maastricht-Aachen, Groningen Eelde and Lelystad. Passengers with animals must use the red 'something to declare' exit. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
NL.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.
NL.authority: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA)

NO.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
NO.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
NO.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: Echinococcus treatment (praziquantel) by a vet 24–120 h before arrival, recorded in the passport, even for day trips (e.g. from Sweden). Exempt: dogs arriving directly from Finland, Ireland, Malta or Northern Ireland. Frequent travellers may use a regular treatment schedule at intervals of at most 28 days (at least two treatments before entry). Cats: none.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Norway does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
NO.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
NO.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued). Dogs: tapeworm treatment 24–120 hours before arrival.
NO.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (incl. any cross): Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Fila Brasileiro, Tosa Inu, Dogo Argentino, Czechoslovakian Wolfdog. Customs says import requires a special police permit applied for in advance; police may order euthanasia or removal of non-compliant dogs.
NO.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU/EEA (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Norway and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Pets from outside the EU/EEA may only arrive via Oslo Airport Gardermoen (or the Storskog road crossing, Kirkenes). Always use the customs red channel (by air, even from Sweden). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
NO.export: Leaving Norway for EU/EEA: EU pet passport (EEA rules). To third countries: destination rules; contact Mattilsynet.
NO.authority: Norwegian Food Safety Authority (Mattilsynet); Norwegian Customs

NP.microchip: Not stated in the official embassy guidance; confirm with the Animal Quarantine Office before travel.
vaccinations: Rabies: rabies vaccination card required (Embassy of Nepal, London); confirm the timing with the Animal Quarantine Office.
documents: International health certificate issued within 10 days of arrival in Nepal (valid 30 days; a new one can be issued in Nepal)
Rabies vaccination card/certificate
Owner's passport copy and flight details (sent to the Animal Quarantine Office in advance)
Optional: Embassy recommendation letter (UK embassy, GBP 40, not mandatory)
NP.import_permit: No separate import permit in the embassy guidance for personal pets. Advance notification to the Animal Quarantine Office, Tribhuvan International Airport (ktmquarantine@gmail.com) 72 hours before arrival.
NP.quarantine: Inspection at the airport animal quarantine checkpoint, then customs clearance. No fixed quarantine is described for compliant pets.
NP.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: health certificate within 10 days of arrival → email the Animal Quarantine Office 72 hours before arrival.
NP.private_aviation: Kathmandu (TIA) Animal Quarantine Office handles arrivals; give 72 hours' notice.
NP.authority: Animal Quarantine Office, Tribhuvan International Airport (Department of Livestock Services, Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development)

NZ.microchip: Microchip required. 2026 IHS official identity check: Category 2, microchip scanned by an official vet at least 6 months before shipment. Category 3, official scan before the RNATT sample (twice, the first at least 6 months before shipment, if the RNATT is taken 3-6 months before shipment). Mandatory for all arrivals from 1 April 2027; the ID check process started on 1 October 2026.
vaccinations: Rabies (Category 3): at 12 weeks of age or older, continuously valid; a primary vaccination must be at least 6 months before shipment (2026 IHS).
Category 2: no rabies vaccination required.
NZ.rabies_titer: Category 3 (2026 IHS): RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/mL on a sample taken 3-12 months before shipment.
NZ.parasite_treatment: 2026 IHS: internal parasites treated twice (first within 30 days of shipment and at least 14 days before the second; second within 5 days of shipment). Ticks and fleas: last treatment within 16 days of shipment with continuous protection. Dogs also need heartworm prevention and tests for Babesia gibsoni, Brucella canis (entire dogs), Leishmania, leptospirosis and others, per the IHS.
documents: MPI import permit
Signed quarantine booking form
Category 3: rabies vaccination records, RNATT result, Category 3 Rabies Certification Form
Pre-export ID check notified by the exporting competent authority directly to MPI
Government-endorsed veterinary certificate; vet exam within 2 days of shipment
NZ.import_permit: Required for Category 2 and 3 (including assistance dogs). Book quarantine first and attach the booking form. Allow 30 working days after all documents are received (USDA says at least 20 business days).
NZ.quarantine: At least 10 days at an MPI-approved transitional facility for Category 2/3, longer if extra tests or treatments are needed or the period ends outside business hours. Book before the permit application. Australia and assistance dogs are exempt.
NZ.timeline: Allow at least 200 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU (Category 3 under the 2026 IHS): official ID check at least 6 months before shipment, RNATT 3–12 months before shipment, quarantine booking, then the import permit (allow 30 working days). Category 2 (rabies-free) origins: plan 6–7 months (6-month ID check). Australia: weeks.
NZ.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Brazilian Fila, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, American Pit Bull Terrier type. Hybrid dogs and cats (other than Bengal) need EPA approval. Approximate minimum ages: 8 weeks (Category 1), 12 weeks (Category 2), 9 months (Category 3). Not more than 42 days pregnant.
NZ.private_aviation: The 2026 IHS says a cat or dog arriving by air must travel as manifested cargo (only assistance dogs excepted) and may arrive only at Auckland or Christchurch. Category 2 crates must carry a government seal. A pet in the cabin of a private jet does not meet the IHS, so arrange manifested-cargo status with MPI before booking.
NZ.export: NZ-origin pets need the MPI veterinary (export) certificate or Animal Welfare Export Certificate (AWEC), which is also required to re-enter as an 'NZ-origin' pet. Short trips of 30 days or less use a simplified short-stay certificate.
NZ.authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), Biosecurity New Zealand

OM.microchip: Electronic microchip number must be shown on the immunisation record.
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccinated after 12 weeks of age. No more than 12 months may have passed since vaccination at the time of import.
Full immunisation record since birth (with a photo of the pet) must be submitted.
OM.rabies_titer: Required: RNATT or FAVN from an accredited lab. Sample drawn 21–30 days after the last rabies vaccination. The result must be at least 3 months and no more than 12 months old at export.
documents: Veterinary import permit (Bayan)
Government veterinary health certificate from the exporting country
Passport or immunisation record
Accredited lab certificate for the rabies antibody test
OM.import_permit: Required before arrival via Customs Bayan, issued by MAFWR Veterinary Quarantine Department. Fee OMR 20. Approval within about 2 hours during official hours, 7 days a week. Validity is not stated.
OM.quarantine: Not stated. Shipment release takes about 2 hours after inspection (24/7).
OM.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: titre blood draw, then wait until the result is at least 3 months old → Bayan import permit → government health certificate → arrival. From scratch, plan at least 4–5 months (rabies vaccination at 12 weeks or older, titre 21–30 days later).
OM.restricted_breeds: Prohibited under Resolution 222/2019 (including mixes): Pitbull, Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, Mastiff, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Rottweiler, Doberman Pinscher, Presa Canario, Boxer, Boerboel, Caucasian Shepherd Dog, Anatolian Karabash, Great Dane. Pets must be over 4 months old.
OM.private_aviation: The official customs page lists arrival documents for land, sea, air cargo and passenger ports. Confirm in-cabin carriage on a private jet with the Muscat airport veterinary quarantine before the flight.
OM.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries Wealth and Water Resources (MAFWR) – Veterinary Quarantine Department, via Royal Oman Police Customs (Bayan)

vaccinations: Rabies: from 3 months of age; at least 30 days must pass after the first rabies vaccination before entry.
documents: International health certificate for dogs or cats (forms dated June 2025), signed by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by APHIS.
Panamanian consulate/embassy stamp and signature after APHIS endorsement (apostille requirement temporarily waived since 31 Dec 2020, but the consular stamp is still required).
Home Quarantine Request (MINSA form) with a scanned health certificate, arrival date/time and flight, emailed to cam@minsa.gob.pa at least 3 days before arrival.
PA.quarantine: Home quarantine under a MINSA request.
PA.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies (30-day wait if first dose), health certificate, APHIS endorsement, consular stamp, MINSA request at least 3 days before arrival.
PA.export: Return to the US: Panama is NOT on the CDC high-risk list. It is screwworm-affected, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
PA.authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Control de Zoonosis / Ministerio de Desarrollo Agropecuario (MIDA)

PE.microchip: Not required by SENASA Peru for entry (not listed).
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory for dogs and cats from 3 months of age.
Dogs: canine parvovirus, distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis (plus rabies).
Cats: feline panleukopenia (plus rabies).
PE.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming within 30 days before travel, stated on the origin certificate.
documents: Application with owner and pet data
Original sanitary export certificate (international sanitary certificate) from the origin country's official authority stating vaccinations, deworming and health status
Payment for entry inspection (S/ 98.60)
PE.import_permit: No separate import permit for pet dogs and cats; SENASA performs documentary check and clinical inspection on arrival.
PE.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel: vaccinations → deworming within 30 days → official origin certificate → SENASA inspection and payment on arrival.
PE.private_aviation: SENASA offices at Jorge Chávez (Lima Hub office open 24/7 incl. holidays) and other international airports; confirm SENASA attendance for private arrivals at regional airports.
PE.export: Leaving Peru: SENASA issues the sanitary export certificate per destination requirements; submit ≥72 h before travel: request, destination requirements/permit, vet health certificate and vaccination certificate (Colegio Médico Veterinario format), payment S/ 97.20, any destination tests/microchip; clinical inspection. Offices: Lima Hub (Callao, 24/7), Ate, Lurín and regional offices. Contact viajacontumascota@senasa.gob.pe.
PE.authority: SENASA Perú (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agraria) – MIDAGRI

PF.microchip: Identification certificate showing the implantation date is required.
vaccinations: Rabies: a primary vaccination is valid from 21 days after injection. Boosters must be given before the previous one expires, with the same vaccine.
PF.rabies_titer: For non-rabies-free origins: blood taken at least 1 month after vaccination, at an accredited lab. The result is valid from 3 months after sampling, for 1 year. Pets vaccinated at 3 months cannot enter before 9 months and 21 days of age.
PF.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatments by a vet: first within 30 days of departure (no later than 16-19 days before), second at least 14 days later and within 4 days of departure.
documents: Import permit (mes-demarches.gov.pf; 5,500 XPF per animal)
Identification certificate
Rabies vaccination certificates
Rabies titre result
Dogs: negative leishmaniasis ELISA/IF within 30 days of departure, sent directly to DBS (the permit is issued only after this)
Females: non-pregnancy ultrasound within 30 days of departure, or a sterilisation certificate
Official export health certificate signed within 4 days of departure
PF.import_permit: Yes, online at mes-demarches.gov.pf (separate procedures for air and sea arrivals). Apply about 7 months before departure. Without a direct flight, each leg needs its own application.
PF.quarantine: No quarantine period is stated. The pet gets an inspection and laissez-passer by the DBS official vet at Tahiti (fees about 6,000-12,500 XPF depending on arrival time).
PF.timeline: Plan at least 7 months: microchip, rabies vaccine, titre (1+ month after the vaccine, then a 3-month wait), permit application, leishmaniasis test and parasite treatments in the last 30 days, health certificate within 4 days of departure.
PF.restricted_breeds: Category 1 dogs (attack dogs under French classification) are prohibited. Pets under 3 months are not admitted unless with their mother. Snub-nosed breeds may be refused by airlines.
PF.private_aviation: DBS states that dogs and cats must travel to French Polynesia as manifested cargo in sealed IATA crates; only certified assistance dogs may travel in the cabin. Inspection is done only at Tahiti. Private aircraft are not specifically addressed; a pet in the cabin of a private jet does not meet the stated rule. Confirm with DBS (zoo.aeroport.dbs@administration.gov.pf).
PF.export: DBS publishes a separate page for exporting a pet from French Polynesia.
PF.authority: Direction de la Biosécurité (DBS), Cellule zoosanitaire

documents: NAQIA import permit and prior written permission of the Chief Stock Inspector
Official health certificate meeting permit conditions
Customs clearing agent engaged for clearance
PG.import_permit: Yes. NAQIA import permit (animalbiosecurity@naqia.gov.pg); its conditions take precedence.
PG.quarantine: Post-arrival quarantine at the NAQIA animal quarantine station, Kilakila (Port Moresby). Duration is set by the permit.
PG.timeline: Not determinable for US/EU origin: the pet must first qualify through residence in an approved origin (e.g. more than 1 year in Australia, or cleared Australian quarantine).
PG.private_aviation: Origin restricted to Australia, NZ, Hawaii, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. Arrivals Monday–Wednesday only (no weekends or public holidays). Quarantine at Kilakila, and a customs clearing agent is needed.
PG.authority: National Agriculture Quarantine and Inspection Authority (NAQIA)

PH.microchip: Microchip required (number recorded on the SPSIC and used to track repeat imports). Pets arriving without the required identification are refused entry and returned (consular sources).
vaccinations: Rabies: given by a licensed vet in the source country at 12 weeks of age or older. After a first-ever vaccination, wait 14 days before applying. Annual boosters: can ship at once if given within the vaccine's validity, otherwise wait 14 days. 3-year vaccines are accepted.
Rabies may be waived for pets from WOAH self-declared rabies-free countries.
BAI says only rabies vaccination is required.
PH.rabies_titer: Not currently required. Mandatory for all SPSIC applications from 1 January 2027 (BAI); confirm the test details (laboratory, timing, waiting period) with BAI before booking a 2027 arrival.
PH.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment records are uploaded with the application. They need not be renewed before applying, but must remain valid until arrival.
documents: SPSIC (BAI import clearance)
Vaccination and antiparasitic records
Microchip number and an actual photo of the pet
Pet passport if any
Veterinary health certificate from the origin country matching the SPSIC (animal count must match)
One-time importers: notarised Affidavit of Undertaking (BAI MC 43, 2020)
PH.import_permit: Yes: SPSIC from BAI via the DA Trade System. Processing takes 11 working days. A new permit is needed if the airline changes in transit.
PH.quarantine: BAI's pet import page sets no quarantine. The pet is inspected at the port of entry.
PH.timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks (more for 2027 arrivals because of the titre test): microchip, rabies vaccine (14-day wait if first dose), SPSIC application (11 working days), health certificate, travel within SPSIC validity.
PH.restricted_breeds: Minimum age 4 months. No pregnant animals. Animals that have given birth must have done so at least 12 weeks before travel. BAI's pet import page lists no breed bans.
PH.authority: Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), National Veterinary Quarantine Services Division

PK.microchip: The certificate records the microchip number (or animal name) and the vet verifies the chip. ISO 11784/11785 is advised.
vaccinations: Rabies: listed on the certificate with date, vaccine name and validity period. Must be current.
PK.rabies_titer: Not required (none on the USDA Pakistan certificate).
PK.parasite_treatment: None mandated on the certificate (an 'other treatments, if required' table is provided).
documents: USDA 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Birds, Dogs and Cats from the USA to Pakistan', signed by a licensed vet. USDA endorsement not required. Valid 30 days after issue.
Rabies vaccination record
PK.import_permit: Confirm with the Ministry of National Food Security & Research before travel whether an import NOC or permit is needed.
PK.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: health certificate from a licensed vet (valid 30 days, no USDA endorsement). Add time for an NOC if the Ministry requires one.
PK.authority: Ministry of National Food Security & Research

PL.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
PL.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
PL.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Poland does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
PL.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
PL.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
PL.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the General Veterinary Inspectorate (GIW) before travel.
PL.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Poland and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry: Warsaw Chopin (Okęcie), Warsaw Modlin, Kraków, Katowice, Gdańsk, Poznań, Wrocław, Łódź, Rzeszów, Szczecin-Goleniów, Bydgoszcz and Lublin (Świdnik); customs performs the checks. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
PL.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.

PR.microchip: Official individual ID required: microchip OR collar with metal tag.
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs and cats over 4 months must be vaccinated and carry a rabies certificate. The Puerto Rico Department of Agriculture document says the vaccination must be given 'within six (6) months prior to shipment', which is unusually strict, so confirm with the PR State Veterinarian.
PR.parasite_treatment: External parasite treatment within 72 hours before entry, recorded on the health certificate.
documents: Official certificate of veterinary inspection (e.g. APHIS 7001 or a state CVI) by an accredited vet, valid 30 days from inspection, stating the animal doesn't come from a rabies-quarantined area.
Rabies vaccination certificate.
International arrivals: CDC Dog Import Form and other federal requirements (see the US entry).
PR.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats moving interstate.
PR.timeline: Plan at least 1–2 weeks before travel: rabies status check, CVI within 30 days, parasite treatment within 72 hours of arrival.
PR.private_aviation: Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries CANNOT enter the US via Puerto Rico (no CDC-registered facility in US territories).
PR.export: Puerto Rico to the US mainland is domestic travel (no CDC form). The Cayman Islands classes Puerto Rico as high rabies risk (3-month titer wait).
PR.authority: Departamento de Agricultura de Puerto Rico – Oficina del Oficial Estatal de Sanidad Animal (SAHO)

PY.microchip: Not mandatory under Mercosur rules; if electronic ID is used it must be ISO 11784/11785 with location stated on the CVI.
vaccinations: Rabies: animals 90 days or older, valid vaccine; primary vaccination at least 21 days before embarkation.
Under 90 days: allowed if CVI certifies age and no contact with urban rabies in the last 90 days.
PY.parasite_treatment: Broad-spectrum internal and external antiparasitic treatment within 15 days before CVI issue (Mercosur GMC 20/24).
documents: Original CVI (Mercosur model) from origin official authority, valid 60 days from issue while rabies is valid
Clinical exam within 10 days before CVI issue
Or official passport endorsed by origin authority with all CVI data
PY.import_permit: Not required for up to 5 dogs/cats; 6 or more are treated as a commercial live-animal import.
PY.quarantine: None routinely; non-compliance may lead to refusal, re-export or retention (owner's cost). Paraguay may refuse animals diagnosed with leishmaniasis.
PY.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel: rabies (≥21 days if primary) → antiparasitic within 15 days of CVI → vet exam within 10 days of CVI → official CVI → SENACSA check on arrival.
PY.private_aviation: Present the pet and CVI to the SENACSA veterinary inspector at the point of entry; confirm inspector attendance for private arrivals.
PY.export: Leaving Paraguay: SENACSA issues the CVI via SENACSA Digital (account validated in person once with notarised ID) or in person; private-vet clinical inspection within 10 days before CVI using SENACSA's 'Certificado de Inspección Clínica y Vacunación' form; rabies valid ≤1 year, ≥21 days if primary. EU/UK/Israel/Russia/UAE CVIs processed in person.
PY.authority: SENACSA (Servicio Nacional de Calidad y Salud Animal)

QA.microchip: Required: NZ MPI guidance requires the microchip to be scanned and verified before the rabies vaccination. ISO 15-digit is recommended.
vaccinations: Rabies: required. Valid 30 days after a primary vaccination (NZ MPI). Hukoomi says vaccinations must be at least 30 days before travel.
QA.rabies_titer: Required: the import permit application must include a laboratory report for a rabies titre test (NZ MPI, Aug 2024). Confirm the required result and any waiting period with the Ministry of Municipality before travel.
documents: Ministry of Municipality import permit (valid 30 days from issue, per Hukoomi)
Original official veterinary health certificate from the exporting country
Rabies vaccination certificate
Rabies titre lab report
Copy of owner ID
QA.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Ministry of Municipality (Livestock Department / Department of Animal Resources) as a hybrid online or offline service. Processing about 1 working day. Valid 30 days from issue. NZ MPI says the permit should be issued at least 30 days before arrival. One pet per person (NZ MPI, Aug 2024). Hukoomi states pets must be over 4 months old.
QA.quarantine: No mandatory quarantine if health requirements are met. Otherwise quarantine at the owner's expense (NZ MPI).
QA.timeline: Steps: microchip → rabies vaccination (at least 30 days before travel) → rabies titre blood test → Ministry of Municipality import permit (issued at least 30 days before arrival, valid 30 days) → official health certificate → arrive via Hamad International Airport. Confirm any waiting period after the titre test with the Ministry of Municipality before booking.
QA.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs (NZ MPI Aug 2024 list): Afghan Hound, American Staffordshire Terrier, Boerboel, Boxer, Bull Terrier, Bulldog, Chinese Shar-Pei, Doberman, Great Dane, Japanese Akita, Neapolitan Mastiff, Rottweiler, Staffordshire Bull Terrier.
QA.private_aviation: NZ MPI states dogs and cats may enter only via Hamad International Airport (DOH). In-cabin travel is accepted with written airline permission. For a private jet using Doha International (DIA), confirm with the Ministry of Municipality and the handler before routing that the pet can be cleared there.
QA.authority: Ministry of Municipality – Livestock Department / Department of Animal Resources
