RS.microchip: Required (permanent marking by microchip; tattoo accepted only if applied before 3 July 2011)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccine with ≥1 antigenic unit/dose (WHO); for a primary vaccination, 21 days must pass before entry; boosters within validity
Pets under 16 weeks: accepted only with owner declaration of no contact with wild rabies-susceptible animals, or accompanied by vaccinated mother
RS.rabies_titer: Only if coming from, or transiting, a non-listed country: ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, sample ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before import
RS.parasite_treatment: Echinococcus treatment optional for entry into Serbia (APHIS)
documents: Serbia certificate for non-commercial movement of ≤5 dogs/cats/ferrets (separate form for >5) — valid for 4 months after issue for onward movement, or until rabies vaccine expiry
Owner's non-commercial declaration
Pet passport from origin country (Serbian government tourism page)
RS.timeline: Plan at least 1 month from listed countries (4+ months otherwise): microchip → rabies (21 days) → certificate within 10 days of travel
RS.private_aviation: APHIS notes Serbia restricts imports/transit from Germany and Hungary over foot-and-mouth disease; avoid routing via DE/HU with animals until confirmed this does not apply to pets
RS.authority: Veterinary Directorate, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of Serbia (Uprava za veterinu)

RU.microchip: Not required by Rosselkhoznadzor for import (unidentified pets may be imported for home keeping); recommended
vaccinations: Rabies: all dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before dispatch unless vaccinated within last 12 months; 3-year vaccine accepted if vet confirms still valid; or titer ≥0.5 IU/ml
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis (or dihydrostreptomycin prophylaxis) — ≥20 days before, within last 12 months
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days before, within last 12 months
Unvaccinated puppies/kittens <3 months: only with Form 15 certificate
RU.rabies_titer: Not required (only an alternative to proof of valid vaccination)
documents: ≤2 pets accompanied by owner: international veterinary passport with vaccination records and stamp of the origin country's competent authority confirming clinical exam within 14 days before shipment (serves as the veterinary certificate)
Otherwise: EAEU Veterinary Certificate Form 15 (US: APHIS-endorsed, exam within 5 days per APHIS guidance; APHIS page states Russia allows exam up to 14 days before)
RU.import_permit: None for ≤2 personal dogs/cats with owner. >2 animals or unaccompanied: Rosselkhoznadzor permit via Argus system; annual generic Form No. 1 permit covers up to 5 pets from listed countries (non-commercial)
RU.timeline: Allow at least 5 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (rabies and core vaccines at least 20 days before travel): clinical exam stamped in the pet passport within 14 days, or an EAEU Form 15 certificate within 5 days, then entry at a border point with veterinary control.
RU.private_aviation: Heavily restricted: reciprocal airspace bans with EU/UK/US/Canada and others; US/EU/UK export controls and sanctions bar many business jets (US-origin or Western-registered/operated) from flying to Russia. Check with Elysium Jet operations before quoting. Entry only at border points with veterinary control. APHIS also notes temporary transit restrictions via Germany/Hungary for FMD-susceptible animals (not dog/cat specific)
RU.export: Rosselkhoznadzor: check destination rules; microchip (ISO) and rabies vaccination as required by destination; titer at approved lab for EU, Switzerland, UAE, Japan, Israel, Turkey, US (dogs) etc. Obtain Form No. 1 veterinary certificate from district state vet station (СББЖ) via Mercury, ≤5 days before departure. At airport veterinary control (or in advance at Rosselkhoznadzor offices/VGNKI, up to 5 days ahead, or online via ecert.vetrf.ru) exchange for EU certificate, Form 5a or destination-specific export certificate. No permit for owner-accompanied pets. Within EAEU (BY/KZ/AM/KG) Form 1 suffices.
RU.authority: Rosselkhoznadzor (Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance), applying EAEU common veterinary requirements

documents: Veterinary import permit (RAB)
RW.import_permit: RAB lists 'Veterinary import/export/transit permits' among its services. Contact info@rab.gov.rw, +250 788 385 312, toll free 4675.
RW.timeline: Contact RAB well before travel to apply for the veterinary import permit and confirm the health requirements.
RW.export: Pets leaving Rwanda need an international veterinary certificate signed by an official veterinarian of RAB (Rwanda migration authority travel page).
RW.authority: Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB)

SA.microchip: Electronic microchip or other means of identification (MEWA Naama guide). The 2021 MEWA rules require a passport and an electronic microchip, and the microchip number must appear on the vaccination record uploaded with the application.
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination, with at least 6 months of validity remaining (MEWA Naama service conditions). MEWA checks validity when issuing the permit.
Other vaccines according to the exporting country's approved vaccination programme (2021 MEWA rules).
SA.rabies_titer: MEWA's rules (2021 rules and Naama guide) do not list a titer test. Confirm on Naama for the specific origin country before travel.
SA.parasite_treatment: Pets must be free of external parasites and diseases (2021 MEWA rules). No specific treatment window is stated.
documents: MEWA/Naama pet entry permit (copy or original)
Original government veterinary health certificate from the exporting country, or a digitally endorsed copy for US origin
Original or electronic certificate of origin (no Saudi embassy attestation needed, per the 2021 rules)
Vaccination record or pet passport
For the application: owner's ID, passport or iqama, pet photo, and passport or vaccination page showing the microchip number
SA.import_permit: Required: 'Pet entry and exit permit (dogs, cats)' on naama.sa (login via Nafath). Apply 15 days before shipment (MEWA Naama user guide). Valid 30 days from issue. Entry only through the port named on the permit. Individuals: one permit every 6 months, maximum 2 animals per permit. Applicant age: at least 21 for dogs and at least 18 for cats (the older 2021 rules said at least 30 for dogs). Diplomats are exempt from the age rule with an official letter. Commercial dog imports are not allowed. Import only from countries listed as permitted on the platform. MEWA may set arrival times according to quarantine capacity.
SA.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated for compliant pets. MEWA may schedule arrival according to port quarantine capacity. The GCC veterinary quarantine law applies.
SA.timeline: Allow at least 21 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU: apply for the Naama permit at least 15 days before shipment (valid 30 days), then the government health certificate and certificate of origin. The rabies vaccination must still have at least 6 months of validity at entry, so a booster may be needed first. From scratch, plan at least 6–8 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination → Naama permit → health certificate → enter only via the named port.
SA.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including crosses): Pit Bull, Rottweiler, Boxer, Mastiff, Tosa, Bulldog, Perro de Presa Canario.
SA.private_aviation: MEWA requires entry through the port named on the permit and IATA-compliant containers for air imports, and may set arrival times according to port quarantine capacity. Make sure the permit names the actual private-aviation arrival airport (e.g. Riyadh or Jeddah) and confirm MEWA veterinary inspection at the executive terminal with the handler before the flight.
SA.export: The same Naama 'pet entry and exit permit (dogs, cats)' service covers departures, with the same conditions (30-day validity, apply about 15 days ahead). The destination country's rules also apply.
SA.authority: Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA), Naama platform

vaccinations: Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, canine parvovirus and parainfluenza (per the permit-based certificate).
documents: Import permit (Biosecurity Solomon Islands)
Owner/exporter statutory declaration (no disease signs and no contact with sick animals in the 30 days before export)
Government vet health certificate, one per animal
SB.import_permit: Yes. Biosecurity Solomon Islands (enquiries@biosecurity.gov.sb). Permit conditions take precedence.
SB.quarantine: Biosecurity may inspect, test, detain or treat. Animals other than dogs and cats from Australia or NZ must be inspected by an approved vet before release. Non-compliant animals are destroyed or re-exported at the importer's cost.
SB.restricted_breeds: Dogs and cats must be desexed before import.
SB.private_aviation: The origin condition (no rabies diagnosed in the exporting country for 5 years) blocks direct entry from the USA and other rabies-affected origins.
SB.authority: Biosecurity Solomon Islands (Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock)

SC.microchip: Microchip number required on the permit application.
documents: Veterinary import permit (National Biosecurity Agency)
Original veterinary certificates as set on the permit, presented at the port of entry
SC.import_permit: Mandatory. Apply to the Chief Executive Officer of the National Biosecurity Agency at least 4 months ahead (rabies-infected countries) or 4 weeks ahead (rabies-free countries). Permits are valid for a limited period and one consignment only; the conditions on the permit must be followed. Phone the veterinary services if the permit has not arrived two weeks after applying.
SC.timeline: Apply for the import permit at least 4 months before entry from rabies-infected countries (such as the USA and most of the EU), or 4 weeks before from rabies-free countries, then follow the conditions on the permit.
SC.authority: National Biosecurity Agency (formerly Seychelles Agricultural Agency – Veterinary Services)

SE.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
SE.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
SE.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.
Young animals: Sweden does not accept unvaccinated or insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under about 15 weeks) from other EU states; they are never allowed from outside the EU.
SE.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
SE.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
SE.restricted_breeds: Local dangerous-dog rules may apply; confirm any breed restrictions with the Swedish Board of Agriculture before travel.
SE.private_aviation: Arrivals from outside the EU (other than the Annex I territories Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino and Vatican City, and Northern Ireland) must land at a travellers' point of entry designated by Sweden and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Only two points of entry: Stockholm-Arlanda and Gothenburg-Landvetter airports. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at the owner's cost.
SE.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet the destination's rules; export certificates are endorsed by the official veterinary service.

SG.microchip: ISO 11784 or ISO 11785 Annex A. The chip number must appear on all vaccination and treatment records.
vaccinations: Rabies (Schedule II and III only): valid inactivated or recombinant vaccine, with no lapse in cover. Schedule I pets need no rabies vaccine or serology.
Dogs: canine distemper, adenovirus type 1, parvovirus type 2.
Cats: feline calicivirus, herpesvirus-1, panleukopaenia.
Schedule III pets are vaccinated against rabies again on arrival at AQC.
SG.rabies_titer: Schedule II and III: rabies serology of at least 0.5 IU/ml. The blood sample must be taken at least 28 days after a valid vaccination, and between 90 days and 12 months before export. The lab must be a WOAH reference lab or one approved by the competent authority of a Schedule I or II country.
SG.parasite_treatment: Parasite treatments and the veterinary health certificate must both be done 2 to 7 days before export, as set out in the schedule-specific veterinary conditions.
documents: Dog licence or cat licence (PALS), obtained before the import licence
AVS import licence via GoBusiness (valid 90 days, cannot be extended)
Veterinary health certificate in the schedule-specific format: Sections I-III by the treating vet, Section IV endorsed by an official government vet, issued 2-7 days before export
Vaccination records and rabies serology report
Signed captain's declaration endorsed by the airline (Schedule I/II)
Customs GST In-Payment permit where applicable
Inspection appointment booked at least 5 days before arrival via AVS e-services
SG.import_permit: Yes: an AVS import licence (personal: S$50 normal, 2 working days; S$100 express, 1 working day), valid 90 days. The dog or cat licence must be obtained first. The USDA summary says to apply 30 days before arrival.
SG.quarantine: Schedule I: none. Schedule II: none if the pet arrives less than 5 days after the owner's entry and has lived at the owner's address for 6+ months; otherwise at least 10 days of home quarantine (smart collar, S$29/animal/day, apply via FormSG first) for personal imports, or 10 days at AQC for commercial imports. Schedule III: at least 30 days at AQC (Sembawang), booked through the Quarantine Management System once the serology result is ready.
SG.timeline: Allow at least 100 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU (Schedule II) without serology on file: the blood sample must be taken at least 90 days before export (and at least 28 days after a valid vaccination). With valid serology already on file, or from the UK (Schedule I), about 2–3 weeks. Steps: serology → AQC booking if Schedule III → dog/cat licence → AVS import licence → inspection booked at least 5 days before arrival → vet certificate and parasite treatments 2–7 days before export. From scratch, plan at least 4–7 months for Schedule II/III and about 1 month for Schedule I. UAE (Schedule III): add 30 days at AQC.
SG.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs: Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog), Akita, Boerboel, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Neapolitan Mastiff, Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, and crosses of any of these. Cats: F1-F4 Bengal or Savannah crosses are prohibited. Housing limits apply (e.g. HDB flats). Minimum age 12 weeks at export.
SG.private_aviation: AVS describes air clearance only at the Changi Animal & Plant Quarantine Station (Changi Airfreight Centre); for arrivals at other checkpoints, AVS advises on clearance when the import licence is issued. In-cabin or excess-baggage pets must be in a rigid IATA crate (no soft bags). Before routing a private flight to Seletar, confirm with AVS and the FBO where the inspection will take place.
SG.export: AVS publishes separate 'Exporting dogs and cats' procedures (avs.nparks.gov.sg); follow them and the destination's rules.
SG.authority: Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS), National Parks Board (NParks)

SH.microchip: Required (ISO recommended). The Official Veterinarian reads the chip at every exam (UK EHC 3921 v5).
vaccinations: Rabies: no rabies vaccination clause on UK certificate 3921 (the UK is rabies-free). Vaccination plus a titer is advised if the pet will return to the UK.

Leptospira: dogs tested (MAT) within 30 days of export. If the first result is positive (≤1:400), a paired sample at least 14 days later must show no rise, or the dog is treated with doxycycline or dihydrostreptomycin.
SH.rabies_titer: Not on St Helena's UK certificate. A titer may be needed to enter the UK first from non-listed countries (UK rules), and is advised for return to the UK.
SH.parasite_treatment: Within 30 days before export: 2 broad-spectrum dewormings at least 14 days apart (nematodes and cestodes; praziquantel advised for trematodes). Dogs: milbemycin or moxidectin within 4 days before export. Fipronil topical 2–10 days before export. Exam within 4 days of shipment, free of external parasites.
documents: UK export health certificate 3921EHC (v5), signed by a UK Official Veterinarian
Owner declarations: residence (or fully validated pet passport), not pregnant, more than 24 weeks old, dog not a prohibited type

Original lab reports (within 30 days of export): dogs, heartworm microfilaria and antigen ELISA, Brucella canis, Leptospira canicola MAT and Ehrlichia canis IFAT; dogs, Babesia gibsoni/canis IFAT plus blood smear within 10 days; dogs and cats, 2 faecal hookworm tests at least 14 days apart
St Helena import licence (SHG Biosecurity).
SH.import_permit: An import licence from SHG Biosecurity (ANRD) is required. Contact ANRD/Biosecurity on +290 24724.
SH.quarantine: No quarantine service on St Helena (abolished in 2011). Pets that do not comply cannot be held on the island.
SH.timeline: Allow at least 35 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the UK with a validated pet passport or 6 months' UK/Ireland residence: apply for the SHG import licence → within 30 days of export, dog blood tests and 2 faecal tests 14 days apart plus 2 dewormings → Babesia tests within 10 days → fipronil 2–10 days before → heartworm treatment and Official Veterinarian exam within 4 days. A pet from the USA or the EU must first enter the UK under UK rules; a US pet without a validated pet passport needs 6 months' UK/Ireland residence.
SH.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Pit Bull Terrier, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa and Fila Brasileiro, and crosses of these types (UK NFG 3921). Pets must be more than 24 weeks old and not pregnant.
SH.private_aviation: Only direct imports from the UK (and Ascension) are eligible, so a private flight straight from Africa, Europe or the US with a pet will not be accepted. A flight from the UK carrying a pet with a valid 3921EHC may be possible: get written confirmation and an import licence from SHG Biosecurity before booking.
SH.export: 2013 guidance: pets could not return directly from St Helena to South Africa and had to travel via the UK. Check current South African permit conditions.
SH.authority: St Helena Government – Biosecurity / Veterinary Section, Agriculture & Natural Resources Division (ANRD)
