SL.microchip: Not required by the UK certificate: identification by tattoo, microchip, or full description. Microchip recommended.
vaccinations: Rabies: the UK certificate records rabies vaccination (date window set by the OV), or a statement that no rabies vaccine was given. A current rabies vaccination is strongly recommended because Sierra Leone is rabies-endemic.
SL.parasite_treatment: Exam within 48 hours before export must find the pet free of clinical signs of disease, including distemper, rabies and external parasites (UK certificate 6548).
documents: Sierra Leone import permit (apply at least 6 weeks before export)
Official veterinary health certificate (UK model 6548: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination certificate (if vaccinated)
SL.import_permit: Advised by UK official guidance: apply to the Sierra Leone authorities (Ministry of Agriculture, livestock/veterinary services) at least 6 weeks before export. Confirm the issuing office and process with the Ministry before travel.
SL.timeline: Allow at least 42 days: apply for the import permit at least 6 weeks before export → keep the rabies vaccination current → vet exam within 48 hours of departure and government endorsement (UK certificate valid 7 days).
SL.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Sierra Leone (livestock/veterinary services)

SM.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted), as required by the EU country of arrival. Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
SM.rabies_titer: Under the EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
SM.parasite_treatment: None required under EU rules (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.
SM.quarantine: None if EU requirements are met.
SM.timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
SM.private_aviation: No airport in San Marino. Nearest jet airports are in Italy; Rimini (Miramare) and Bologna are on Italy's September 2026 list of pet points of entry for third-country arrivals.
SM.export: Leaving: the EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport or certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement).
SM.authority: San Marino veterinary service (Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale); at entry, the Italian authorities

vaccinations: Rabies: required. Decree 2002-1094 Art. 173: the international rabies vaccination certificate must be dated more than 15 days and less than 1 year before import. For pets from the USA, APHIS is stricter: a primary vaccination must be given at least 21 days before travel.
documents: Import permit from the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock (valid 3 months)

International zoo-sanitary health certificate from an official veterinarian of the exporting country (Decree 2002-1094 Art. 173). For US-origin pets, APHIS 7001 issued within 21 days of travel is accepted, and no APHIS endorsement is needed if a USDA-accredited vet signs it with their national accreditation number.
International rabies vaccination certificate dated >15 days and <1 year before import (Art. 173)
SN.import_permit: Required. Issued by the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock and valid 3 months from issue. Per APHIS, apply by email to dsvmepa@gmail.com (cc wadesanou@gmail.com) with country of origin, species and breed, owner's name and address of origin.
SN.quarantine: None stated for compliant pets. Animals are inspected at the entry post by the livestock service (Art. 177). Landing is allowed only after the zoo-sanitary certificate is presented to customs.
SN.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: apply for the import permit (processing time is not published) → make sure the rabies vaccination is more than 15 days and less than 1 year old at import (US-origin pets: a primary vaccination at least 21 days before travel, per APHIS) → health certificate within 21 days of travel.
SN.private_aviation: Decree 2002-1094 Art. 176: the authorised sea, air and land entry routes for animal imports are set by ministerial order, and inspection takes place at the entry post. Confirm that veterinary inspection is available at the planned arrival airport (e.g. Dakar Blaise Diagne).
SN.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock (Direction des Services Vétérinaires)

SR.microchip: Not mentioned in the official LVV conditions for cats.
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccinated or revaccinated according to the vaccine manufacturer's recommendations (LVV conditions for cats, 2026).
SR.rabies_titer: From countries not free of rabies: a WOAH-method antibody titration test of at least 0.5 IU/ml, done not less than 3 months and not more than 12 months before export. Not required from rabies-free countries.
SR.parasite_treatment: Within 7 days before export: a broad-spectrum anthelmintic and a treatment against external parasites.
documents: Valid veterinary import permit issued by the Veterinary Inspection of Suriname. Apply on paper or by email to secrdirvee@gmail.com.

Health certificate in Dutch or English from the origin country's competent veterinary authority. It must certify a clinical exam within 7 days before export with no signs of contagious disease or ectoparasites, the rabies vaccination, the titer (where required) and the parasite treatments.
SR.import_permit: Required: veterinary import permit from the Head of the Veterinary Service (Ministerie van LVV, Directoraat Veeteelt, Letitia Vriesdelaan 8–10, Paramaribo; tel. +597 479112; secrdirvee@gmail.com). If any condition is breached, entry can be refused and the permit withdrawn at the holder's cost.
SR.quarantine: No quarantine facility stay. The animal must be kept separate from other animals for at least 2 weeks after arrival, and may not be moved, sold or given away during that time without the Head of the Veterinary Service's permission. Inspectors may take blood or faecal samples at any time.
SR.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from a rabies-affected country such as the USA: titer blood draw at least 3 months before export, then the import permit application, the exam and parasite treatment within 7 days of export, and the endorsed health certificate. Notify the Veterinary Service at least 48 h before arrival.
SR.private_aviation: The Head of the Veterinary Service must be told the time and place of import at least 48 hours before arrival. Give the exact airport (e.g. Johan Adolf Pengel, PBM) and ETA.
SR.authority: Ministerie van Landbouw, Veeteelt en Visserij (LVV), Directoraat Veeteelt, Veterinary Service / Veterinary Inspection, Paramaribo

vaccinations: Rabies: animals over 2 months, vaccinated no more than 365 days before embarkation. The certificate states the date and product.
SV.parasite_treatment: Treated for endo- and ectoparasites with approved products (no timing stated).
documents: Health certificate by a licensed vet, exam within 30 days of departure, in at least duplicate. No USDA endorsement, notary or consular stamp.
Rabies vaccination certificate.
SV.import_permit: Required, from the Dirección General de Sanidad Vegetal y Animal (MAG). Can be obtained before travel or on arrival at the port of entry. A quarantine permit is also obtained at the port on arrival.
SV.timeline: Plan at least 2 weeks before travel: rabies (within 365 days), vet exam within 30 days.
SV.export: Return to the US: El Salvador IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country (USDA-endorsed CDC certification before leaving the US, or arrival at a CDC-registered facility airport). A screwworm certificate is also needed.
SV.authority: Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería (MAG) – Dirección General de Sanidad Vegetal y Animal

SX.microchip: ISO microchip, or a readable tattoo applied before July 2011. The number must be on the certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days and no more than 1 or 3 years (per the vaccine) before departure.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, Bordetella and parvovirus.
Cats: FeLV, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia and pneumonitis.
SX.parasite_treatment: Internal: negative fecal flotation, or if positive, treatment 21 days before departure. External: parasiticide (e.g. Frontline, NexGard, Bravecto) 7–14 days before departure; free of Amblyomma and Boophilus ticks.
documents: Sint Maarten import permit (valid 30 days from issue).
International health certificate in English or Dutch, from an accredited vet and endorsed by the exporting country's Chief Veterinary Officer (APHIS, via VEHCS). EU pet passports are NOT accepted.
Copy of the owner's passport; Animal Movement Authorization Form if the owner isn't travelling.
SX.import_permit: Required. Apply to Inspectorate TEATT – Unit LVV (LVV@sintmaartengov.org) via sintmaartengov.org.
SX.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: rabies at least 21 days before departure, fecal test and deworming, permit, tick treatment 7–14 days before departure, APHIS endorsement.
SX.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier types are permitted only if neutered or spayed (stated on the certificate).
SX.private_aviation: No private-aviation specifics are published. The USDA-hosted version mentions inspection by a licensed vet within 24 hours of arrival, which isn't in the 2022 conditions, so confirm with LVV.
SX.authority: Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport & Telecommunication (TEATT) – Inspectorate, Unit LVV

vaccinations: Rabies and other conditions are set out on the TCI import application and permit. The APHIS page doesn't state the timing, so confirm with the Department of Agriculture.
documents: TCI import permit.
International health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, signed in non-black ink, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement) BEFORE submitting the permit application. Valid 10 days from issue.
If the pet stays 24 hours or more in a transit country: a vet certificate covering that stay.
TC.import_permit: Required for all pets. Email, fax or post the application to the Department of Agriculture, Animal Health Services Division, Providenciales (agriculture@gov.tc, +1 649 946 5801).
TC.quarantine: No standard quarantine is published. Non-compliant animals may be held, deported within 48 hours at the owner's expense, or euthanized.
TC.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: vet certificate and APHIS endorsement, then the permit application within the 10-day certificate validity, then at least 48 hours' notice of arrival.
TC.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, American Pit Bull Terrier, American Bulldog, American Staffordshire Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, Fila Brasileiro. Restricted (contact TCI first): Appenzeller, Aryan Molossus, Bandog, Beauceron, Belgian Mastiff, Bull Mastiff, Danish Broholmer, Dogue de Bordeaux, Great Swiss Mountain Dog, Korean Jindo, Kuvasz, Leonberger, Moscow Watchdog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Perro de Presa Mallorquin, Boerboel, Tibetan Mastiff.
TC.private_aviation: Must enter through an official port of entry. Give at least 48 hours' notice to the Inspection Unit of the confirmed arrival date, time, aircraft/flight and port of entry.
TC.authority: Turks and Caicos Islands Department of Agriculture – Animal Health Services Division

TG.microchip: Required (US-origin certificate lists the microchip number as required and the vet must verify the chip).
vaccinations: Rabies: current at the time of export; the certificate records vaccine name, batch number and validity end date (APHIS, US-origin)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to the Togolese Republic (AUG 2025 form), signed by an accredited vet (electronic signature accepted) and ink-endorsed and embossed by USDA; the original must travel with the pet
TG.timeline: Plan at least 3-4 weeks before travel: microchip and rabies vaccination, then an accredited-vet health certificate, then USDA ink endorsement (allow time for mail or appointment).
TG.authority: Togolese veterinary authority (not named by APHIS); USDA APHIS for US-origin certification

TH.microchip: Microchip number required on the application and records. The DLD advises implanting it before or on the same day as the rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days before departure for a primary vaccine, given at 12 weeks of age or older. Boosters need no wait. Pets from rabies-free countries may be exempt.

Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, leptospirosis. If the leptospirosis vaccine is not valid or not 21+ days old, a negative leptospirosis test within 30 days before departure is accepted instead.
Cats: feline panleukopenia.
documents: Application Form R.1/1 with pet details and microchip implantation certificate
Copy of owner's passport and flight itinerary
Colour photo of the pet
English vaccination certificates
Official health certificate endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority (US: valid 10 days from USDA endorsement; originals only)
Printed import permit; Form R-6 and Import License R-7 issued at the AQS on arrival (500 THB per animal)
TH.import_permit: Yes: DLD import permit, emailed by the AQS at the port of entry. Processing takes 5-7 Thai business days and the permit is valid 60 days. Owners travelling with their pet may apply on arrival if all originals are ready, but airlines may refuse boarding without a permit.
TH.quarantine: No fixed quarantine when documents are complete. The pet is inspected at the AQS on arrival. If documents are incomplete, the pet may be held at the quarantine station.
TH.timeline: Allow at least 14 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU: apply for the import permit at least 7 days before departure (5–7 Thai business days' processing; 30 days ahead is recommended), then the health certificate endorsed within 10 days of arrival. From scratch, plan at least 5–6 weeks: microchip and vaccines (at least 21 days before applying) → permit request → endorsed health certificate.
TH.restricted_breeds: The Thai Embassy (Washington) says no dog breeds are banned, but airlines may restrict some. Minimum age 4 months (USDA summary).
TH.private_aviation: AQS offices are at Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Samui and Krabi (all 24 hours for hand-carried pets; the Suvarnabhumi cargo AQS is open 08:30-16:30 Mon-Fri). The permit names the port of entry. Coordinate the arrival airport's AQS inspection and the FBO in advance.
TH.export: DLD: the microchip must be implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccine. Present the pet and documents at the departure port's quarantine station, ideally 2-3 days before departure, to get the export certificate.
TH.authority: Department of Livestock Development (DLD), Animal Quarantine Stations

vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and no more than 12 months before entry. A multi-year vaccine given more than 12 months ago would not qualify, so revaccinate.
documents: Official veterinary health certificate attesting good health and no clinical signs of species-specific diseases
Valid rabies vaccination certificate
TN.timeline: If the last rabies vaccination is more than 12 months old: revaccinate ≥30 days before entry. Then get the official health certificate shortly before travel (validity not published).
TN.restricted_breeds: Dangerous dogs such as Pit Bulls are prohibited (full list not published).
TN.export: For return to the EU: Tunisia is not EU-listed, so a rabies titer is needed (ideally done before leaving the EU).
TN.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries – Direction Générale des Services Vétérinaires (DGSV); Tunisian Customs

documents: MAFF import permit
Signed owner/exporter declaration (identification, history, origin)
International animal health certificate, signed and stamped by the exporting country's official vet (cats: exam within 24 hours of shipment, per the 2019 Australian-origin permit)
TO.import_permit: Yes. Ministry of Agriculture and Food, Forests and Fisheries (info@mafff.gov.to).
TO.quarantine: On arrival, held under veterinary control at an approved quarantine ground or premises until released by a veterinary officer. Duration is per permit.
TO.private_aviation: Post-arrival veterinary control and quarantine premises must be arranged.
TO.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Food, Forests and Fisheries (MAFFF), Quarantine Division

TR.microchip: Required: ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or legible tattoo) applied before rabies vaccination; owner must supply reader if non-ISO
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated or recombinant vaccine (not modified live), given on/after microchip date; booster after lapse counts as primary. Canada's CFIA notes Türkiye does not accept 3-year vaccine validity
Pets <3 months unvaccinated: admitted only under Ministry conditions (APHIS: 21-day home quarantine, or no-wildlife-contact declaration, or accompanied by vaccinated mother)
TR.rabies_titer: Required: at least 0.5 IU/ml at an accredited (EU-approved) lab, blood sampled at least 30 days after vaccination. Waiting period: 90 days counted from the date of the test RESULT (Istanbul Airport veterinary border post page); not required on later trips if the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The Ministry page states no country exemption (APHIS mentions a 21-day quarantine with on-arrival testing if the titer is missing).
TR.parasite_treatment: APHIS guidance (US origin): tick (ectoparasite) treatment and Echinococcus (tapeworm) treatment within 30 days before travel, signed by vet
documents: Veterinary Health and Origin Certificate for cats/dogs/ferrets with passenger (one certificate per pet), issued by origin competent authority within 2 days before travel (US: APHIS endorsement ≤2 days before departure)
Pet passport or ID showing ownership
Original rabies titer report
Rabies vaccination certificate
TR.quarantine: None if compliant; 21 days possible if titer missing or for young unvaccinated pets
TR.timeline: Allow at least 110 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA or EU without a previous titer: titer blood draw, then 90 days from the result; tick and tapeworm treatment within 30 days (APHIS, US origin); health certificate within 2 days of travel. With a prior valid titer and rabies boosters that never lapsed, about 7 days. Return to the EU/GB: Türkiye is not EU-listed, so do the titer before leaving the EU.
TR.restricted_breeds: Import banned (Law 5199 Art. 14(1)(l) and Ministry dangerous-animals circular): American Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, and their crosses.
TR.private_aviation: Pets must enter through a Ministry-approved veterinary border post; Istanbul Airport is confirmed by the Ministry, and APHIS links the list of approved ports. Before routing to business-aviation terminals such as Bodrum, Dalaman or Antalya, confirm with the handler that a veterinary border post is on duty. Since 17 Jul 2026 Türkiye restricts dogs and cats from Texas and New Mexico (New World screwworm).
TR.export: Pet must be microchipped and registered in PETVET with a Turkish pet passport (foreign pets keep existing chip/passport). Rabies vaccine at ≥12 weeks, on/after chip date. FAVN titer (Etlik VKMAEM, ≥30 days after vaccination) if destination requires. Veterinary Health Certificate from the Provincial/District Directorate of Agriculture within 48 hours before departure. Protected native breeds (Kangal, Akbaş, Kars dog, Çatalburun, Zağar, Ankara cat, Van cat) need prior permission to leave; passports listing breed/colour only as 'mix' are rejected. Banned dangerous breeds may leave only if registered and destination accepts
TR.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of the Republic of Türkiye (General Directorate of Food and Control; Veterinary Border Control Posts)

TT.microchip: ISO 11784 / 11785 Annex A, implanted before rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: required (timing beyond the FAVN rule isn't stated).
TT.rabies_titer: FAVN or RFFIT at an approved lab, at least 1 month after vaccination. The lab emails original results to aphmalmr@gmail.com. No post-test waiting period is stated, so confirm with the CVO.
TT.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment before export (timing not stated).
documents: Import permit ('Application for a permit to import dogs and cats').
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, endorsed by USDA within 7 days of arrival (digital VEHCS accepted), listing all countries of residence in the past 6 months.
Intact dogs: negative Brucella canis test.
TT.import_permit: Required, held before entry. Apply to the Office of the Chief Veterinary Officer, 80 Abercromby Street, Port of Spain (aphmalmr@gmail.com, 868-625-5997) at least 1 month before travel.
TT.quarantine: Not stated on the APHIS page. Confirm with the CVO whether home or facility quarantine applies.
TT.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN (1 month later, plus lab time), permit at least 1 month ahead, health certificate and endorsement within 7 days, 2 working days' notice.
TT.private_aviation: Notify the Veterinary Officer, Quarantine (868-693-2910, nadcaph2013@gmail.com) at least 2 working days before the scheduled arrival.
TT.export: Return to the US: Trinidad and Tobago is NOT on the CDC high-risk list, but it is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
TT.authority: Office of the Chief Veterinary Officer, Ministry of Agriculture, Land and Fisheries

TW.microchip: Required. Pet must be at least 90 days old. No microchip means refusal, return, euthanasia or quarantine.
vaccinations: Rabies (inactivated only; Merial Purevax accepted): given at 90 days of age or older, 30 days to 1 year before import.
TW.rabies_titer: Non-rabies-free origins: at least 0.5 IU/ml, sample taken 90 days to 1 year before shipment, at a WOAH reference lab or an APHIA-designated lab. Not required for recognised rabies-free origins (APHIS lists Hawaii and Guam).
documents: Import permit from APHIA (apply with the rabies vaccination certificate, the importer's ID or passport, and the titer report)
Official veterinary health certificate on Taiwan's required form, government-endorsed. Original required. A non-compliant certificate means refusal of entry or destruction of the animal.
Rabies-free origin: statement of 180 days' continuous residence (or since birth) and no third-country visit

US form (version 20250228): pregnant dogs and cats are allowed only if under 4 weeks pregnant. The pet must arrive within 30 days of the USDA endorsement. A second titer is needed if export is more than 1 year after a satisfactory test.
TW.import_permit: Yes. Apply and reserve post-entry quarantine space at least 20 days before shipment.
TW.quarantine: Non-rabies-free origins: 7 days at a designated post-entry quarantine station, with a rabies antibody re-test (revaccinated if below 0.5 IU/ml). Rabies-free origins: reduced or no quarantine if compliant (confirm with APHIA).
TW.timeline: Allow at least 90 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: titer blood draw at a WOAH- or APHIA-designated lab (US: KSU, DoD Texas, Auburn or Missouri FAVN) at least 90 days before shipment → import permit and quarantine booking at least 20 days before → Taiwan-form certificate, endorsed; arrival within 30 days of endorsement → 7-day quarantine. If shipped more than 1 year after the first titer test, a second test is needed.
TW.private_aviation: Transshipment through countries Taiwan does not recognise as rabies-free is not allowed for rabies-free-origin pets. The APHIA airport branch inspection and the quarantine booking apply as for any arrival.
TW.export: APHIA branch offices issue export animal health certificates based on the destination's requirements. Apply in advance.
TW.authority: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency (APHIA, formerly BAPHIQ), Ministry of Agriculture

TZ.microchip: Not explicitly required. The APHIS US-origin certificate accepts either a microchip number or the animal's name.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 1 month and no more than 3 years before entry (Tanzania Embassy); US-origin certificate: current at export, or for animals under 3 months the dam was vaccinated when they were born
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis (adenovirus) and leptospirosis more than 1 month before export (APHIS US-origin certificate; the embassy lists DHLP as recommended)
Cats: panleukopenia, feline herpesvirus-1 and calicivirus (APHIS US-origin certificate)
TZ.parasite_treatment: Embassy advice: deworm every 3 months (or worm tablets every 45 days); no pre-entry treatment window is set.
documents: Import permit from the Director of Veterinary Services

Veterinary health certificate from the exporting country (US: Tanzania-specific APHIS certificate, NOV 2024 form, signed by an accredited vet and endorsed by USDA; can be endorsed digitally via VEHCS; valid 30 days after issue)
Vaccination certificates
TZ.import_permit: Required. Send a letter of request to the Director of Veterinary Services (Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries; the embassy page still uses the old ministry name) stating type/breed, age and port of entry, with vaccination certificates attached. APHIS directs US applicants to the Veterinary Investigation Centre (VIC). Embassy contacts: zoosanitary@mifugo.go.tz, epid1@mifugo.go.tz, +255 22 2862592.
TZ.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated. Animals are examined by a veterinarian at the port of entry and may be quarantined if needed.
TZ.timeline: Allow at least 42 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 1 month before entry) travelling from the USA: apply for the import permit, then the health certificate within 30 days of travel with USDA endorsement.
TZ.private_aviation: Animals may enter only through designated ports. For Zanzibar, confirm the rules with the Zanzibar authorities before travel.
TZ.export: An export permit is required to take the pet back out of Tanzania (Tanzania Embassy).
TZ.authority: Director of Veterinary Services, Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries (Veterinary Investigation Centre, Dar es Salaam)

UA.microchip: Required: ISO microchip, or tattoo applied before 3 July 2011
vaccinations: Rabies: over 12 weeks must be current (US-licensed vaccine for US origin); ≥21 days after primary vaccination or after a booster given outside the validity period
Pets under 12 weeks: must NOT have been vaccinated; 12–16 weeks unvaccinated/<21 days: allowed only with no-wildlife-contact declaration or vaccinated mother
UA.rabies_titer: US origin (APHIS): required, ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, sample >3 months before export; remains valid if no vaccination lapse. Model certificate wording also references 'not more than 12 months' — confirm with Ukrainian authority. From the EU and other countries, confirm the titer requirement with the DPSS before travel (Order No. 553 of 16.11.2018 governs).
UA.parasite_treatment: Model certificate includes an anti-Echinococcus treatment section; APHIS page does not list it as mandatory — confirm
documents: International certificate for introduction into Ukraine of dogs, cats and ferrets for non-commercial movement (issued by accredited vet, endorsed by competent authority)
International pet passport with rabies vaccination
Original rabies titer lab report
UA.timeline: Plan at least 4 months: microchip → rabies → titer → 3-month wait → certificate
UA.private_aviation: Ukrainian airspace closed to civil aviation since 24 Feb 2022 (martial law); no flights possible — reach via neighbouring country (e.g. Poland, Moldova) and cross by land at a border post with veterinary control
UA.authority: State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection (Derzhprodspozhyvsluzhba / DPSS)

vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus, at least 30 days before arrival (Uganda Embassy Washington)
Cats: rabies and feline enteritis (panleukopenia), at least 30 days before arrival (Uganda Embassy Washington)

UK official guidance (NFG 3925, revised 12/2023): rabies, and for dogs distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis and parvovirus, or for cats feline enteritis, each at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export
documents: Import permit from the Commissioner for Animal Health (MAAIF)

Official veterinary health certificate from the origin country's veterinary authority, in English or with an English translation (the embassy says signed and stamped within 10 days of shipment, stating the pet is free from disease)
Movement permit from the veterinary authority of the area of origin (embassy)
Certificate or letter from the local veterinary authority that the area of origin is rabies-free (embassy)
Invoice or price list, packing list, and air waybill (MAAIF general procedure)
UK model certificate 3925: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days, microchip number recorded, owner declaration of 6 months' residence
UG.import_permit: Required. Written application to the Commissioner for Animal Health at least 7 days before import, stating country of origin, supplier, and animal type, breed, sex and quantity. The permit is then sent to the origin veterinary authority for inspection and certification. It may be refused if the disease risk is unmanageable.
UG.quarantine: MAAIF's general post-import procedure (which its dogs-and-cats page says applies) puts imported animals in quarantine or holding for 21-30 days, with release after tests. The page does not state this specifically for pets accompanying their owners, so confirm with MAAIF.
UG.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (at least 30 days before arrival): permit application at least 7 days before, health certificate within 10 days of shipment, and confirmation of arrival with the port veterinary officer at least 3 days before.
UG.private_aviation: Confirm the arrival date with the port-of-entry veterinary official at least 3 days before arrival; pets must be crated individually with no contact with other animals.
UG.export: Apply to the Commissioner for Animal Health at least 15 days before export for a veterinary health certificate. Dogs need records of vaccination against rabies, distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis, parainfluenza and tracheobronchitis. The destination country's import permit is also required.
UG.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF), Commissioner for Animal Health

US.microchip: Dogs: required, readable by a universal scanner. For the high-risk-country routes it must be implanted before the rabies vaccine, or the vaccine is invalid. Cats: no federal requirement.
vaccinations: Dogs only in dog-rabies-free/low-risk countries in the past 6 months: no federal rabies certificate required (CDC recommends vaccination; states and airlines may require it).

Dogs in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months: valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks (84 days) of age or older, after the microchip. US-vaccinated dogs: a first vaccine must be at least 28 days old when the CDC certification form is completed.
Cats: no federal USDA/APHIS requirement. Many states require rabies vaccination.
US.rabies_titer: Only for foreign-vaccinated dogs from high-risk countries: serology at a CDC-approved lab, drawn at least 30 days after the first valid vaccine and at least 28 days before entry. It stays valid as long as vaccination doesn't lapse. Without a valid titer, the dog does a 28-day quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility.
documents: CDC Dog Import Form receipt for every dog. Free, online, one per dog. Low-risk route: receipt valid 6 months. High-risk routes: single entry on the listed date and port.

US-vaccinated dogs returning from a high-risk country: Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination, completed in USDA's system by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by USDA BEFORE the dog leaves the US.

Foreign-vaccinated dogs from a high-risk country: Certification of Foreign Rabies Vaccination and Microchip, endorsed by an official government vet and completed no more than 30 days before travel; titer report; reservation at a CDC-registered animal care facility (exam and US revaccination on arrival).

Dogs from screwworm (NWS)-affected regions, including US dogs returning from Mexico: certificate signed by a full-time official government vet of the region (Mexico: a SENASICA-authorized vet may sign) stating the dog was inspected within 5 days of shipment and is free of screwworm. APHIS's affected list includes most of Central America, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago, Aruba and the UAE; Mexico is under a separate temporary restriction.
Dogs from FMD-affected countries: no document, but coat and bedding must be free of excess dirt or straw, bathe on arrival, and keep away from livestock for 5 days.
US.import_permit: None for personal pets. Dogs imported for resale or adoption have additional USDA APHIS Animal Care permit and health requirements.
US.quarantine: None for compliant dogs. Foreign-vaccinated high-risk-country dogs without a valid titer: 28 days at a CDC-registered facility. HAWAII (state rule): up to 120 days' quarantine unless the 5-Day-Or-Less program is met: 2 rabies vaccinations (latest at least 30 days before arrival), a passing FAVN with arrival at least 30 days after the test, tick treatment, and documents received at least 10 days before arrival. Hawaii certificates also need a New World screwworm statement.
US.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a dog already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the EU/UK or another low-risk country: CDC Dog Import Form (dog at least 6 months old, microchipped); cats need no federal paperwork. Foreign-vaccinated dogs that were in a CDC high-risk country (e.g. UAE) need a CDC-approved titer at least 28 days before entry plus a facility reservation: plan at least 2 months (microchip, rabies vaccine at 12 weeks or older, titer at least 30 days later, facility reservation at least 30 days before travel). Hawaii direct release: plan 3–4+ months, because FAVN results can take 1–2 months.
US.private_aviation: CDC rules apply equally to private and charter flights; the arrival airport must match the CDC Dog Import Form. Dogs from low-risk countries and US-vaccinated dogs returning from high-risk countries may use any airport, land border or seaport. FOREIGN-VACCINATED dogs that were in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months (list of 15 Apr 2026 includes the UAE, Qatar, Türkiye, Israel, Morocco, Thailand and South Africa; not Saudi Arabia, Mexico, Bahamas, Japan, Singapore or Hong Kong) may enter ONLY through an airport with a CDC-registered animal care facility: ATL, DFW, LAX, MIA, JFK (not Teterboro, Newark or LaGuardia), PHL, SEA, IAD (CDC list updated 1 Sep 2026). Some facilities (SEA, LAX) work cargo-only or prefer cargo. This rules out typical FBO airports such as Teterboro, Van Nuys or Opa-locka for Dubai-vaccinated dogs. Hawaii: HNL direct airport release 8:30 am-4:30 pm daily; neighbor-island arrivals need a permit 30 days ahead; for private aircraft, contact the Animal Quarantine Station before the flight.
US.export: Leaving the US: a USDA-accredited vet issues the destination-specific health certificate, preferably in VEHCS, and APHIS endorses it. Most endorsements are digital, but some destinations still require an original ink signature and embossing; a few (e.g. Bermuda, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras) need no APHIS endorsement. Before taking a dog to a CDC high-risk country, get the USDA-endorsed Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination; otherwise re-entry requires the foreign-vaccinated route.
US.authority: CDC Division of Global Migration Health (dogs); USDA APHIS Veterinary Services; state veterinarians (Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity, Animal Quarantine Station)

UY.microchip: Dogs: mandatory ISO 11784/11785 microchip (MGAP Res. 273/2018), with implantation or reading certificate. Cats: not listed.
vaccinations: Rabies: current, origin-approved vaccine; CVI states date, type, serial, brand; first vaccination at least 21 days before entry.
Under 3 months: age and no exposure to urban rabies in the 90 days before shipment certified.
Animals from WOAH rabies-free countries may enter unvaccinated if certified.
UY.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming within 15 days before CVI issue/passport endorsement (date and product recorded); for dogs the internal product must contain praziquantel.
documents: CVI from origin official authority (Mercosur model, valid 60 days) or official passport validated by the official authority (unvalidated passports refused)
Clinical exam by registered vet within 10 days before CVI issue

Dogs (over 90 days) from countries not WOAH-free of leishmaniasis: negative test (IFAT, ELISA, direct agglutination or molecular) within 60 days before entry; dogs diagnosed/under treatment not admitted
UY.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats travelling with owner. Pets arriving as cargo at Carrasco: notify aeropuertoic@mgap.gub.uy at least 72 working hours before arrival with scanned documents.
UY.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: leishmaniasis test for dogs (within 60 days), deworming within 15 days of the CVI (praziquantel for dogs), vet exam within 10 days of the CVI, official CVI, then the MGAP check at entry. From scratch, plan at least 4–6 weeks.
UY.private_aviation: No prior MGAP authorization for accompanied pets; documents checked at the border point. For Carrasco cargo arrivals, 72 working hours notice to MGAP airport office.
UY.export: Leaving Uruguay: MGAP issues the CVI. Mercosur destinations: digital only via VUCE (since 04/01/2025) through an accredited private vet. Other destinations: accredited vet health certificate within 10 days of travel, dog microchip + INBA registration, pre-filled CVI, payment (UYU 666 per page), at an MGAP Sanidad Animal office by appointment (Montevideo, Carrasco cargo terminal). Mercosur CVI valid 60 days, multiple trips.
UY.authority: MGAP (Ministerio de Ganadería, Agricultura y Pesca) – Dirección General de Servicios Ganaderos

UZ.microchip: Required (microchip number checked on the certificate)
vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (vaccine name, batch and validity recorded)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to Uzbekistan (US: accredited vet + APHIS endorsement; valid 30 days after issuance)
UZ.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: microchip → rabies vaccination (current) → certificate within 30 days of arrival
UZ.authority: Committee for Veterinary and Livestock Development of the Republic of Uzbekistan

VA.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted), as required by the EU country of arrival. Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
VA.rabies_titer: Under the EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
VA.parasite_treatment: None required under EU rules (the EU tapeworm treatment applies only to dogs going to Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway or Northern Ireland).
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.
VA.quarantine: None if EU requirements are met.
VA.timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
VA.private_aviation: No airport in Vatican City. Private jets land in Rome: Fiumicino and Ciampino are both on Italy's September 2026 list of pet points of entry for third-country arrivals.
VA.export: Leaving: the EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport or certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement).
VA.authority: Governorate of Vatican City State; at entry, the Italian Ministry of Health

VC.microchip: ISO microchip implanted before rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated adjuvanted vaccine given at 12 weeks or older, after the microchip.
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, leptospirosis, hepatitis and parainfluenza at least 7 days before export.
Cats: rhinotracheitis, panleukopenia, FeLV, calicivirus and Chlamydophila.
VC.rabies_titer: FAVN at an approved lab (e.g. Kansas State), blood drawn at least 3 weeks after rabies vaccination, result above 0.5 IU/ml. Results must reach the office before the permit is issued; no further waiting period is stated.
VC.parasite_treatment: External and internal (broad-spectrum anthelmintic) treatment within 7 days before export. Dogs: negative heartworm test within 7 days before export.
documents: Import permit (exporter's responsibility).
US veterinary health certificate for SVG, endorsed by APHIS (original ink signature and embossing).
Animal born in or resident in the US for the previous 6 months.
VC.import_permit: Required. Apply to the SVG veterinary authorities; the permit is issued only after FAVN results are received and confirmed.
VC.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN at least 3 weeks later, results to SVG, then the permit; vaccines, heartworm test and parasite treatment within 7 days; APHIS endorsement; 48 hours' notice.
VC.private_aviation: Give 48 hours' notice of arrival (784-456-1111 ext 326, 784-457-2452 or 784-493-1749). Inspection fee EC$55 / US$20 per animal on arrival; landing after 4:00 pm Mon–Fri, on weekends or on public holidays carries separate (overtime) fees.
VC.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, St. Vincent and the Grenadines – Veterinary Services

vaccinations: Rabies: current, valid 1 year from application (under 3 months may enter unvaccinated if age certified) — per SENASA Argentina destination page.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, coronavirus, leptospirosis, parainfluenza (valid 1 year).
Cats: panleukopenia, calicivirus, rhinotracheitis (valid 1 year).
VE.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming within 3 months before entry (per SENASA Argentina destination page).
documents: Official CVI from origin authority (SENASA Argentina states validity 30 calendar days from issue to entry check)
Vet health certificate within 30 days before entry
Vaccination certificates; copy of traveller's ID/passport
VE.import_permit: Confirm with INSAI before travel whether an import permit is needed.
VE.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: confirm INSAI requirements → vaccinations → deworming → health certificate and official CVI → INSAI inspection on arrival.
VE.export: INSAI issues zoosanitary certificates for departure; confirm the procedure with INSAI before travel.
VE.authority: INSAI (Instituto Nacional de Salud Agrícola Integral)

vaccinations: Rabies: at least 2 inactivated vaccines, the first at 3 months of age or older and the next at least 6 months later (1- and 3-year vaccines accepted).
Dogs: parvovirus, distemper, hepatitis/adenovirus, parainfluenza, leptospirosis and Lyme disease.
Cats: calicivirus, panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis and FeLV.
VG.rabies_titer: FAVN at least 1 month after the second or later rabies vaccine, more than 0.5 IU/ml, before departure. Valid 12 months for re-entry.
VG.parasite_treatment: Treated against internal and external parasites (no timing stated).
documents: Health certificate by an accredited vet, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement), with lab results and rabies certificates attached.
BVI import permit (US$10 per animal).
Residence: in the US and/or BVI for at least 6 months before import; area of origin not under rabies quarantine.
VG.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Veterinary Division, Department of Agriculture (Paraquita Bay, Tortola) with the endorsed certificate, rabies certificates and FAVN results. Allow at least 48 hours (2 working days) for processing.
VG.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated. Non-compliant animals may be held in a facility, deported or euthanized.
VG.timeline: Plan at least 7–8 months before travel for an unvaccinated pet (2 rabies doses 6 months apart, then FAVN); otherwise about 6 weeks: FAVN, then health certificate and APHIS endorsement, then the permit, then 24 hours' notice.
VG.private_aviation: Give the Veterinary Division at least 24 hours' notice of the confirmed arrival date, time, aircraft and port of entry. Agricultural officers handle animal clearance at Terrance B. Lettsome Airport (EIS). Keep the pet in its carrier until entry is granted.
VG.authority: BVI Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Division

vaccinations: Rabies: currently vaccinated (or an adequate FAVN titer within 12 months of travel). First-time vaccination must be at least 10 days before arrival; boosters have no wait. 3-year vaccines are accepted if labelled. Animals too young for rabies vaccination are not admitted.
Recommended (not required): leptospirosis vaccine for dogs; flea, tick and heartworm prevention.
VI.rabies_titer: Optional alternative: adequate FAVN titer within 12 months of travel.
documents: Health certificate (APHIS 7001, official state CVI or NASAHO-approved eCVI) with the vet's accreditation number, issued within 10 days of arrival, including rabies date, product and lot. Business-specific certificates are not accepted.
Email the certificate to veterinaryservices@doa.vi.gov at least 1 business day before arrival.
VI.import_permit: Not required from the US or Puerto Rico (interstate). For foreign origins, contact USVI Veterinary Services.
VI.quarantine: Non-compliant animals are confiscated and quarantined for at least 10 days at the owner's expense.
VI.timeline: Plan at least 2 weeks before travel: rabies (10 days if first dose), health certificate within 10 days, email at least 1 business day before arrival.
VI.private_aviation: Arrivals by cruise ship or private boat need a separate inquiry. Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries cannot enter via US territories.
VI.authority: USVI Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Services

VN.microchip: Microchip number required on the USDA Vietnam certificate, and the vet verifies the chip. Vietnamese law sets no separate chip standard; ISO 11784/11785 is advised.
vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (USDA Vietnam certificate, Sept 2025). Vaccine name, batch and validity end date must be listed. No minimum wait is stated on the certificate.
At the border, Vietnamese quarantine officers vaccinate animals not already vaccinated against dangerous infectious diseases (Circular 25/2016, Art. 10).
VN.rabies_titer: Not required (no titer on the USDA Vietnam certificate or in Circular 25/2016).
documents: Health/quarantine certificate issued by the exporting country. For the USA: the Vietnam-specific USDA certificate (Sept 2025 version), signed by an accredited vet and USDA-endorsed (digital endorsement accepted). It covers the microchip check, a clinical exam on the day of issue, origin outside rabies-quarantined areas, and current rabies vaccination. Valid 30 days from issue to departure.
On arrival: import quarantine registration at the border-gate animal quarantine office. The office checks the certificate and examines the pet, then issues a Vietnamese import quarantine certificate.
VN.import_permit: Not needed for up to 2 animals carried by a person for pet/household use, travel or transit: register directly with the border-gate animal quarantine office (Circular 25/2016/TT-BNNPTNT, Art. 10.1). For more than 2 animals, file prior quarantine registration with the Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health (Cục Chăn nuôi và Thú y) via the National Single Window, then declare at the border (Art. 8 and 10.3).
VN.quarantine: No fixed quarantine for compliant pets: clinical inspection at the border only. Animals with a dangerous infectious disease are destroyed near the border gate. An invalid export certificate means the pet is held and dealt with under the regulations (Art. 10.2).
VN.timeline: Allow at least 7 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: accredited-vet exam and Vietnam certificate → USDA (or EU official) endorsement → fly within 30 days of issue. For 3 or more animals, add time for Department registration.
VN.restricted_breeds: The national quarantine rules set no breed ban.
VN.private_aviation: The 2-animal 'carried by a person' route matches owner-accompanied pets on a private jet. Arrange in advance for the airport animal quarantine office (regional Sub-Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health) to inspect at the GA/FBO arrival point.
VN.authority: Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health (Cục Chăn nuôi và Thú y, formerly Department of Animal Health), Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. Border work is done by regional sub-departments / border-gate animal quarantine offices.

documents: Biosecurity Vanuatu import permit
Health certificate attached to the permit (new format since 30 May 2024)
Flight details to the Principal Veterinary Officer at least 1 working day before embarkation
VU.import_permit: Yes. Biosecurity Vanuatu (biosecurity@vanuatu.gov.vu, +678 33580 / 23519). The permit carries the applicable conditions and certificate.
VU.quarantine: On arrival a Veterinary Officer checks documents and inspects or treats the dog. The dog stays in the airport quarantine area until a Permit to Land is issued. Non-compliant dogs may be seized, destroyed or re-exported at the owner's cost.
VU.timeline: Not determinable for US/EU origin without the permit conditions. Origin and transit are restricted to Australia, NZ or New Caledonia routing.
VU.private_aviation: Dogs must travel as manifested air cargo, transiting or offloading only in Australia, NZ or New Caledonia, in line with IATA live animal rules. Yacht arrivals have a separate schedule (4Y).

WF.microchip: Microchip or tattoo matching the import permit (DAVAR certificate).
vaccinations: Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, kennel cough (parainfluenza), leptospirosis. Cats: coryza, panleukopenia. Booster more than 14 days and less than 12 months before export (DAVAR certificate).
WF.parasite_treatment: Two internal treatments (nematodes and cestodes, incl. Echinococcus for dogs) and two external treatments (long-acting, fleas and ticks), at least 15 days apart: the first within 30 days, the second within 3 days of departure.
documents: BIVAP import permit (owner application form, version 06/09/2019)
DAVAR health certificate E.CD.WF.10/17: exam within 3 days of departure, countersigned by an official vet and emailed to BIVAP Wallis (bivap@agripeche.wf) before export
WF.quarantine: Pets from metropolitan France must complete quarantine in New Caledonia before entry. Other origins: not published.
WF.restricted_breeds: Category 1 and 2 dogs (Pit Bull, Mastiff, Tosa, American Staffordshire, Rottweiler and similar) are banned from transport.
WF.private_aviation: Entry goes through New Caledonia (DAVAR certificate, NC quarantine for pets from metropolitan France). A direct private flight with a pet from outside New Caledonia is not supported by the published procedure.
WF.export: New Caledonia lists Wallis and Futuna as a rabies-free Pacific origin with its own dog/cat health certificate, so pets can move from Wallis and Futuna to New Caledonia under DAVAR conditions.
WF.authority: BIVAP – Bureau d'inspection vétérinaire, alimentaire et phytosanitaire (Service territorial des affaires rurales et de la pêche, Wallis and Futuna)

vaccinations: Dogs (Australia-origin permit): current distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, leptospirosis and parvovirus.
WS.parasite_treatment: Dogs (Australia-origin permit): praziquantel within 21 days before transport; roundworm treatment (e.g. pyrantel pamoate) and long-acting topical tick/flea/lice treatment within 4 days before transport.
documents: Samoa import permit
International Animal Sanitary Certificate signed and stamped by a Government Veterinarian within 4 days of departure, recording treatments, doses and dates
WS.import_permit: Yes. Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (maf.info@maf.gov.ws; Biosecurity: biosecurity.info@maf.gov.ws, +685 22561/22562).
WS.quarantine: Quarantine inspection on arrival. The importing country may set further pre- and post-arrival quarantine.
WS.private_aviation: The MAF permit sets the conditions; confirm with MAF before travel whether pets from the USA or EU are eligible.
WS.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (MAF), Samoa Quarantine Service (biosecurity.info@maf.gov.ws)

XK.microchip: Required: electronic identification (ISO 11784 / Annex A ISO 11785). Tattoos were accepted only during the 4-year transitional period after 2009. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must provide a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination per manufacturer's recommendations, certified in a passport/veterinary certificate. IATA Timatic: at least 30 days before departure. Unvaccinated pets under 3 months only under specific conditions (passport, raised with mother, no wild-animal contact).
XK.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/listed countries (Annex II Parts A–C, which include the USA, Canada, UAE, Bahrain, Japan, Russia, Belarus, Australia, etc.). Required from unlisted countries: ≥0.5 IU/ml, sample ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before entry (waived on re-entry if the titer was done before leaving).
XK.parasite_treatment: Echinococcus treatment for dogs and cats (praziquantel or epsiprantel), documented in the certificate/passport. Under AI 02/2009 it applies to animals from unlisted countries, '30 days before the import'. IATA Timatic lists it for all pet entries; treat and document to be safe.
documents: Pet passport or veterinary certificate issued by an authorised veterinarian, certifying identification and valid rabies vaccination (plus titer and echinococcus treatment where applicable)
XK.timeline: EU/listed origin (incl. USA): microchip → rabies vaccination ≥30 days before travel → vet certificate/passport (+ echinococcus treatment, documented). Unlisted origin: add titer ≥30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months.
XK.private_aviation: IATA Timatic gives no airport restriction. Pristina International Airport is the international entry point.
XK.authority: Kosovo Food and Veterinary Agency (AUV/AUVK), Fushë Kosovë/Prishtinë, infoauv@rks-gov.net

YT.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted before 22 April 2026 under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; the primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
Unvaccinated dogs and cats under 3 months cannot enter, except by DAAF derogation.
YT.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Northern Ireland, or the territories and countries listed in Annexes I and II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/636. Annex I: Andorra, Switzerland, Faroe Islands, Gibraltar, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City. Annex II: Ascension Island, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Aruba, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Barbados, Bahrain, Bermuda, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Canada, Chile, Curaçao, Fiji, Falkland Islands, United Kingdom (Great Britain), Guernsey, Hong Kong, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Japan, Jersey, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Cayman Islands, Saint Lucia, Montenegro, Montserrat, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia, Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Serbia, Singapore, Saint Helena, Sint Maarten, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, United States (including American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands), Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, British Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna. From any other country: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after the rabies vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved laboratory, and the sample taken at least 3 months (90 days) before the animal health certificate is issued; a copy of the lab report accompanies the certificate. No retest is needed while the rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to an EU pet re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before it left the EU.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or an Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705). Passports on the Regulation (EU) No 577/2013 model issued before 22 April 2026 remain valid, and passports on the transitional model issued before 1 January 2028 are accepted.

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model in Annex III to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705, under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131), completed by an official veterinarian, or by an authorised veterinarian and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. It is valid for 10 days from issue until the documentary and identity checks on entry, then for onward travel within the EU for 6 months or until the rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old model (Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 577/2013) are accepted only if issued before 1 October 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (model in Annex V, Part 2 to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/705).

Non-commercial means at most 5 dogs, cats or ferrets per movement (more only for competitions, shows or sporting events, with written proof of registration and animals over 6 months old), travelling with the owner or an authorised person, or within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules apply.

Category 2 dogs: prefectoral authorisation (Arrêté préfectoral 2014-6571), DAAF prior-introduction form (Annex 1), identification, valid rabies certificate, sterilisation certificate, liability insurance, owner's aptitude certificate and behavioural assessment

From mainland France or another French overseas department: EU pet passport; from another EU state, New Caledonia, French Polynesia, Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon or Wallis-et-Futuna: EU pet passport with a valid rabies vaccination.
YT.import_permit: Not required for ordinary dogs and cats. A DAAF prior-introduction authorisation form (alimentation.daaf976@agriculture.gouv.fr) is required for category 2 dogs and for exotic pets (NAC).
YT.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
YT.timeline: Allow at least 10 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated (more than 21 days ago) travelling from the USA: EU animal health certificate issued and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From scratch (EU or listed origin), plan at least 4 weeks: microchip → rabies vaccination (pet ≥ 12 weeks) → 21-day wait → EU pet passport or health certificate. From an unlisted country: at least 4 months (titer blood test ≥ 30 days after vaccination, then 3 months from the sample date before the certificate is issued).
YT.restricted_breeds: Category 1 dogs (non-pedigree American Staffordshire terrier/'pit-bull', Mastiff/'boerbull' and Tosa types) may not be introduced, and air transport of them is prohibited. Category 2 dogs (pedigree American Staffordshire terrier and Tosa; Rottweiler and Rottweiler types) are allowed only if sterilised and with prefectoral authorisation under Arrêté 2014-6571.
YT.private_aviation: Pets from outside the EU must be checked at an EU travellers' point of entry. Confirm with DAAF Mayotte and customs before routing that Dzaoudzi-Pamandzi can carry out the check for a private flight. Category 1 dogs cannot be carried by air.
YT.authority: DAAF de Mayotte (Service Alimentation), French Ministry of Agriculture; alimentation.daaf976@agriculture.gouv.fr

ZA.microchip: Mandatory for all dogs and cats; must be readable by ISO 11784/11785 scanners (tattoos not accepted). The microchip number must appear on all lab reports.
vaccinations: Rabies (US-origin, per APHIS guidance Sept 2024): vaccinated within 12 months before export, and more than 30 days before export for a primary vaccination. The 30-day wait does not apply if the booster was given before the previous vaccination expired.
Other origins: as stated on the import permit / South African model health certificate.
ZA.rabies_titer: Not on the US-origin dog certificate (APHIS guidance). Requirements for other origins are set on the permit; confirm with the Permit Office.
ZA.parasite_treatment: Dogs (US-origin certificate): heartworm (D. immitis) preventive given at least once after the negative heartworm test and before certificate issue. Effective acaricide plus insect repellent within 30 days before departure, recorded on the certificate.
documents: Original South African veterinary import permit (DoA, VetPermits@daff.gov.za)

Original veterinary health certificate on the South African model (dogs: IMP. DOG. GEN 05/22 CG), issued and endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority within 10 days of travel (US: USDA APHIS ink-signed and embossed)
Rabies vaccination certificate (original or copy)

Dogs: English lab reports, all within 30 days of import and all negative: Brucella canis, Trypanosoma evansi (CATT plus Giemsa smear at a WOAH reference laboratory), Babesia gibsoni (two tests), Dirofilaria immitis (microfilarial filtration only), Leishmania
Indemnity declaration where specified (e.g. dogs entering quarantine)
ZA.import_permit: Required for ALL dogs and cats. Apply at least 4 weeks before arrival (separate forms: domestic cats; dogs not subject to quarantine; dogs subject to quarantine). Proof of payment is required. Issued 3-5 working days after approval. Valid for a limited period (stated on the permit) and for one consignment only. Fees are set in the annual tariff list (2026/27 list published by DoA).
ZA.quarantine: Cats are generally not quarantined. Dogs from some origins are subject to quarantine at state stations (Kempton Park/Johannesburg or Cape Town), which must be booked in advance using the 'subject to quarantine' application. APHIS lists no quarantine for US-origin dogs. Non-compliant dogs face a high risk of return or euthanasia: DoA has told APHIS they will no longer be placed in quarantine.
ZA.timeline: Allow at least 45 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated travelling from the USA: import permit at least 4 weeks ahead, dog blood tests within 30 days of arrival (surra samples sent to Belgium or Japan), parasite treatments, then the certificate and APHIS endorsement within 10 days of travel, and notice to the port of entry. Cats need less time.
ZA.private_aviation: DoA information document (06-2022): dogs and cats must be registered as manifested cargo, not excess baggage. No state veterinarians at passenger terminals, so pets clear only via the cargo terminal at O.R. Tambo, Cape Town or King Shaka (Durban, depending on the permit). On a private jet, the pet must be on the cargo manifest/air waybill, the aircraft should land at the airport named on the permit, and inspection must be arranged with the port's state vet/cargo handler. Do not plan an arrival at Lanseria or other private/regional airports unless DoA confirms it in writing on the permit.
ZA.export: Exports follow the destination country's rules. South African state veterinarians endorse export health certificates. Movement to Namibia uses an inter-territorial movement permit from a local state vet.
ZA.authority: Department of Agriculture (formerly DALRRD/DAFF), Directorate Animal Health – Import Export Policy Unit / Food Import & Export Standards (VetPermits@daff.gov.za)

ZM.microchip: Not required on the UK model certificate (identification marks are used).
vaccinations: Rabies: no more than 12 months before export (UK EHC 3928). If not vaccinated before export, the pet must be presented to the nearest Government Veterinary Station in Zambia for vaccination on arrival.
ZM.parasite_treatment: Exam within 48 hours before export must find the pet free of external parasites including ticks (UK EHC 3928).
documents: Zambian veterinary import permit (accompanies the animal)
Official health certificate meeting the permit conditions (UK model: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Owner declaration of 6 months' residence in the exporting country or since birth (UK)
ZM.import_permit: Required. Issued by the Department of Veterinary Services HQ, Mulungushi House, P.O. Box 50060, Lusaka (UK guidance uses the older name 'Department of Veterinary and Tsetse Control Services'). Must be attached to the consignment and travel with the animal. Conditions vary by species, origin and purpose. A contact person in Lusaka can apply.
ZM.timeline: Allow at least 28 days for a pet already microchipped and rabies-vaccinated: apply for the import permit (processing time is not published) → send it to your vet and the origin veterinary authority → vet exam within 48 hours of export and government endorsement → notify the nearest Zambian Veterinary Officer of the arrival.
ZM.private_aviation: The importer must inform the nearest Veterinary Officer of the arrival so the animal can be inspected.
ZM.authority: Department of Veterinary Services, Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock (the embassy page uses an older department name)

ZW.microchip: Not required on the UK model certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: not mandatory before export per UK guidance. If given, within 12 months before export. All dogs in Zimbabwe must be rabies-vaccinated; unvaccinated dogs must be vaccinated by a Government Veterinary Officer after arrival. Pre-travel vaccination is recommended.
Other vaccinations: the UK OV must be satisfied that 'necessary vaccinations' were done.
ZW.parasite_treatment: Exam within 48 hours before export must find the pet free of external parasites (UK EHC 3929).
documents: Zimbabwe import permit (permit number entered on the certificate)
Official health certificate (UK model: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination certificate (if vaccinated)
Owner declaration: not imported into the exporting country in the past 6 months (UK)
ZW.import_permit: Required (UK NFG 3929). Director of Veterinary Services, P.O. Box CY 66, Causeway, Harare (tel +263 4 791 355 per UK guidance).
ZW.timeline: Before travel: apply for the import permit (allow for processing; no official time is published) → vet exam within 48 hours of export and government endorsement → travel.
ZW.authority: Department of Veterinary Services (Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development), Harare
